signals.title: Fix data race on DataTypeAggregateFunction version during Native serialization
signals.text: Related: found by the `arm_tsan` and `azure, amd_tsan` Stress tests (STID 3977-4818, ThreadSanitizer data race). No existing issue. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/94859 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112052 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Not for changelog. ### Description A single `DataTypeAggregateFunction` instance is shared across query result blocks: it lives once in the table's column description and is aliased by shallow column copies. `NativeWriter`/`NativeReader` called `setVersionToAggregateFunctions`, which walked to the leaf type and wrote its `mutable version` field in place. Two concurrent `Native` serializations of the same aggregate-function-typed column then raced on that field, and the version written for one old connection stayed on the shared type, so every later query read the states at that version - for `sumMap` over `Decimal32` that returns wrong values. Reports: * https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109496&sha=62eeb400eafe86cedff9b5a4e9a36aa722633cda&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_tsan%29 * https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=b59441bd06c2fcb6b103a30874528cc398afc723&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28azure%2C%20amd_tsan%29 **That fix has since landed on `master`** through #94859 and #112052: `setVersionToAggregateFunctions` now replaces every versioned nested type instead of mutating it, and `replaceNestedSimpleTypes` carries the custom names (`Nested`, `SimpleAggregateFunction`) over the rebuild. This branch is therefore resolved in favour of that implementation, and what it added on top of it - an `IDataType::transformChildren` override per container type, and the `unique_ptr` to `shared_ptr` switch of `DataTypeCustomNamePtr` - is dropped as duplicate machinery. What remains here is what `master` does not have, and it keeps this PR's intent - the race cannot come back, because the version can no longer be assigned in place at all: * `DataTypeAggregateFunction::setVersion` and `updateVersionFromRevision` are removed, and `version` is no longer `mutable`. Both mutators were left without callers by the rewrite on `master`; the version is now set only at construction (parsed from AST, decoded from the binary type encoding, or chosen by `setVersionToAggregateFunctions`, which builds a new type). * Unit and functional coverage of the behaviour, which `master` has only indirectly. ### Testing * `gtest_aggregate_function_version_race` (14 tests) pins the type-level behaviour: the shared type object is not mutated; a wrapper is rebuilt only when a leaf was actually replaced; the `Point`, `Nested` and `SimpleAggregateFunction` custom names survive, including a `Tuple`-backed `SimpleAggregateFunction`; a `Variant` keeps its discriminator order and throws when two alternatives would collapse; a `JSON` typed path keeps the version spelled in its own type name; and an 8-thread x 2000-iteration stress over one shared type object is race-free. * `04612_aggregate_function_version_custom_type_names` round-trips `Nested`, `SimpleAggregateFunction` and a wrapper-named type through `Native` (which assigns the version in the writer and again in the reader) and through `DETACH`/`ATTACH`, and checks that a deeply nested `Nested` stays linear in the nesting depth. * `04613_aggregate_function_version_not_sticky` asks for a `Native` response at a revision below the one that introduced versioning and then checks the column again, so a version pinned for that one response would be visible both in the values read back (`sumMap` over `Decimal32`) and in `system.columns`. The revision is pinned explicitly and the type name the response carries is asserted, so the test cannot pass without that path having run.

signals.title: Fix ReadBuffer-canceled abort in GraceHashJoin spilled-block reader
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you do not need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `LOGICAL_ERROR: ReadBuffer is canceled. Can't read from it.` that could occur in a `grace_hash` join when reading spilled blocks failed mid-read while multiple threads shared the reader. ### Description `GraceHashJoin` shares one `AccumulatedBlockReader` between concurrent `DelayedJoinedBlocksWorkerTransform` threads. If `reader->read` throws while reading a spilled block, `ReadBuffer::next` cancels the underlying buffer and rethrows. Previously the shared reader was not marked finished, so a sibling worker could re-enter `read` on the canceled buffer and throw `LOGICAL_ERROR: ReadBuffer is canceled. Can't read from it.` The query should instead preserve and report the original read exception. The fix marks `AccumulatedBlockReader` finished on every read exception while holding its existing mutex. Subsequent workers return an empty block and cannot re-read the canceled buffer. This covers both the left delayed reader and the right reader that use the same `read` implementation. The new stateless regression deterministically forces a failure only in the shared left delayed reader: it cancels the underlying buffer, throws `FAULT_INJECTED`, verifies the query reports that original exception, and then verifies that the server remains alive. Without the `eof` assignment, a sibling worker re-enters the canceled buffer and triggers the original logical exception. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111056&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/111056](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F111056+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix optimize_distributed_group_by_sharding_key wrong result for JOIN
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111087 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111274 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111087 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111274 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a wrong result with `optimize_distributed_group_by_sharding_key` when grouping a distributed `JOIN` by a column from the other join side that shares the sharding key's name (e.g. `GROUP BY r.k` over a `LEFT JOIN` where `r.k` is not the distributed table's sharding key). Such groups can span shards, so the per-shard aggregation shortcut is no longer applied for them, avoiding duplicate group keys with split aggregate values. ### Description `optimize_distributed_group_by_sharding_key` lets `StorageDistributed` skip the cross-shard merge when the `GROUP BY` key equals the sharding key, assuming each group's rows live on a single shard. In the new analyzer, `isShardingKeySuitsQueryTreeNodeExpression` matched the grouping expression against the sharding key by column name only (table qualifiers are stripped when building the comparison DAG). So a right-side column `r.k` in a distributed `LEFT JOIN` that merely shares the left table's sharding-key name `k` wrongly triggered the shortcut. Unmatched left rows are padded with `r.k = 0` on every shard, so the `r.k = 0` group spans shards and per-shard partial aggregates were returned unmerged, producing duplicate group keys with split values (silent wrong result). The fix skips the shortcut when the grouping/DISTINCT/LIMIT BY expression references any column that is not from the distributed table's own table expression, reusing the existing `hasUnknownColumn` helper. `GROUP BY` over the distributed table's actual sharding key is unaffected. Only the new analyzer path was affected; the old analyzer compares qualified identifier names and was already correct. Issue #111274 (`optimize_skip_unused_shards = 1` duplicating every group of a distributed self-join on an expression sharding key `intHash64(k)`) is the same root cause and is fixed by the same guard: `GROUP BY negate(r.k)` over a global self-join references `r.k` from the broadcast side, whose required column matches the sharding key name after qualifier stripping. Verified locally on master: the self-join returned 1000 rows (500 groups duplicated, each with an empty aggregate copy) and returns the correct 500 with this fix.

signals.title: Add `max_rows` setting for databases
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109355 Adds a `max_rows` setting for `Atomic` and `Ordinary` databases: a ceiling on active MergeTree rows counted toward the database limit. It is enforced on `INSERT`, `ATTACH`, and partition-import/move operations. A batch `INSERT` may overshoot, and the next `INSERT` throws `TOO_MANY_ROWS`. The counted total is exposed through the nullable `system.databases.rows` column. It intentionally excludes engines that do not participate in `max_rows` accounting. The setting can be changed at runtime with `ALTER DATABASE ... MODIFY SETTING max_rows = N`; its default value, `0`, is unlimited. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add the `max_rows` setting for `Atomic` and `Ordinary` databases, limiting active MergeTree rows counted across a database. It is enforced on `INSERT`, `ATTACH`, and partition imports, is reconfigurable via `ALTER DATABASE ... MODIFY SETTING`, and is exposed through `system.databases.rows`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111166&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/111166](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F111166+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fsync backup files and directories when writing a backup to local disk
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111320 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `BACKUP ... TO File(...)` / `Disk(...)` now fsyncs the backup data files, the `.backup` manifest and the containing directories before reporting `BACKUP_CREATED`, so an acknowledged backup to local storage survives power loss. The guarantee covers `backups.allowed_path` and everything the backup writes below it. Controlled by the new backup setting `fsync_backup_files` (default `true`). Object-storage destinations (`S3`/`Azure`) are unaffected. ### Description Fixes #111320. `BACKUP ... TO File()/Disk()` returned `BACKUP_CREATED` without issuing any `fsync`/`fdatasync` at the destination: not the data files, not the `.backup` manifest, not the directories (there was no `fsync` anywhere in `src/Backups/`). On power loss after the acknowledgement the backup could be lost entirely or left torn, even though `BACKUP_CREATED` is what an operator relies on before dropping the source data. Only local `File()`/`Disk()` were affected; object-storage destinations were already durable. Report URL: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111320 (reproduced 3/3 with a `dm-flakey` power-loss simulation). Fix, gated on the new backup setting `fsync_backup_files` (default `true`), following the durability audit family (#68958 -> #111346, #111269 -> #111335): - Two writer hooks with a no-op default on `IBackupWriter`, overridden only by the local `File`/`Disk` writers (`S3`/`Azure`/`Memory`/`Null` inherit the no-op): `syncFileToDisk(file_name)`, called right after each data file is written in `BackupImpl::writeFile` (each call fsyncs its own file, so the concurrent write path is safe), and `syncDirectoriesToDisk()`, which fdatasyncs every directory the backup created, deepest-first. - In `BackupImpl::finalizeWriting` the `.backup` manifest (or, for archives, the archive file) is synced last, after all data files, so a persisted manifest never precedes its payload. Directory syncing runs for every writer, including the internal writers of `BACKUP ON CLUSTER` which write their own data files. Regression test `tests/queries/0_stateless/04412_backup_to_file_fsync.sh` asserts the `FileSync`/`DirectorySync` ProfileEvents of the `BACKUP` query, present with `fsync_backup_files=1` and absent with `0`; integration coverage adds the `Disk`, archive and `ON CLUSTER` internal-writer cases. Guarantee boundary, stated rather than left implicit: `backups.allowed_path` and everything written below it are synced in a loop that propagates failures. Ancestors above it are best-effort, because `fsyncBackupDirectory` needs `O_DIRECTORY` (read permission) while writing a backup only needs them searchable: measured with the area inside a `0311` directory, writing succeeds and `open(O_DIRECTORY)` on the ancestor fails `EACCES`, so throwing there would newly fail backups that work today. So if a directory above `backups.allowed_path` was itself created without being made durable, a power loss can still take the whole tree. The setting's docs row now says this. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111394&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/111394](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F111394+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR in normal projection optimization with correlated subqueries
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103695 (same `Invalid number of columns in chunk pushed to OutputPort` error family) ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `LOGICAL_ERROR` raised when a normal projection was used to read the input of a correlated subquery (decorrelated into a join) and all parts were served from the projection. Depending on the settings it was reported as `Invalid number of columns in chunk pushed to OutputPort` or as `Block structure mismatch in joined block stream`. It is an exception in release builds and aborts the server in debug and sanitizer builds. ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer, reproduces on current master and is unrelated to the pull requests it was seen on: [amd_msan](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=100332&sha=766a499fbbfcfb5b1cbd865a4f435f75c7b5ee28&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_msan%29) (STID 2270-3452), [amd_tsan](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=92472&sha=0d58afae81ce01111323d3f73a59d6d032d199f7&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_tsan%29) (STID 0993-3a3c), and `Stress test (arm_debug)`. Root cause: `optimizeUseNormalProjections` reads the projection over `required_columns = reading->getAllColumnNames()`. Columns of that set which the rebuilt `query.dag` does not consume survive as pass-throughs, because `ActionsDAG::updateHeader` appends every un-consumed input, and widen the rewritten read's output header. The all-parts-from-projection branch spliced that widened node in without the `blocksHaveEqualStructure` check the Union branch already had, so a downstream step got more columns than its declared header. The default `query_plan_remove_unused_columns = 1` re-narrows the stream and masks both asserts, so CI hits this only under `compatibility = '25.3'`. Change: emit the replaced header's columns by name, dropping the surplus pass-throughs so the projection stays usable, and hoist the equal-structure check to cover both replacement branches. It stays below the narrowing as a fail-closed net for what narrowing cannot repair (a missing column, or a type difference), skipping the projection and keeping the regular read. Since `filterPartsByProjection` mutates the parent analysis result in place, it now runs only after that check passes, so a skipped projection no longer drops parts; `has_parent_parts` moves ahead of it and is computed non-destructively. Validation: both carriers abort before the change and run clean after, returning the projection-off results; reverting only this change makes them abort again. Regression tests are in `04410_normal_projection_correlated_subquery_part_offset`, whose `EXPLAIN` assertions pin that every read is served by the projection and none declined. The failing-test set across the projection, prewhere, part_offset and correlated suites is unchanged. <details><summary>Both carriers: error signatures</summary> Carrier 1, virtual columns (`_part_offset` in the projection), output port assert: ``` Invalid number of columns in chunk pushed to OutputPort. Expected 2, found 4 src/Processors/Port.h:425 src/Processors/Transforms/JoiningTransform.cpp:101 DB::JoiningTransform::prepare() ``` Carrier 2, real columns. The inner decorrelation join's right side carries exactly one column by design, so the leaked columns trip its structure check instead of the output port one: ``` Block structure mismatch in joined block stream: different number of columns: __table3.timestamp UInt64 UInt64(size = 0) __table3.timestamp UInt64 UInt64(size = 2), payload String String(size = 2), id UUID Sparse(size = 2, UUID(size = 1), UInt64(size = 0)) src/Core/Block.cpp:863 DB::assertBlocksHaveEqualStructureAllowReplicated src/Interpreters/ConstantJoin.cpp:230 DB::ConstantJoin::addBlockToJoin src/Processors/Transforms/JoiningTransform.cpp:373 DB::FillingRightJoinSideTransform::work() ``` `correlated_subqueries_use_in_memory_buffer = 0` selects the `ConstantJoin` assert; adding `correlated_subqueries_default_join_kind = 'left'` selects the output port one. Runnable reproducers for both are the statements in the new test file. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111401&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/111401](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F111401+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Refactor columns deserialization to avoid all assumeMutable calls, simplify the substreams cache, and remove rows_offset
signals.text: PR #109105 replaced `assumeMutable` with `IColumn::mutate` in the some pars of the deserialization code. When a column is shared via the substreams cache, `IColumn::mutate` clones the whole accumulated column, giving O(rows × granules) cost and a 3–4× deserialization slowdown. Rework the deserialize path so it never clones: - `deserializeBinaryBulkWithMultipleStreams` and its helpers take `IColumn &` instead of `ColumnPtr &`. - The substreams cache never shares a `ColumnPtr`; consumers copy the current range out via `insertRangeFrom`. - `assumeMutable`/`IColumn::mutate`/`const_cast` are removed from the deserialize paths; mutable children come from non-const accessors. - Cache-shared members are dropped from the `Deserialize*State` structs. - The MergeTree reader stack reads into `MutableColumns`. Additionally, remove `rows_offset` from the deserialization API. `rows_offset` (the number of leading rows to skip while deserializing a range) is provably always `0` for every caller, so it is dropped from `deserializeBinaryBulkWithMultipleStreams`, `deserializeBinaryBulk` and all their helpers. This deletes the read-side skip machinery: - the skip loops / `istr.ignore(size * rows_offset)` seeks; - the `Map` bucketed reorder-with-skipped-rows path (which also removes a latent substreams-cache over-count on bucketed `Map`); - the `Object` shared-data `granules_offsets` / `last_incomplete_granule_offset` cursors (the load-bearing `StructureGranule` continuous-read state is kept); - the `SerializationArrayOffsets` helper (`rows_offset`-only); - assorted dead offset arithmetic. <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Refactor columns deserialization to avoid all assumeMutable calls, simplify the substreams cache, and remove the always-zero rows_offset parameter.

signals.title: Fix logical error !raw_type->isNullable() in AND-compare chain optimization
signals.text: Keep NULL-constant and nullable-result comparisons out of AND-compare pruning <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111292 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111292 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer: `AST fuzzer (amd_debug, targeted)` [CI report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111535&sha=5d41a4d4d9fe7efc9a932917ac11ac20f376ea85&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29) and `Stress test (amd_asan_ubsan)`, `Logical error: '!rhs_literal->getValue().isNull()'` (STID 2508-5318 / 2508-5717). The assertion aborts in debug/sanitizer builds; in release builds the `chassert` is a no-op, so this is a CI/sanitizer fix. This extends the original fix to two more paths in the same `Nothing`-collapsed AND, reached by fuzzing the added test: 1. A comparison whose constant side is itself NULL-valued (e.g. `expr = NULL`) hit `chassert(!literal->getValue().isNull())` in the classification loop of `tryOptimizeAndCompareNotEqualsChain`. A NULL-valued constant has no comparable value, so it is no longer treated as the constant side and the operand is kept as-is, mirroring the sibling `tryOptimizeOrEqualsChain`. 2. The `addComparisonFilter` pruning guard tested only the raw operand type via `isNullable()`, which is false for `LowCardinality(Nullable(T))` (nested nullability) and for the NULL-capable carriers `Dynamic` / `Variant`, whose comparison result is still `Nullable(UInt8)`. Those slipped past the guard and folded a contradictory chain, changing the handled exception from `ILLEGAL_COLUMN` to `TYPE_MISMATCH` depending on `optimize_redundant_comparisons`. The guard now tests the comparison node's own result type, which is the robust signal and covers all of `Nullable` / `LowCardinality(Nullable)` / `Dynamic` / `Variant`; both entry functions share `addComparisonFilter`. Verified the error is identical across `optimize_redundant_comparisons` / `optimize_and_compare_chain` for the whole wrapper matrix, non-nullable `Int32` / `LowCardinality(Int32)` are unchanged, and plain-column pruning still fires.

signals.title: Text index: introduce new storage layout for positions for the phrase search support
signals.text: Previous implementation of the phrase search was based on the Roaringish (#101473) positional information which has many benefits such as embedding doc ids directly in the positional data, vectorized (SIMD) phrase search, and single I/O seek per token. However, those benefits come with their trade-offs: 1. embedding doc ids in the positional data: doc ids are duplicated between posting list and positional data - so the index size is grown significantly. 2. vectorized phrase search: it is fastest on AVX-512 and relies on x86 vector instructions throughout, which ARM machines do not have. 3. single I/O seek per token: whole positions is read no matter how few documents survive the posting-list intersection, so selective phrases pay the most.. These trade-offs led us to redesign the layout of the positional data. The new layout stores each token's positions as blocks of 128 posting ranks behind a small directory (document count, block count, and every block's byte size). The rank addresses the document, so no doc id is stored in the positional data, frequencies default to a single occurrence and only exceptions are recorded, as (rank, frequency) pairs. Within a document the first position is absolute and the rest are deltas, PFor-compressed. A phrase query intersects the posting lists first, maps the surviving documents to their ranks, and reads only the blocks those ranks fall into — which is what turns the trade-offs above around. This PR also includes new `PforDelta` compression. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Rework the on-disk layout of text index positions (experimental phrase search): positions are now stored in PFor-packed blocks addressed by posting rank, and phrase search reads only the blocks covering candidate rows, greatly reducing position-data reads and memory usage. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111550&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/111550](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F111550+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Preserve unchanged TOAST values in MaterializedPostgreSQL
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/83517 Preserve PostgreSQL columns encoded as unchanged TOAST references in `MaterializedPostgreSQL` replication instead of replacing them with default values. The consumer resolves the previous value from an earlier row in the same replication buffer when possible. Otherwise, it reads the current row from the nested `ReplacingMergeTree` by replica identity, batching key lookups to avoid a query per value. The old replica identity tuple is used when an update changes the key. An unchanged TOAST value in a replica identity column is rejected because the replication message does not contain a value that could identify the row. The integration test covers a regular update, multiple updates of the same row in one PostgreSQL transaction, and a replica identity change. The user-facing documentation is updated for both `MaterializedPostgreSQL` engines. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `MaterializedPostgreSQL` now preserves unchanged PostgreSQL `TOAST` values during updates instead of replacing them with default values. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111552&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/111552](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F111552+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix CI crash reporter naming logical errors after query-echoed text
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108735 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Related: #108735 The functional/stress crash reporter (`FuzzerLogParser` in `ci/jobs/scripts/log_parser.py`, invoked by `ClickHouseProc.check_fatal_messages_in_logs`) names a failure by running `rg -o 'Logical error.*'` over the whole `clickhouse-server.log` and taking the first match. `executeQuery` logs the full query text (SQL comments included) into the server log, and the signal handler embeds the crashing query inside a `<Fatal>` record. So when a job hits a real logical-error crash, the reporter can pick up a *different* test's comment that merely quotes `Logical error '...'` and use it as the failure name, while the STID and stack come from the actual crash. This mislabels unrelated crashes and pollutes failure tracking. Concrete example (MasterCI, `Stateless tests (amd_llvm_coverage, ParallelReplicas, s3 storage, parallel)`): the real crash was `<Fatal> : Logical error: 'Got read request from replica 1 for unknown stream ...'` (`ParallelReplicasReadingCoordinator`), but the reporter named it after a regression test's `!part.empty()` / `Bad cast ...` comment. This wrongly reopened an unrelated tracking task. Fix, in `log_parser.py`: - Match `Logical error` only as the message of a real formatted log record, anchored to the line prefix `^<date> <time> [ tid ] {query_id} <Fatal> [logger]: Logical error: ...`. A query echo, a comment continuation line, and query text embedded mid-line on a `<Fatal>` signal record all fail that anchor. The anchor also requires the `<Fatal>` level and the `Logical error:` colon, so a benign `<Warning> ...: Logical error. Not all polled messages ...` is not selected. Genuine logical errors are always emitted via `LOG_FATAL` (`abortOnFailedAssertion`), so nothing real is missed. The other patterns (sanitizer, assertion, segfault, signal, memory) are byte-for-byte unchanged. - `get_failed_query()` reuses the query id of the selected fatal record instead of re-grepping the log from the top, so the reported failing query matches the crash. An explicitly empty id (background exception with no query) reports no query rather than an unrelated one; the inline `Inconsistent AST formatting` query (which aborts before an `executeQuery` record is logged) is still extracted, scoped to the selected record; and the query id is matched inside its `{...}` delimiters and escaped, so `q2` no longer also matches `{q20}` and a metacharacter id is literal. Added regression tests in `ci/tests/test_log_parser.py`; existing tests unchanged.

signals.title: Reject truncated/incomplete AI text function responses
signals.text: The AI text functions (`aiGenerate`, `aiClassify`, `aiExtract`, `aiTranslate`) could silently return a truncated answer. When a provider stops early — most commonly by hitting the `max_tokens` limit — it reports this in the response, but the shared base class `FunctionBaseAI` never inspected the signal and returned whatever partial text came back. For example, `aiGenerate('Write three sentences about the ocean.', map(..., 'max_tokens', '5'))` returned the fragment `The ocean covers more than` with no error. This change normalizes each provider's native stop reason (OpenAI `finish_reason`, Anthropic `stop_reason`) into a canonical `FinishReason` enum, so the base class can make a single completeness decision without knowing the provider dialect: - `Truncated` (token/context limit) → throws `AI_PROVIDER_RESPONSE_TRUNCATED`. - `ContentFilter` (OpenAI `content_filter`, Anthropic `refusal`) and `ToolCall` → throws `AI_PROVIDER_RESPONSE_INCOMPLETE`. - `Complete` (natural end, or a caller stop sequence such as Anthropic `stop_sequence`) and `Unknown` (unrecognized reason) are accepted, so benign non-`stop` reasons are not misclassified as truncation. The rejection is thrown inside the existing per-row `try`, so it is non-retriable (retrying would hit the same limit) and honors `ai_function_throw_on_error`: with `1` the exception propagates; with `0` the row becomes the column default. `aiEmbed` is unaffected (embeddings have no finish reason). Integration tests in `test_ai_functions` cover truncation (throw + graceful), content-filter, an accepted unknown reason, and the Anthropic `stop_sequence` (must not throw) and `max_tokens` (must throw) cases. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): AI text functions (`aiGenerate`, `aiClassify`, `aiExtract`, `aiTranslate`) now reject truncated or otherwise incomplete provider responses (e.g. when the model hits the `max_tokens` limit) instead of silently returning partial output. Behavior follows the `ai_function_throw_on_error` setting. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111830&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/111830](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F111830+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Implement PromQL functions clamp(), clamp_min(), clamp_max() and round()
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/57545 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): PromQL: implemented functions `clamp`, `clamp_min`, `clamp_max`, and `round`. ### Description Implements four PromQL functions previously reported as not implemented: - `clamp(v, min, max)`, `clamp_min(v, min)`, `clamp_max(v, max)` — new `applyClampFunction` converter mapping to `greatest`/`least` SQL with explicit guards, because vectorized `least`/`greatest` in ClickHouse treat NaN as the largest value and ignore NULLs, which would corrupt NaN sample values and missing points. Prometheus special cases are reproduced exactly: `min > max` returns an empty vector, and a NaN bound propagates NaN. - `round(v[, to_nearest])` — new `applyRoundFunction` converter; replicates Prometheus inverse arithmetic (`floor(v * (1/to_nearest) + 0.5) / (1/to_nearest)`), including ties rounding toward `+Inf` and NaN propagation for `to_nearest = 0` or NaN. Both drop the metric name from results, matching Prometheus. Non-constant scalar bounds (for example, `clamp(v, time()*0-1, 2)`) are supported. No parser changes were needed; arity is enforced by each converter. The embedded support matrices for `prometheusQuery` and `prometheusQueryRange` list the new math functions and retain the implemented range functions `increase`, `changes`, and `resets`. **Semantics verified against Prometheus 3.5.0** for bound combinations `(0, 1)`, `(0, 1e12)`, `(1e12, 0)`, `(1e12, 1e12)`, and fractional `to_nearest`. **Testing**: adds `test_clamp` and `test_round`, plus conversion and aggregation regressions for empty scalar handling and a runtime scalar `quantile` parameter outside `[0, 1]`. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1566` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Add exclude_data_from_backup MergeTree setting
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111827 ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added exclude_from_backup and exclude_data_from_backup MergeTree table settings so BACKUP can skip a table entirely or skip only its data while still restoring its DDL. ### Description Implements #111827: a table-level setting so that `BACKUP` can skip a table's data while still including its DDL, so the table is restorable (empty) later. Useful for tables whose data can be regenerated from a source table (e.g. materialized-view targets), to reduce backup size. - New `Bool` MergeTree setting `exclude_data_from_backup` (default `false`). - Hooked into `BackupEntriesCollector::shouldBackupTableData()`: when the setting is enabled on a `MergeTreeData`-derived table, data collection is skipped for that table; DDL collection is unaffected (existing code path already handles DDL/data independently). - Added `tests/integration/test_exclude_data_from_backup/test.py` covering both the default (`false`, data backed up) and enabled (`true`, data skipped) cases; both pass. **Not yet tested** (feedback welcome): behavior on `ReplicatedMergeTree` specifically, and `BACKUP DATABASE`/`BACKUP ... ALL TABLES` paths (the hook is in the shared per-table code path used by all backup forms, so it should behave the same, but I haven't added explicit coverage for these yet). The setting name/interface is intentionally not MergeTree-specific in wording, per @alexey-milovidov's suggestion on the issue, so it could be adopted by other engines later.
signals.author: adityaksolves

signals.title: Support the NetCDF format
signals.text: Adds support for the [NetCDF](https://www.unidata.ucar.edu/software/netcdf/) format, a self-describing binary format for multidimensional arrays that is the standard way climate, weather, oceanographic and other scientific data is distributed. There is a lot of public data in it (ERA5, CMIP, NOAA, Copernicus), and until now the only way to query it with ClickHouse was to convert it first. Reading is supported for the three "classic" versions of the format: CDF-1, CDF-2 (64-bit offset) and CDF-5 (64-bit data), and writing produces CDF-2 or CDF-5, whichever the data needs. The files are parsed directly, so there is no new dependency. A NetCDF-4 file, which is an HDF5 file with a different data model on top, is recognized and reported with a message that says how to convert it. **Data model.** Every variable of a file becomes a column, and the rows enumerate the Cartesian product of all the dimensions that the variables use; a variable that does not use some of them is repeated along them. The `to_dataframe` method of `xarray` produces a table with the same columns and the same set of rows, though possibly in a different order: `to_dataframe` puts the dimensions in alphabetical order by default, while ClickHouse keeps the order of the dimensions of the variables. So a file with the dimensions `time`, `lat`, `lon` and the variables `time(time)`, `lat(lat)`, `lon(lon)`, `temperature(time, lat, lon)` reads as a table with four columns and `time * lat * lon` rows. The classic format has no string type, so a `char` variable is read as a String whose length is the last dimension of the variable, when that dimension serves only as the length of the strings; a dimension that anything else in the file uses as a real axis stays in the row space, and such a `char` variable is read as one character per row. Only the variables that a query needs are read, the number of rows comes from the header (so `count()` does not read any data), and an input that cannot be seeked is read into memory instead. **Writing.** Every column becomes a variable over a single dimension named `row`, so a file written by ClickHouse is read back with the same column names and the same rows; the types come back as the closest types of the classic format (a `FixedString` as a `String`, an `Enum` or a `LowCardinality` column as the type it wraps, dates and times as plain numbers, a `Nullable` column as its base type unless read with `input_format_netcdf_fill_value_as_null`). The version of the format is chosen automatically: CDF-5 when a column needs a type that only CDF-5 has or takes more than 4 GiB, CDF-2 otherwise. A `Nullable` column is written with the `_FillValue` attribute, and a column with dates or times gets the `units` attribute of the CF conventions, so `xarray` decodes it back into timestamps. **Settings.** `input_format_netcdf_fill_value_as_null` reads the values equal to the `_FillValue` (or `missing_value`) attribute of a variable as NULL, which is how the CF conventions mark missing data such as sea surface temperature over land. `input_format_netcdf_add_dimension_columns` adds a column with the index along every dimension that has no coordinate variable of the same name, for the files that have none. **Testing.** The test files in `tests/queries/0_stateless/data_netcdf` were written by the netCDF C library, not by this code. Beyond the two functional tests, during development the reader was compared value by value against an independent reference implementation for all three format versions, the output was checked by opening it with the netCDF C library for every supported type family, and 321 truncated and bit-flipped files were fed to the reader — all of them either parsed or failed with a clean error, with no crashes. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Support the `NetCDF` format for both reading and writing. It is a self-describing binary format for multidimensional arrays, widely used for climate, weather and other scientific data. Reading supports all three classic versions of the format (CDF-1, CDF-2 and CDF-5), and writing produces CDF-2 or CDF-5, whichever the data needs. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)

signals.title: Measure the compressed size of aggregate states in `estimateSizeOfCompressedState`
signals.text: `Aggregator::estimateSizeOfCompressedState` estimates how many bytes the aggregate states would take when a replica sends them to the initiator, which is how automatic parallel replicas decides whether distributing a query pays off. It builds a `CompressedWriteBuffer` over a `NullWriteBuffer`, but serializes the sampled states into the `NullWriteBuffer` directly and then reads that buffer's counter: ```cpp NullWriteBuffer wb; CompressedWriteBuffer wbuf(wb); // never written to ... aggregate_functions[j]->serialize(place + offsets_of_aggregate_states[j], wb); ... wbuf.finalize(); res += it ? static_cast<size_t>(table.size() * wb.count() / ((it + period - 1) / period)) : 0; ``` So nothing is ever compressed and, despite the function's name and its own `We only interested in the size of compressed state` comment, it returns the plain serialized size. `recordAggregationStateSizes` then stored that single number as all three of `bytes`, `sample_bytes` and `compressed_bytes`, which pins the compression ratio of the aggregation-state statistics to 1. `recordAggregationStateColumnSizes`, documented as `Mirrors the logic of Aggregator::estimateSizeOfCompressedState` for in-order aggregation, feeds the same `AggregationState` counters via `estimateCompressedColumnSize` and does measure the compressed size - so two producers of one statistic disagreed on what it means. This change serializes the sample through the compressing buffer and returns the sample's uncompressed and compressed sizes alongside the extrapolated total, letting the existing compression-ratio machinery in `RuntimeDataflowStatisticsCacheUpdater` apply the states' real ratio. Taking the ratio from the sample rather than compressing the extrapolated size also keeps the per-compressed-block framing overhead out of the extrapolation, where multiplying it by `table.size() / num_samples` would have inflated it. **Effect on the estimate.** Only queries whose output is dominated by compressible aggregate states move. That is exactly the shape that showed up as a CI failure of `03634_autopr_output_bytes_estimation` on master: `query_28` (`MIN(Referer)` states over a two-level hash table with many groups) estimated 59335657 bytes against a recorded 23722663, a ratio of 2.4996 that left the test's 2.5x bound no margin. Reading the estimates out of the failing job's server log, the ten other queries in that test match their recorded values within 1.00..1.41x, because their output is dominated by aggregation keys or by output columns, both of which were already measured compressed. So the recorded values expect the compressed size and this defect is why that one entry looked wrong. **Two small-sample corrections found while validating this in CI.** The compressed format writes a checksum and a block header in front of every block, so a sample of a few bytes comes out of `CompressedWriteBuffer` larger than it went in and the derived ratio drops below one, *inflating* the estimate. With an early conversion to a two-level hash table (`group_by_two_level_threshold=1`, which the test randomization sets) every one of the 256 buckets holds a handful of states and every per-bucket sample is dominated by that framing, which is what made `04034_autopr_dataflow_cache_reuse_between_different_queries` fail on the first run of this pull request: the two cache-reusing queries lost parallel replicas. When the states are really sent, the framing is amortized over `min_compress_block_size` of data, so such a sample is now reported as incompressible rather than as expanding, keeping the ratio at 1 - exactly what the caller assumed before the ratio was measured at all. The new test `04653_autopr_state_size_estimate_small_buckets` pins `group_by_two_level_threshold` to 1 and fails without that. Reviewing the same statistic end to end also turned up the mirror-image defect on the in-order-aggregation side, reported in review: `recordAggregationStateColumnSizes` totalled `IColumn::byteSize`, which for a `ColumnAggregateFunction` whose states live in a foreign arena (as `AggregatingInOrderTransform` hands them over) counts one pointer per row, so arena-backed states - `min(String)`, `groupArray`, `uniqExact` - were under-counted. That column is now sized from its serialized states too, sampling at most as many of them as the hash-table producer samples per bucket. **Recorded values.** The values in `03634_autopr_output_bytes_estimation` are empirical and need `test.hits`, so they are re-measured from this PR's own CI run rather than guessed - the test reports every query that lands outside the 2.5x band, and I will update whatever it reports. `query_1` and `query_20` are single `count()` states whose estimate becomes the ~29-byte compressed-block framing instead of a 2-3 byte varint; the test's `NOT (res.2 < 100 AND res.3 < 100)` guard already covers those. Verified so far: both changed translation units pass a full `-fsyntax-only` typecheck against master. The estimate itself is validated by CI, since reproducing it needs the stateful dataset. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111981 That PR is the interim, test-only fix for the master CI failure linked below: it re-records `query_28` as the ~58 MB the estimator currently reports. **The two changes touch the same line and are mutually exclusive.** If #111981 merges first, this PR must set `query_28` back to the post-fix measurement (expected to land near the original 23722663); if this PR merges first, #111981 should be closed as unnecessary. https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=5baed0f5a10c333cd220b9646d6ef4647425079d&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_asan_ubsan%2C%20distributed%20plan%2C%20parallel%29 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed the estimation of the size of aggregate states used by automatic parallel replicas: it measured the serialized size of the states instead of their compressed size, overestimating how much data a replica would send for queries that aggregate into large, compressible states. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111985&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/111985](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F111985+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Keep the function name of a stack frame attributed to a libc++ `__functional` header
signals.text: Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/57201 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/100419 `collapseDemangledNames` replaced a stack frame's function name with `?` whenever the frame's source location was a file in a directory ending in `functional`. The intent was to hide `std::function` plumbing frames, whose demangled names spell out the whole captured lambda type and say nothing the neighbouring frames do not already say. But the file of a frame is the source line the *instruction* maps to, which is not necessarily where the enclosing function is defined. An ordinary function can have individual instructions attributed to a libc++ `__functional` header - an inlined `std::function` operation, or compiler-generated code reported with line 0 - and then its name was dropped too, which loses the only useful part of the frame. This PR requires the symbol to name the `std::function` plumbing as well: the type-erasing wrappers (`std::__function::__func`, `__value_func`, `__policy_func`, ...) and the type erasure of `std::function` itself - its `operator()`, its copy, move and callable-taking constructors and assignment operators, and its destructor. The ordinary members of `std::function` (`swap`, `target_type`, `operator bool`, the `nullptr` reset `operator=(std::nullptr_t)`, the empty-constructing `function()` / `function(std::nullptr_t)`, ...) do work of their own, so they keep their names too. Those are still displayed as `?`, exactly as before; every other frame keeps its name - not only an ordinary `DB` function, but also a meaningful libc++ symbol that happens to live in a `__functional` header, such as `std::hash<String>::operator()` from `__functional/hash.h`, or the generic invocation helpers `std::invoke` / `std::__invoke` / `std::mem_fn`, which are not `std::function`-specific and whose frames can name the callable they dispatch to. This is much more likely in a build with ThinLTO enabled, where `std::function` calls are inlined across translation units, so it went unnoticed for a long time: `amd_cfi` is the only integration-test build with ThinLTO on, and its `test_crash_log` failure is what surfaced it. In that build, the frame that actually terminated the server was displayed as ``` 8. contrib/llvm-project/libcxx/include/__functional/function.h:0:7: ? @ 0x1c01f41f ``` both in the fatal log and in `trace_full` in `system.crash_log`, where `0x1c01f41f` is inside `DB::executeQuery` (the symbol resolves correctly - only the display suppressed it). Official release builds also use ThinLTO, so the same frames were being anonymised for users. `collapseDemangledNames` becomes a static member of `StackTrace` so that the heuristic is covered by a unit test in every build, rather than only by the weekly ThinLTO job. Fixes `test_crash_log/test.py::test_crash_log_extra_fields[terminate_with_exception-trace_full]` and `[terminate_with_std_exception-trace_full]`, seen in https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=b05161aa67d75ad84151a392f3e87156efd42842&name_0=WeeklyCFI&name_1=Integration%20tests%20%28amd_cfi%2C%202%2F4%29 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a stack frame being displayed as `?` instead of its function name in fatal log messages and in the `trace_full` column of `system.crash_log`. It affected frames of ordinary functions that have code attributed to a libc++ `__functional` header, which is common in release builds. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1334` (included in `26.8` and later) - Backported to: `26.7.4.44`, `26.5.7.57` <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Fix wrong intDiv/divide monotonicity for a constant dividend
signals.text: Fix wrong intDiv/divide monotonicity for a constant dividend Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106136 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes silently missing rows when a query filters on `intDiv(constant, key)` or `divide(constant, key)`. Primary-key and partition analysis reports the wrong direction of monotonicity for a constant divided by a key column, so matching granules are pruned away and the query returns fewer rows with no error. Also fixes `intDiv` with an unsigned constant dividend whose high bit is set, stops claiming monotonicity when a `Decimal` operand makes the division compute in the decimal's native width, and stops key analysis from raising `Cannot compare DB::IPv4 with long` for a valid query that divides an `IPv4`/`IPv6` constant by a key column. ### Description `FunctionBinaryArithmetic::getMonotonicityForRange` reports the direction of `c / x` incorrectly in its `const / variable` branch, so `KeyCondition::applyMonotonicFunctionsChainToRange` inverts the transformed range exactly when it must not, the range matches no granule, and matching rows are dropped with no error and exit code 0. Reproduced at completely default settings (no `SETTINGS` clause), 20000-row `Int32`-keyed MergeTree: ```sql SELECT count() FROM t WHERE intDiv(toInt32(-1000000), a) >= 11; -- keyed MergeTree: 0 ENGINE = Memory oracle: 10909 ``` #### Root cause For `f(x) = c / x` on an interval excluding 0, `d/dx (c/x) = -c/x²`, whose sign is `-sign(c)` for every `x != 0` — the `x²` denominator is positive on both sides of 0. So the direction is governed by `sign(c)` alone and is the *same* on the negative and the positive branch; only the values differ. The code instead treated the two arms as needing opposite polarity, which is the intuition that `1/x` "flips" across the branches. It does not: it is monotone on each branch separately, which is exactly why the strict range-sign guards are there. The two arms are now one return with a single `!is_constant_positive`, and the strict guards are kept verbatim. Fixing only that is not sufficient, and on its own would be *worse* than the current code for one shape. Three further defects live in the same branch: * **Unsigned constant dividend.** `intDiv` casts the dividend through `make_signed_t` whenever either operand is a signed integer (`DivisionUtils.h`), so an unsigned constant whose high bit is set divides as negative — `intDiv(toUInt8(200), x)` is `intDiv(toInt8(-56), x)` — while the raw `Field` still compares as positive. The boundary is `2^(8 * width - 1)` of the dividend's own width (verified for 8/16/32/64/128/256-bit dividends; the divisor width is irrelevant). This is reachable with no cast at all, because the literal `200` is `UInt8`. On a *negative* range the un-negated arm is accidentally correct for this shape, so adding the missing `!` alone would turn a correct answer into a wrong one. A new `intDivConstDividendReinterpretsNegative` helper corrects the effective sign; it deliberately does not reuse the existing `intDivConstReinterpretsNegative`, whose width early-out has the opposite polarity here. * **`Decimal` operand.** With a `Decimal` on either operand and no `Float` operand, the division computes in the decimal's native width (`DecimalBinaryOperation` casts both operands to `NativeResultType` and substitutes the integral operation even for `divide`). The divisor is then truncated, so `intDiv(toDecimal32(1000, 0), x)` is periodic in `x` with period `2^32` and not even monotonic. Nothing is claimed for that combination, mirroring the rejection the sibling `variable / constant` branch already performs. A `Decimal`/`Float` pair is exempt: it is converted to `Float64` before the operation, never truncates, and is itself a carrier of the direction defect, so those shapes are fixed rather than rejected. The rejection is deliberately keyed on the operand types and not on the constant's value, so it also covers a *zero* dividend and therefore runs ahead of the `constant == 0` fast path. That ordering is load-bearing: the truncation moves where the quotient is defined, so a range that strictly excludes 0 can still contain a point where the function is undefined, which is exactly what the zero-constant guard assumes away. With `Decimal32` the divisor truncates to `Int32`, so `intDiv(toDecimal32(0, 0), key)` over an `Int64` key range around `2^32` raises `ILLEGAL_DIVISION`; letting the zero guard win would claim monotonicity, prune the raising row away, and return a silent answer instead. Pinned by `c5iv`. * **Non-numeric operand (pre-existing exception on a valid query).** `IPv4`/`IPv6` are substituted with `UInt32`/`UInt128`, so their declared width does not describe the arithmetic, and their raw `Field` cannot be compared with a numeric zero. Two existing comparisons against zero therefore raise `Code: 169 BAD_TYPE_OF_FIELD "Cannot compare DB::IPv4 with long"` during key analysis today: one in the single-value fast path (reached when a granule's min equals its max) and one in the zero-constant guard (reached otherwise). Both roles are affected — `intDiv(toIPv4('192.168.0.1'), numeric_key)` and `intDiv(1, ipv4_key)` — and one of them fires even when the key range spans 0. A numeric gate hoisted above the fast path removes both; after it each query returns the correct rows with no pruning. Placing the gate inside the `const / variable` block would cover only the second site, which the new test pins at two granularities. Scope note: "both roles" here means the IP value as the dividend constant and as the key column, both with the constant on the left. The mirror shape, an IP constant as the *divisor* (`intDiv(numeric_key, toIPv4(...))`), still raises the same exception, as do `plus`/`minus`/`multiply` with an `IPv4`/`IPv6` operand. Both are pre-existing (measured byte-identical on `origin/master`) and are tracked separately rather than widened into this PR, since a correct fix for them also has to touch the `multiply` arm and the shared fast path. #### Behaviour changes to be aware of * **Two pre-existing key-analysis exceptions disappear.** As above, a non-numeric operand now reports non-monotonic instead of raising, so the query succeeds unpruned. This is a scope extension beyond "fix the direction", included because those same comparisons against zero are the mechanism being corrected and an exception on a valid query is a bug either way. * **Pruning is lost for `Decimal` shapes with no `Float` operand.** Measured with `EXPLAIN indexes = 1`: | shape | before | after | |---|---|---| | `Decimal32(0)` key, `intDiv(toInt32(-1000), a) = -25`, positive range | `Granules: 2/4` | `Granules: 4/4` | | `UInt64` key, `intDiv(toDecimal32(1000, 0), a) = 250` | `Granules: 2/4` | `Granules: 3/4` | | `Int64` key, `intDiv(toDecimal32(0, 0), a) = 5`, range around `2^32` | `Granules: 0/2` | `Granules: 2/2` | The first two queries return the same rows before and after — the index simply stops filtering. The third is the zero-dividend case: it must stop pruning, because the pruned plan silently returned `0` for a query that correctly raises `ILLEGAL_DIVISION`. This mirrors the decision already shipped for the `variable / constant` branch, where the same truncation applies. `Decimal`/`Float` pairs keep pruning and are additionally fixed. No committed reference in the repository changes. * **Everything else keeps pruning.** Strictly-positive ranges with a signed constant, both-unsigned operands, `Float` divisors, and unsigned key ranges crossing the divisor's own `2^(8W-1)` are all unaffected. That last group is worth naming: the *values* jump across the wrap while the *order* is preserved, which satisfies the non-strict definition of `Monotonicity`, so rejecting them would delete pruning that is correct today. The new test pins them, with plan-level assertions. #### Testing `04651_intdiv_const_variable_monotonicity` and its three siblings `..._decimal_float`, `..._controls` and `..._ip` compare a keyed MergeTree against an identical `ENGINE = Memory` table on the same data, so each of their 86 count rows prints `1` when index-based pruning agrees with the full-scan ground truth. The probes are split by family across four files, sharing one case numbering, so that no single file outgrows the CI per-test time limit: the cost is fixture DDL for the 26 tables of the (type, range, granularity) matrix, which cannot be trimmed without dropping coverage. Together they cover both range signs for both functions and both constant signs, unsigned dividends at several widths, `Decimal` in either role plus the `Decimal`/`Float` exemption, `Float64`/`LowCardinality`/`Nullable` keys, ranges that span zero or have zero as an endpoint, the unsigned wrap shapes, and the `IPv4`/`IPv6` cases at two granularities. Twelve further rows assert with `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` that the surviving shapes still prune (so the fix cannot silently degrade into "no pruning at all") and that the zero-dividend `Decimal` shape stops pruning — 98 asserted rows in total. On a master-HEAD binary the tests fail: 34 rows print `0` and `..._ip` aborts with `Code: 169 BAD_TYPE_OF_FIELD`. On this branch they pass, including 50/50 runs with randomized settings. Each of the four edits was mutation-tested individually — reverting the negation, the sign correction, the `Decimal` rejection, the `Float` exemption, the numeric gate, the gate's hoisted position and its role restriction each make specific named rows fail. `index_granularity` decides whether the range handed to `getMonotonicityForRange` is strictly negative, strictly positive or spans zero, so it is pinned per DDL and the test carries `no-random-merge-tree-settings` with that reason stated inline in each of the four files. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112156&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/112156](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F112156+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
