signals.title: Speed up window functions by evaluating each `MergeTree` partition independently
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108326 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114645 A window function plan sorts its input partitioned by the window `PARTITION BY` columns: every row is reshuffled across streams by `ScatterByPartitionTransform` (a hash pass over the `PARTITION BY` columns plus a repack of every column of every row through a full cross-stream `Resize`), so that whole window partitions land in single streams before the per-stream sort and `WindowTransform`. If the partition expression of the `MergeTree` table is a deterministic function of the window `PARTITION BY` columns, the reading will now emit each partition through a single port instead: every stream already carries whole window partitions, so the scatter is skipped entirely and the read, sort, and window all stay within per-partition streams. ```sql CREATE TABLE test_16 (a UInt64, b UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple() PARTITION BY sipHash64(a) % 16; INSERT INTO test_16 SELECT number % 100000, number FROM numbers_mt(30000000); OPTIMIZE TABLE test_16 FINAL; EXPLAIN PIPELINE SELECT a, sum(b) OVER (PARTITION BY a ORDER BY b) FROM test_16 SETTINGS allow_window_partitions_independently = 1, max_threads = 16; ``` ```response (Expression) ExpressionTransform × 16 (Window) Resize 16 → 16 WindowTransform × 16 (Sorting) MergeSortingTransform × 16 LimitsCheckingTransform × 16 PartialSortingTransform × 16 <- was: fed through Resize 16 → 1 + ScatterByPartitionTransform 1 → 16, reshuffling every row across streams (Expression) ExpressionTransform × 16 (ReadFromMergeTree) MergeTreeSelect(pool: ReadPoolInOrder, algorithm: InOrder) × 16 0 → 1 <- per-partition reading (16 partitions → 16 streams) ``` On `test_str_64 (a UInt64, b UInt64, s String)` with 30M rows, 100k window partitions over 64 balanced table partitions (`PARTITION BY sipHash64(a) % 64`), and a 100-byte random string in `s`, at `max_threads = 16`: | query | off | on | speedup | |--------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------|--------|---------| | `SELECT a, s, count(b) OVER (PARTITION BY a) FROM test_str_64` | 1.014s | 0.554s | 1.83× | | `SELECT a, s, sum(b) OVER (PARTITION BY a ORDER BY b) FROM test_str_64` | 1.492s | 0.956s | 1.56× | The scatter repacks every column of every row, so the win grows with the row width. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Speed up window functions on partitioned `MergeTree` tables by reading each partition through its own stream and evaluating the windows per partition, skipping the hash scatter that ordinarily reshuffles every row across threads before the window sort. This applies when the table partition expression is a deterministic function of the window `PARTITION BY` columns and is gated by the same cost heuristic as per-partition `GROUP BY` / `DISTINCT` (enough partitions relative to `max_threads`, no dominant partition). Controlled by the new settings `allow_window_partitions_independently` (enabled by default), `force_window_partitions_independently`, and `max_number_of_partitions_for_independent_window`. --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114783&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114783](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114783+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)]

signals.title: Convert OUTER join to INNER join by null-rejecting join conditions
signals.text: Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112456 Outer join to inner join conversion works by looking if a filter above the join rejects default values, NULLs in the case of nullable columns. This change allows join conditions of enclosing joins to be used for rejecting NULLs too: 1. optimizer pass `deriveNotNullFiltersFromJoin` derives `col IS NOT NULL` filters and adds them to the plan. 2. these filters get pushed down and used for the conversion as usual. 3. filters derived during planning are compiled away before execution. 4. optimizer pass `promotePlannerOnlyFilters` can promote planner derived filters to executable filters based on their estimated selectivity. #### Performance result from `join_convert_outer_to_inner_by_join_predicates.xml` and `promote_planner_only_not_null_filters.xml` ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Convert `OUTER JOIN` to `INNER JOIN` when a later JOIN filters out its NULL-extended rows, and filter NULL join keys directly at the table scan when column statistics show it is selective. Controlled by the new settings `query_plan_convert_outer_join_to_inner_join_by_join_predicates`, `query_plan_promote_planner_only_not_null_filters` and `query_plan_max_selectivity_for_promoting_not_null_filters` (all enabled by default).

signals.title: Extract reusable `ActionsDAG` lineage computation into `actionsDAGUtils`
signals.text: The new `traceActionsDAGLineage` computes lineage for every `ActionsDAG` output using iterative traversal with memoization shared across all output roots. Each output is traced to at most one input through supported hops. Hops are classified as: - `Identity` - `ValuePreserving` - `DistinctValuesBound`, meaning output NDV is bounded by input NDV plus `ndv_delta` Inputs and outputs are identified by position rather than column name, so the reusable lineage result remains unambiguous when names are duplicated. `remapColumnStats` in the join-order optimizer now uses this API instead of its local `describeValueHop`/ `backTrackColumnsInDag` traversal. This changes the call site as follows: - Lineage is computed once per `ActionsDAG`, with memoization shared across all outputs, instead of running an independent DFS for every statistics entry. - Statistics names that do not match a DAG input no longer trigger additional per-name traversals. A nonempty statistics map causes at most one lineage computation. - An explicit mapped.empty() guard preserves the common case where absent statistics require no lineage traversal. - Remapping becomes a direct loop over output lineage results, using the traced input position and ndv_delta. The lineage-related complexity changes from approximately `O(#stats × DAG)` to `O(DAG + #outputs)`, with the remaining statistics-map handling linear in the number of entries. For outputs that can be represented unambiguously by the name-keyed statistics map, the computed statistics remain unchanged. The supported-hop and `ndv_delta` rules are equivalent to the previous implementation: nullable-to-non-nullable hops may add one distinct value, and the existing overflow guard remains in place. `remapColumnStats` does not currently distinguish between lineage kinds; it only uses `traceability`, `input_position`, and `ndv_delta`. The reusable API handles duplicate names positionally. `remapColumnStats` itself remains keyed by column name and therefore cannot represent separate statistics for conflicting duplicate output names. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): - Not for changelog

signals.title: Fix `optimize_inverse_dictionary_lookup` for single-column complex keys wrapped in `tuple`
signals.text: Since 25.12, the analyzer pass `InverseDictionaryLookupPass` (setting `optimize_inverse_dictionary_lookup`, enabled by default) rewrites `dictGet(dict, attr, key_expr) <op> const` into a comparison of the key expression against dictionary keys: either constants folded from `dictGetKeys` (`key_expr = const`, `key_expr IN [consts]`, or `0`), or the subquery form `key_expr IN (SELECT <key columns> FROM dictionary(dict) WHERE attr <op> const)`. The key expression is reused verbatim as the left-hand side, while all rewrite shapes produce bare key values on the right-hand side. A complex-key dictionary with a single key column accepts (and much existing SQL uses) the `tuple()`-wrapped call form `dictGet(..., tuple(k))` — for it, the rewrite pits a one-element `Tuple` against a scalar, and a query that works on every release before 25.12 fails with `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT`. Multi-column keys are unaffected: `(k1, k2) IN (SELECT k1, k2 ...)` is the standard SQL form and the types line up. ## How to reproduce ```sql CREATE TABLE dict_source (k UUID, k2 String, attr String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k; INSERT INTO dict_source VALUES ('11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111', 'a', 'paywall'), ('22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222', 'b', 'onboarding'); CREATE DICTIONARY single_key_dict (k UUID, attr String DEFAULT '') PRIMARY KEY k SOURCE(CLICKHOUSE(TABLE 'dict_source')) LIFETIME(0) LAYOUT(COMPLEX_KEY_HASHED()); CREATE TABLE data (k UUID, k2 String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k; INSERT INTO data VALUES ('11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111', 'a'), ('33333333-3333-3333-3333-333333333333', 'c'); -- Must return 1, but fails since 25.12: SELECT count() FROM data WHERE dictGet('single_key_dict', 'attr', tuple(k)) = 'paywall'; ``` On master the query fails in the constant-fold path: ``` Code: 43. DB::Exception: Illegal types of arguments (`Tuple(UUID)`, `UUID`) of function `equals`. (ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT) ``` On 26.3 (before the `dictGetKeys` constant fold existed) the same query fails in the subquery path with `Illegal type Tuple(UUID) of argument of function toUUID`. The workaround on affected releases is `SETTINGS optimize_inverse_dictionary_lookup = 0`, which returns the correct result. The bare-key form `dictGet(..., k)` and multi-column keys work on all versions. ## The fix Normalize the key expression once, before both rewrite paths, when the dictionary key is composite with exactly one key column and the key expression resolves to a one-element tuple (including a `Nullable` one, e.g. produced by `if(cond, tuple(k), NULL)`): - a syntactic `tuple(k)` call is replaced by its argument; - any other tuple-typed expression (e.g. a column of type `Tuple(UUID)`) is wrapped in `tupleElement(expr, 1)`, which propagates `NULL` with the same semantics `dictGet` has for `NULL` keys. The rewrite still fires for these queries — the new test asserts the rewritten plans via `EXPLAIN SYNTAX run_query_tree_passes=1` for all three constant-fold shapes and both subquery shapes. Simple-key dictionaries are deliberately not unwrapped: `dictGet(simple_dict, attr, tuple(id))` is rejected (`Illegal type Tuple(UInt64) of argument of function toUInt64`) even with the optimization disabled, so normalizing there would make otherwise-invalid queries succeed only while the optimization is on. A `Tuple`-typed dictionary key column cannot conflict with the unwrapping because dictionaries reject `Tuple` attribute types (`Unknown type Tuple(UUID) for dictionary attribute`). ## Implicit key type conversion Review pointed out a second gap in the same rewrite: `dictGet` implicitly converts the key expression to the key column type (`IDictionary::convertKeyColumns`, which uses `castColumnAccurate` — see also `02176_dict_get_has_implicit_key_cast`), so e.g. a `String` key expression is a valid lookup key for a `UUID` key column. The rewritten comparison converts via a common supertype instead, so any single-column key whose type has no common supertype with the key column type failed with `NO_COMMON_TYPE` — with the tuple wrapper, bare on a complex-key dictionary, and on simple-key dictionaries alike (the latter two forms were broken this way before this PR as well). The conversion contract includes the throwing behavior: `castColumnAccurate` throws on values the key column type cannot represent (with a `UInt8` key column, `dictGet(..., toInt16(x))` throws on `x = -1` or `x = 300`), while a comparison evaluated in a common supertype would silently return false for them. So the key expression is left untouched only when the key column type is itself the least supertype of the two types — a provably total widening, e.g. a narrow integer column against a wide key type, which keeps the expression usable for index analysis and keeps `04276_function_dict_get_keys_edge_cases` byte-identical (this is the same criterion `canReplaceWithDictGetKeys` already uses for the attribute side). Any other single-column mismatch is wrapped in `accurateCast` to the key column type, which matches `castColumnAccurate` semantics exactly, including throwing the same `CANNOT_CONVERT_TYPE` on lossy values. The criterion is total for integer-to-float pairs as well: `getLeastSupertype` refuses e.g. `Int64` with `Float64` (not enough mantissa bits), so an integer expression stays on the no-cast path only when the float key type represents every its value exactly. A `Nullable` expression that needs such a conversion makes `dictGet` itself throw regardless of the optimization (at `NULL` rows the nested column holds default values, and e.g. an empty string does not parse as `UUID`), so the rewrite is skipped there and the query keeps its unoptimized behavior. One pre-existing behavior is kept and pinned by the test: when the attribute value matches no keys, the predicate constant-folds to `0` without evaluating the key expression, so a conversion error that the unoptimized `dictGet` would throw for unconvertible rows disappears together with the lookup — the same already happens for bare mistyped key expressions on master, like for any constant fold that eliminates evaluation. Review also caught a related pre-existing defect in the single-match constant fold, fixed here since the tuple normalization newly routes the wrapped spelling into it (it used to throw instead): when the attribute value belongs to the NULL-keyed row of a dictionary with a `Nullable` key column, the fold produced `key_expr = NULL`, which is NULL for every row, while `dictGet` misses the NULL row for non-NULL keys and the predicate must be false there (observable under `NOT`, `isNull`, or in a projection; a bare `Nullable` key expression like `toNullable(id)` hits the same fold on master). A single NULL key now keeps the `IN [NULL]` form, which is false for non-NULL keys and NULL for NULL keys — matching `dictGet`, which returns NULL for a NULL key expression and does not match the NULL-keyed row through it. Known pre-existing gap, intentionally out of scope: multi-column composite keys with a mistyped component (e.g. `dictGet(dict, attr, tuple(toString(id), id_key))` over a `(UInt64, String)` key) hit the same `NO_COMMON_TYPE` failure. Fixing that requires rebuilding the tuple with per-element casts and is better done as a follow-up than inside this backport-targeted fix. The new test `04891_optimize_inverse_dictionary_lookup_single_key_tuple` covers the failing forms (syntactic tuple, tuple-typed column, `Nullable` tuple, implicitly-converted `String` keys — wrapped, bare, and simple-key, and lossy `Int16`-over-`UInt8` keys both in-range and throwing out-of-range), the bare-key, numeric-widening and two-column-key controls, a constant on either side of the comparison, the equal-error behavior for `Nullable` keys that need conversion, the zero-match constant-fold behavior, and result equality with the optimization on and off. All existing `optimize_inverse_dictionary_lookup` tests pass unchanged. ## Backport This is a regression in an official stable release (25.12) affecting all later releases, including 26.3 LTS. Please consider labeling for backport to 26.3 (`v26.3-must-backport`). ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` and `NO_COMMON_TYPE` errors when `optimize_inverse_dictionary_lookup` rewrites `dictGet` comparisons: for complex-key dictionaries with a single key column called with a `tuple()`-wrapped (possibly `Nullable`) key expression, and for single-column keys whose expression relies on `dictGet`'s implicit key type conversion (e.g. a `String` expression for a `UUID` key). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114865&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114865](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114865+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Prometheus HTTP API: implement /api/v1/series
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - **Experimental Feature** ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ****Prometheus HTTP API:** implement **`/api/v1/series`** for **`TimeSeries`** tables.** ### Why this matters **Prometheus clients** use **`/api/v1/series`** to discover the label sets stored for active series. This endpoint is used by **Prometheus-compatible tools** such as **Grafana** when they need to populate metric and label selectors. ClickHouse **`TimeSeries` tables** can store labels in the main **`tags` Map**, in dedicated columns configured with **`tags_to_columns`**, or in a mixture of both layouts. The endpoint needs to expose the **same logical series** regardless of how those labels are stored. ### Description This PR adds **Prometheus `/api/v1/series` support** for **`TimeSeries` tables**. The endpoint is available through both a **dedicated `/api/v1/series` handler** and the **combined `/api/v1` handler**. It supports **GET requests** and **`application/x-www-form-urlencoded` POST requests**. Supported parameters: - **`match[]`** selects series by metric name and label matchers. Repeated parameters are combined as a **union** and overlapping results are returned only once through **deduplication**. - **`start` and `end`** select series overlapping the requested **time range**. - **`limit`** limits the number of returned series and reports when the response was **truncated**. ### Changes - **Selector parsing:** parse Prometheus series selectors with equality, inequality, regular-expression, and negative regular-expression matchers. - **Storage compatibility:** support metric names, labels in the **`tags` Map**, dedicated tag columns, and mixed rows that use both storage layouts. - **Label normalization:** normalize missing labels to the **Prometheus empty-value semantics** and include the full logical label set in each response. - **PromQL compatibility:** support quoted label names and anchor regular expressions to the **complete label value**. - **Input validation:** validate selectors and timestamps before executing the query. - **Time ranges:** apply the time-range filter when trusted min/max data is available. When it is not available, keep the request valid and return the **compatible candidate superset** allowed by the Prometheus API. - **Result limits:** support zero and positive limits, exact-limit responses, truncation reporting, and invalid-value errors. - **Access control:** read the underlying series metadata through the **`TimeSeries` table-function path** after checking access to the configured **`TimeSeries` table**. Unknown routes are resolved before authorization, so they keep the normal **404 response**. - **Existing endpoints:** apply the configured **`TimeSeries` table access boundary** consistently to the existing Prometheus query endpoints. - **Query lifecycle:** run the generated query through the **normal query pipeline** and keep **query logging** and **query completion handling** intact. ### Tests Added integration coverage for: - **Matcher operators:** metric-name and label selectors with all matcher operators. - **Repeated selectors:** repeated **`match[]`** parameters, selector unions, and overlapping-result deduplication. - **Storage layouts:** Map labels, dedicated tag columns, missing labels, mixed carriers, conflicting carriers, and **`__name__`**. - **Regex and names:** quoted label names and whole-value regular-expression anchoring. - **Selector validation:** invalid and unbounded selectors, including the valid **`{host!~".*"}`** case. - **Time ranges:** two-sided, one-sided, inclusive, and invalid time ranges. - **Min/max behavior:** requests with and without trusted min/max metadata. - **Limits:** zero, exact, positive, maximum, and invalid **`limit`** values. - **HTTP methods:** GET and form POST requests. - **Authorization:** wrapper-only **`SELECT` grants**, access checks for all query endpoint families, and unknown-route handling. - **Observability:** query completion records and the existing query API limit behavior. Also ran **Python syntax checks** and **`git diff --check`**. ### Documentation **Documentation is written.** The **TimeSeries engine documentation** now covers the Prometheus handler configuration and the **`/api/v1/series` endpoint parameters**. ### Stack This is the **base PR** for the follow-up Prometheus API endpoints: - **#114868** adds **`/api/v1/labels`**. - **#114869** adds **`/api/v1/label/<name>/values`**. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114867&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114867](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114867+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Sync BACKUP FROM SNAPSHOT settings, failpoints and backup writer helpers
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-private/pull/67265 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-private/pull/69490 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-private/pull/63082 Resumable `BACKUP FROM SNAPSHOT` is implemented in ClickHouse Cloud, but it touches files shared with this repository. This syncs the parts that shared code refers to unconditionally, so those files compile here as well. **Setting.** `resumable_backup_from_snapshot` is declared, and `BackupsWorker` rejects it with `WRONG_BACKUP_SETTINGS` instead of accepting and ignoring it, because `BACKUP FROM SNAPSHOT` does not exist in this build. Query settings are declared through a macro list that cannot carry preprocessor directives, so a Cloud-only query setting cannot simply be omitted here; recognizing it and reporting a clear error is the alternative to silence. The two batch-size settings of the same feature, `resumable_backup_batch_size` and `resumable_backup_batch_size_bytes`, are deliberately **not** synced. They are read only from Cloud-only code, so here they would be accepted and then ignored, and a setting cannot be withdrawn once released. They are being declared as Cloud-only backup settings instead. **Backup writer helpers.** Two `IBackupWriter` members that shared backup code already calls: - `readFile(file_name, expected_file_size)` was a protected member of `BackupWriterDefault`, used only by `fileContentsEqual`. Every writer already implements it, so promoting it to the interface adds no implementation. - `writeFileIfNotExists` creates a file without replacing an existing one. The default implementation falls back to `writeFile`, so `File`, `Disk`, `Null` and `Memory` writers are unchanged; the `S3` and `AzureBlobStorage` writers pass `object_storage_write_if_none_match` so the creation is atomic. **Failpoints.** The backup failpoints are listed in the same order as in ClickHouse Cloud, so `src/Common/FailPoint.cpp` is identical in both repositories and does not conflict on every back-sync. Verified by compiling every translation unit under `src/Backups`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114871&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114871](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114871+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Follow-ups for CREATE HANDLER: parse limits of the stored query, docs, refactoring
signals.text: Follow-ups from https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106231 (`CREATE HANDLER`). Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106231 **Requested in review of #106231:** - The two predicates over `IAST::QueryKind` that describe the `readonly` mode - whether a query of that kind is rejected under it, and whether `readonly = 2` still lets it produce side effects - moved out of `SQLDefinedHandlerFromAST` into `Interpreters/QueryKindUnderReadonly.h`; `queryKindRequiresMutatingMethod` is renamed to `isQueryKindRejectedUnderReadonly` after the property it reports. The handler code keeps the statement-level refinements and the HTTP-method fences. - `currentHandler` and `currentRequestURL` were registered with `IntroducedIn` 26.6 (the development version when they were written); they are released in 26.8. **The one unresolved review finding:** a request could still lower the parse limits of a handler's query. `HTTPHandler::processQuery` relaxed `max_parser_depth` / `max_parser_backtracks` *before* applying the settings the request supplies, and a request names settings freely - so `GET /h?max_parser_depth=1` put the caller's value back and broke a handler the server itself had accepted. The relaxation now happens after the request settings. `max_query_size` had the same hole and did not even need a hostile request: a stored query longer than its default value is creatable and reloadable (both parse without a size limit) but failed on every invocation; it is now raised to fit the query text - not disabled, because `executeQuery` also uses `max_query_size` to decide how much of the request stream to read ahead in search of the query text, where `0` would make it read a single byte. New tests `04897_handler_request_parser_limits` and `04898_handler_large_query_invocation`, both verified to fail without the fix. **Documentation:** the `CREATE HANDLER` page was written into `docs/en/sql-reference/statements/create/handler.md` - a path in the legacy Docusaurus tree that `9440ca729a3` had already removed - so the only documentation of `CREATE HANDLER` / `ALTER HANDLER` / `DROP HANDLER` was published nowhere. It moves to `docs/reference/statements/create/handler.mdx`, with the frontmatter and internal links converted to that tree's conventions and the page registered in `docs/reference/navigation.json`. `docs/en/operations/system-tables/handlers.md` was a leftover copy of the generated `docs/reference/system-tables/handlers.mdx` whose hand-written `SHOW HANDLERS` / secret-masking paragraph had been lost; that paragraph is restored and the legacy copy deleted. The statement is now cross-referenced from the HTTP interface page, the `DROP` page and the `ALTER` overview, and the anchored (`RE2::FullMatch`) semantics of `URL REGEXP` are documented. Verified locally: all 30 SQL-defined-handler stateless tests pass against a server built from this branch (the 31st match of the `handler` filter, `03354_tcp_handler_async_insert_bug`, is unrelated and needs a writable `/var/lib/clickhouse/user_files`), and `04844_handler_deep_query_invocation` still passes without the fix, confirming it covered only the session-level limit. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed HTTP handler invocation so request-level `max_parser_depth`, `max_parser_backtracks`, and `max_query_size` no longer break stored handler queries, and published the `CREATE HANDLER`, `ALTER HANDLER`, and `DROP HANDLER` documentation. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114883&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114883](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114883+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: AI functions: Make quotas per query not per block
signals.text: `AIQuotaTracker` was a stack local inside `executeImpl`, so every block and every pipeline stream started with a fresh allowance. The `ai_function_max_api_calls_per_query`, `ai_function_max_input_tokens_per_query` and `ai_function_max_output_tokens_per_query` limits therefore scaled with the data (one allowance per block per function) instead of bounding the query — any limit above the largest block's row count could never fire. The tracker is now a single instance owned by the query `Context` and shared by every AI function call in that context, with atomic counters for the concurrent pipeline threads. The API-call limit is claimed with an atomic bounded reservation, so it is an exact cap within a query-execution context even under `max_threads > 1`; the token limits are best-effort, since a call's token usage is known only after its response arrives. The limits are enforced per server / query fragment: a distributed query (across shards or parallel-replica fragments) enforces them independently on each, not summed globally. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The AI-function quota settings (`ai_function_max_api_calls_per_query`, `ai_function_max_input_tokens_per_query`, `ai_function_max_output_tokens_per_query`) were enforced per block rather than per query, letting a query exceed the configured limit in proportion to the number of blocks and threads processed. They now bound the whole query per server: the API-call limit is an exact cap (atomic reservation), and the token limits are best-effort. A distributed query enforces the limits independently on each participating server / fragment. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114885&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114885](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114885+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not abort the server when a loader worker cannot be spawned
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110174 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a server abort that happens when the global thread pool is momentarily saturated while tables are still loading. `AsyncLoader` now keeps running if it cannot spawn an extra loader worker and some worker will still drain the queued jobs, instead of calling `std::terminate`. ### Description `AsyncLoader::spawn` wrapped `scheduleOrThrowOnError` in `NOEXCEPT_SCOPE`, whose handler is unconditionally `std::terminate()`. A transient `CANNOT_SCHEDULE_TASK` from a saturated global thread pool therefore killed the server (`Received signal 6`) during table loading. Seen 4 times over 4 unrelated PRs and 4 build flavours in 30 days, e.g. [`Stress test (arm_tsan)`](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108468&sha=27a154474608ee82636207020a9bd13beb8c9449&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_tsan%29), whose stack is `terminate_handler()` -> `std::terminate()` -> `AsyncLoader.cpp:908` `spawn()` -> `:744` `enqueue()`. A spawn must succeed only when nothing else will drain the pool's ready queue, so it now tells three states apart: - a worker that entered `worker()` and is not inside `wait()` drains the queue now; - a worker inside `wait()` on *another* pool's job resumes draining once that job runs; - neither of those means nobody ever will. In the first two cases `spawn` uses the non-throwing `trySchedule`, rolls back its `Pool::workers` increment on failure, warns and returns false. Only the last case keeps the fatal path, byte for byte: the queued jobs would be stranded, and throwing is not an option because `schedule` marks that region non-exception-safe. Covering it needs rollback-and-retry across the loading DAG, out of scope here. All 4 observed rows are recoverable. `BackgroundSchedulePool` narrows the same way (`929227464f9736b`). Two counters are added because `Pool::workers` also counts a worker still queued in the global pool, which drains nothing, and one blocked in `wait()`, which cannot take its own pool's jobs. A saturated pool is remembered so the failing thread creation happens once per episode, not once per queued job, counted by the new `AsyncLoaderSpawnFailures` event; entering `wait()` clears the memo. Tests are gtests asserting which branch was taken, not just that the process survived. A SQL test cannot reach the line: on master the whole call sits under `blockFaultInjections()`. Related: #110174, which removed the mask that hid this exception. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Backported to: `26.7.4.53` <!-- ch-version-info:end -->
signals.author: groeneai

signals.title: Fix AI functions embedding counters behavior on error
signals.text: `aiEmbed` and `aiSimilarity` under-report provider usage in `system.query_log` when a request fails: with the default `ai_function_throw_on_error = 1` the exception row shows `AIAPICalls = 0` and `AIInputTokens = 0`, although the provider was called and billed. Flipping only that setting records the call: | `ai_function_throw_on_error` | `AIAPICalls` | `AIRowsSkipped` | |---|---:|---:| | `1` (default) | 0 | 0 | | `0` | 1 | 1 | Same query and endpoint, with `ai_function_max_retries = 0` so exactly one attempt is made. **Cause.** `embedTexts` accumulates the counters in a local `EmbeddingResult` and returns it by value. When a failed request rethrows, `return` is never reached: the local is destroyed while unwinding and the caller's `embedding_result` is never constructed, so the caller's `ProfileEvents::increment` calls are both skipped and left with nothing to read. That defeats the intent stated at the accumulation site, which counts `api_calls` *before* issuing the request so that failed calls are still counted. **Fix.** `embedTexts` now reports `AIAPICalls` and `AIInputTokens` itself, from a `SCOPE_EXIT` guard, so the normal and throwing exits both publish them. They are plain locals rather than fields of `EmbeddingResult`, so no caller can count them twice. Callers keep their own row counters, which mean different things: texts for `aiEmbed`, pairs of texts for `aiSimilarity`. **Not covered.** Row counters are still dropped when the query throws. It delivered no rows, and preserving them would need `embedTexts` to take an out-parameter in both callers. **Tests.** Three integration tests, each verified to fail with the source reverted to `master`: one per caller for `AIAPICalls`, plus one driving the quota-exceeded throw so a batch succeeds first and `AIInputTokens` is non-zero. The failed-request tests cannot cover `AIInputTokens`, since there the first request fails and no tokens are consumed. The same defect on the text-generation path is fixed in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111830, which is what introduced a throwing path there. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111830 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `aiEmbed` and `aiSimilarity` reporting zero `AIAPICalls` and `AIInputTokens` in `system.query_log` when a provider request failed, despite the request having been made and billed.

signals.title: Fix undefined behavior in DateTime64 reservoir quantiles
signals.text: The reservoir-sampling implementation of `quantile` and `quantiles` previously interpolated decimal-backed values through `Float64`. `DateTime64` ticks close to the upper `Int64` boundary, as well as `Decimal128` and `Decimal256` values near their limits, can collapse to the same `Float64` value and make conversion back to the native representation undefined or return an incorrect endpoint. Interpolate decimal-backed samples in their exact native domain instead, and cover scalar/plural `DateTime64` plus wide-decimal boundary cases with stateless regression tests. Found by the `arm_asan_ubsan` stress test: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112573&sha=762fa93f05ca081011efec5fef767e3c36be6853&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%2C%20s3%29 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114485 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107154 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed undefined behavior and incorrect boundary results in `quantile` and `quantiles` for `DateTime64` and wide `Decimal` values.

signals.title: Make a table read by a scalar subquery in a CONSTRAINT a loading dependency
signals.text: Attaching a table analyzes its constraints in `InterpreterCreateQuery::getConstraintsDescription`, and the analysis executes the scalar subqueries of a constraint expression. The tables such a subquery reads were not registered as loading dependencies, because `DDLLoadingDependencyVisitor` only looks at functions, dictionary sources and the storage definition. Nothing prevented dropping such a table, and the server did not start afterwards - attaching the dependent table threw `UNKNOWN_TABLE` and loading the metadata failed: ```sql CREATE TABLE t1 (id UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); CREATE TABLE t2 (conversation UInt64, CONSTRAINT c CHECK (SELECT id FROM t1 LIMIT 15) IN (conversation)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); DROP TABLE t1; -- accepted, and the server cannot start anymore ``` The referential dependency was recorded, since `DDLDependencyVisitor` visits `ASTTableExpression`, so `check_referential_table_dependencies = 1` rejected the `DROP`. But that setting is off by default, and it is the loading graph that the default `check_table_dependencies` check and the `DROP DATABASE` drop order (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/97057) use. A constraint declaration is now visited, and the tables of every subquery that the analysis executes are added to the loading dependencies. Subqueries which the analysis does not execute - the right argument of `IN` and the argument of `exists`, see `ExecuteScalarSubqueriesMatcher::visit` - are skipped, because what they read is needed only when the constraint is checked, not to attach the table. That keeps `02916_joinget_dependency`-style patterns working, in particular `02841_not_ready_set_constraints`, which drops the table read by an `x IN (SELECT ...)` constraint on purpose. Seen in CI as a `Cannot start clickhouse-server` stress failure, e.g. https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110231&sha=4de836223549fd5224ca017b8c1a28e344ce38e9&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_msan%29 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114918 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/87369 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A table read by a scalar subquery inside a `CONSTRAINT` is now a loading dependency of the table that declares the constraint. Previously such a table could be dropped, after which the server did not start, because attaching the dependent table executes the subquery. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114923&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114923](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114923+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Add a style check for the spelling of `ClickHouse`
signals.text: The product name is written `ClickHouse` - one word, with a capital `C` and a capital `H`. Two case variants are accepted, because a mixed case is unusable there: `clickhouse` for identifiers, package, binary and host names, and `CLICKHOUSE` for macros and environment variables. Everything else - `Clickhouse`, `clickHouse`, `click_house`, `CLICK_HOUSE`, `click-house`, `Click House` - is a misspelling, and until now nothing stopped it from being committed. ## The check The new `clickhouse_spelling` check of the style job searches every file tracked by git, and the file names themselves, in code as well as in comments, messages and documentation. A `git grep -P` prefilter finds the candidate lines (a provable superset of what is reported), so the check costs about a second on a warm page cache and a minute on a cold one. Only the space-separated form is anchored at word boundaries, so an unrelated phrase - "click Household" - is not taken for the product name. The other forms are left unanchored on purpose, so that a misspelling inside a longer identifier - `ClickhouseBuffer` - is reported too. Rather than a long list of excused files, the sources of false positives are handled structurally: * `contrib` - third-party sources. * The generated locale directories of the documentation, `docs/<locale>/` and `docs/snippets/<locale>/`, taken from `docs/gt.config.json`. They are a machine translation of the English pages, so a misspelling there is fixed by fixing the English page; the default locale is not excluded, and `docs/en/` stays enforced. * Release notes - a record of what was published, not edited after the fact. Same pattern as the "new analyzer" wording check in `various_checks.sh`, so the landing and status pages that live next to them stay enforced. * `docs/_specs` - API specifications pinned from their generator by `ci/jobs/cloud_api_docs_nightly.py`. * Regions between `AUTOGENERATED_START` and `AUTOGENERATED_END` markers. Their source of truth - a `FunctionDocumentation` string, for instance - is checked instead, which is what a contributor is supposed to edit. * URLs. A link whose path spells the name differently is not a mistake we can fix, and rewriting it would only break the link. `docs/resources/about/adopters.mdx` alone holds eleven of them. What is left goes into `ci/jobs/scripts/check_style/clickhouse_spelling_ignore.txt`, in the spirit of the existing `experimental_settings_ignore.txt`: a path alone exempts a file, a path followed by a literal exempts only the lines containing that literal. It has fifteen entries, each with the reason next to it, and every one of them is text that is not ours to spell: names defined by other projects (the `ClickhouseClientOptions` of our Azure SDK fork, the `clickHouse*` parameters of Google's Dataflow templates, a third-party client library), verbatim quotations (Stack Overflow post titles shown as query output), and the misspellings that tests feed to the server on purpose - `LIKE` / `ILIKE` case variants, `hasPhrase(message, 'Click House')`, `click_house:` as an unknown URI scheme. ## The fixes The check found 191 misspellings, all fixed here. Most are prose and comments. The renamed identifiers are `isClickhouseApp`, `getClickhouseAttemptNumber` / `setClickhouseAttemptNumber`, `getClickhouseTableSchemaById` / `hasClickhouseTableSchemaById`, the `Clickhouse*` classes of `clickhouse-diagnostics`, the `tabClickhouse` / `btnQueryClickhouse` element ids of the `utils` web tools, and `clickHousePartsInserter.js`, which is renamed. No stale reference to an old name survives - one would be a misspelling, and the check reports those. Three of the fixes are visible to tests, and the first two rely on the server being case-insensitive there, which I confirmed against a running server rather than assumed: * the `X-Clickhouse-Format` HTTP header of `02015_async_inserts_1` - Poco header collections compare names case-insensitively; * the `SOURCE(Clickhouse(...))` dictionary source of `03071_fix_short_circuit_logic` - the parser lowercases the source name (`ExpressionElementParsers.cpp`); * a directory named `Clickhouse` in `03600_disk_app_plain_rewritable_disks_list_cmd`, renamed in the command and in the reference. Its position in the listing is unchanged, since `ClickHouse` sorts before `Cloud` either way. The rule is also written down as item 18 of the `Names` section of the style guide, so a contributor can find it before CI tells them. ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114926&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114926](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114926+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Keep 04896_orfill_merge_group_by_overflow_any on the projection merge path at any granularity
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114740 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `04896_orfill_merge_group_by_overflow_any` fails deterministically whenever the test runner randomizes `index_granularity_bytes` small: ``` Code: 117. DB::Exception: Projection p is specified in setting force_optimize_projection_name but not used. (INCORRECT_DATA) ``` Seen at four different values (7801, 9281, 49209 and locally at 1024), so it reds unrelated PRs' CI (most recently #112889 and #76867), and the arm stops covering the null-place `mergeBatch` segfault it was added for in #114740. A throw is not coverage. The optimizer is correct here. The table declares two projections, and `p` stores four aggregate states where `p2` stores one; granule sizing charges an aggregate-state column at its serialized width, so at small `index_granularity_bytes` `p` reads more marks than the base table and than `p2`, and is dropped (`optimizeUseAggregateProjection.cpp:1036` and `:1048`). At coarse granularity every candidate floors to one granule per part, the marks tie, and `p` wins only because it is declared first. The fix removes both comparisons from the fixture rather than constraining the randomizer: `index_granularity_bytes = 0` turns off adaptive granularity on the table, so a projection's mark count no longer depends on state width. The `sumOrNull` arm, the only one where `p2` is a candidate at all, also names `p` as preferred, which reduces the candidate list to one entry before any cost comparison. `force_optimize_projection_name = 'p'` is kept, so each arm still asserts that `p` specifically was used. `index_granularity_bytes`, `min_bytes_for_wide_part` and `use_const_adaptive_granularity` stay randomized. This matches `04063` and `04365`, the other tests using this pin. Validated: all four culprit values pass; 5 arms x 36 setting combinations (Compact and Wide) pass with the pinned projection applied; 50/50 runs with and without randomization; and the pre-fix binary still segfaults in `AggregateFunctionOrFill::mergeBatch` with this fixture, so the defect stays covered. `.reference` is unchanged.

signals.title: Coordinate a read with pinned block numbers in classic parallel replicas
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114263 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/97557 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix wrong results when a `SELECT` with `select_sequential_consistency = 1` on a `ReplicatedMergeTree` table runs with classic (task-based) parallel replicas. Every replica performed a complete local read clamped to the quorum boundary instead of a coordinator-assigned slice, so rows were returned once per participating replica. ### Description `StorageReplicatedMergeTree::read` routes a `select_sequential_consistency = 1` query into `readLocalSequentialConsistencyImpl`, which called `MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor::read` with `enable_parallel_reading` hardcoded to `false`. The setting is propagated to the followers, so each follower took that same branch: `read_task_callback` was never installed, the follower never announced its parts, and it read the whole pinned range locally. The initiator then merged N complete copies. On a 5-part `ReplicatedMergeTree` with a pinned boundary of 12000 rows and `max_parallel_replicas = 3`, `count()` returned 36000 and `sum()` was likewise tripled, with no exception and no warning. It scaled exactly linearly with `max_parallel_replicas`, and `uniqExact` stayed correct, confirming pure per-replica duplication. Reaching the defect requires turning off one of the optimizations that would otherwise bypass this read path: `optimize_trivial_count_query = 0` for `count()`, since at its default the planner serves the count from `totalRows()` and disables parallel replicas, or `parallel_replicas_local_plan = 0` or `parallel_replicas_prefer_local_replica = 0` for data reads. All three are documented, settable per query, and leave the wrong result silent. The fix passes `canUseParallelReplicasOnFollower()` at that call site, exactly as the sibling `readLocalImpl` already does for the non-pinned path, so the pinned read participates in coordination instead of being silently excluded from it. The boundary stays computed and applied: when it binds it comes from ZooKeeper and is identical on every replica (measured on two replicas holding different part sets, 7 and 6 active parts, both clamping to the same block), and with no quorum node it is the replica's own maximum, which excludes nothing it owns. Validation: new test `04912_pr_classic_pinned_block_numbers` fails on master and passes with the change, 50/50 green under randomized settings. Full matrix in the validation-gate comment below. Out of scope, neither introduced nor altered here: the plan-based path with `parallel_replicas_local_plan = 0` (#114263), and divergent part sets with no quorum node (#105710).

signals.title: Report RabbitMQ container recreation attempts made by the startup retry
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114415 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114434 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description #114415 made the RabbitMQ readiness waiter recreate a container that fails to start and try again, turning a 21-case module abort into a passing run. When the second attempt succeeds, every channel that could record the first failure closes at once: artifact collection is gated on a failing suite (`if failed_suits:`), the report log strips setup logs from passed tests (`--report-log-exclude-logs-on-passed-tests`), and `job.log` never carried harness logging. The recovered failure survives only as an anomalous duration on the module's first test: +123.5 s against a p99 of 13.4 s over 7774 runs of that test and lane. So a retry-absorbed run discards exactly the diagnostics #114415 added to show where a hang is stuck. Now: - the waiter copies the failed attempt's `rabbit.log` out of the instance directory before recreating the container (that directory is removed on teardown) and emits a stable `RABBITMQ_RECREATE` token. The copy is named per process, cluster, waiter call and attempt, because S3 upload keys use the basename alone; - at job end the script counts those tokens across the per-worker pytest logs, puts the count in `Result.info` and attaches the preserved logs, whatever the outcome. The failure-gated paths are left alone. A recreation is not itself a verdict, so only `info` and `files` are touched: status and labels stay as the test results set them, and the count is appended after the job's own `Failures: N/M` summary rather than replacing it. Forcing a retry on a healthy host passes, and the count reaches `result_*.json` with the 107,336 B broker log attached. The same run with the reporting removed attaches nothing; a run that never retried writes no count; a forced-red run keeps its `Failures: 1/1`. `test_system_stop.py` is 21 passed. Both sides are unit-tested, each arm checked against a mutation of the code it pins. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114947&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114947](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114947+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Support ROLLUP, CUBE, GROUPING SETS and grouping() with make_distributed_plan
signals.text: Support `ROLLUP`, `CUBE`, `GROUPING SETS` and the `grouping` function under `make_distributed_plan`. 11 of the 99 TPC-DS queries use `ROLLUP`. - `RollupStep` and `CubeStep` are serialized (query plan serialization version 8), so they can run in a worker stage, for example below a distributed `ORDER BY`. - The `grouping` function specializations held their parameters inside the function object and could not be serialized. The new analyzer now appends them as trailing constant arguments when it resolves `grouping`, and registered `groupingFor*` resolvers rebuild the function from them, so a serialized plan carries the function by name and arguments alone. The old analyzer keeps constructing the functions directly; such plans are not serialized. - `GROUPING SETS` aggregation uses the partial-aggregation split, the same one the shard-based distributed path uses. `WITH TOTALS` and extremes remain unsupported. The distributed results of all new stateless tests are verified against non-distributed execution of the same queries. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Support `ROLLUP`, `CUBE`, `GROUPING SETS` and the `grouping` function in queries executed with `make_distributed_plan = 1`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114950&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114950](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114950+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix `rows_before_limit_at_least` under parallel replicas local plan (#113279)
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113279 ### Change log category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Change log entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `rows_before_limit_at_least` returning 0 when querying with LIMIT under parallel replicas local plan (`parallel_replicas_local_plan = 1`). ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is not required for this bug fix --- ### Detailed Description #### Problem With parallel replicas enabled (`parallel_replicas_local_plan = 1`), queries with a `LIMIT` incorrectly returned `rows_before_limit_at_least = 0` even when `exact_rows_before_limit = 1`. #### Root Cause In `createLocalPlanForParallelReplicas` (`src/Processors/QueryPlan/ParallelReplicasLocalPlan.cpp`), `select_query_options.is_local_shard_plan` was previously only initialized to true when `processed_stage == QueryProcessingStage::WithMergeableStateAfterAggregationAndLimit`. For queries planned at `QueryProcessingStage::WithMergeableState`, `is_local_shard_plan` evaluated to false. Consequently, `addPreliminaryLimitStep` in `src/Planner/Planner.cpp` did not invoke `limit->markAsShardLimit()`, causing `initRowsBeforeLimit` in `src/QueryPipeline/QueryPipeline.cpp` to treat the preliminary limit as a top-level query accounting boundary and terminate processor traversal without attaching the rows-before-limit counter to the local input stream. #### Solution Set `select_query_options.is_local_shard_plan` to true for both `QueryProcessingStage::WithMergeableState` and `QueryProcessingStage::WithMergeableStateAfterAggregationAndLimit`. This marks the preliminary limit on the local replica branch as a shard limit, enabling `initRowsBeforeLimit` to traverse through it and attach the statistics counter to the local input stream matching remote replica behavior. #### Test Plan - Added `tests/queries/0_stateless/02590_parallel_replicas_local_plan_rows_before_limit.sh` and reference test asserting correct `rows_before_limit_at_least` row count under `parallel_replicas_local_plan = 1`.

signals.title: Codex tries to learn from its mistakes
signals.text: The unattended PR continuation workflow made two kinds of unsafe decisions. It incorrectly closed PR #114849 after confusing commit visibility with containment by the current `master`, and it force-pushed PR #111032 from a malformed single-parent commit that changed 673 files and deleted 26,457 lines. Require an explicit base-branch ancestry check and a separate current-state check so reverted changes are not considered integrated. Before committing or pushing, the workflow must inspect the staged and complete PR diffs, preserve the existing remote head as an ancestor, and stop on unexplained scope changes. A `pre-push` hook now enforces fast-forward-only updates and rejects branch deletion even if an agent attempts a force-push. An audit of recent automation activity found eight account-level force-pushes since 2026-08-13. PR #111032 was the only malformed large-diff outlier; the other seven replacement heads changed 2–8 files. The audit also found a smaller scope failure in PR #104495, where conflict resolution accidentally staged three unrelated untracked test files. The new explicit-path staging rule and staged-diff inspection cover that failure mode. The safety hook was tested in a throwaway repository: normal fast-forward updates were accepted, while non-fast-forward updates, branch deletion, and the exact PR #111032 rewrite were rejected. Shell syntax and ShellCheck validation also pass. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114849 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111032 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104495 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Not for changelog.

signals.title: Report the real error when an in-place `IN`-set build destroys its source
signals.text: `FutureSetFromSubquery::buildOrderedSetInplace` speculatively builds the set of an `IN` subquery during index analysis. A subquery whose source plan cannot be cloned - a read from a remote cluster, for example - takes the destructive path there, which consumes the source plan. When that build then throws, the set can never be built again: `build` returns a null plan, every caller takes that for "nothing left to build", and the query keeps running with an unready set until `FunctionIn` reports the logical error `Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'in'`. That is exactly what happens whenever a caller deliberately ignores an in-place build failure. Statistics-based part pruning is such a caller: it logs the failure and keeps reading the part whose condition it could not evaluate. So ```sql SELECT count() FROM t WHERE a IN (SELECT a FROM clusterAllReplicas('cluster_with_an_unavailable_replica', currentDatabase(), t)) ``` reported `Not-ready Set` instead of the connection error, which aborts the server in a build with `abort_on_logical_error`. The failure of a destructive in-place build is remembered now and rethrown from `build` instead of returning a null plan, so the query fails with the real reason - the same error it fails with when no in-place build is attempted at all. This is the cause of the recurring master `Stress test` failure `Logical error: Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'A (STID: 0250-3e49)`, seen on `arm_release` and `arm_msan` a few times a day since 2026-07-23: CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=2926be24e6102daae60b8f44c88969495a76ec3c&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_release%29 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107924 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107619 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix the logical error `Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'in'` for a query with an `IN` subquery reading from a remote cluster: the query now fails with the actual error from the subquery, such as a connection failure.

signals.title: Reuse LowCardinality aggregation mappings across blocks
signals.text: Previously dictionary position to aggregate state mappings were only valid within a block. For parts where there's only a single dictionary, this is too restrictive and resulted in repeated work. This moves the mapping cache to the aggregation method, matching its lifetime to the aggregation hash table. We keep the successful mappings while the dict remains unchanged. Non-shared dictionaries remain block local. This gives a very nice speedup to the benchmark in the previous commit: | Width | LC before | LC after | Change | |-----------------|----------:|----------:|-------:| | `UInt8` | 0.1220 s | 0.1158 s | -5.1% | | `UInt16` | 0.1703 s | 0.1395 s | -18.1% | | `UInt32` | 0.1884 s | 0.1489 s | -20.9% | | `UInt64` | 0.1952 s | 0.1513 s | -22.5% | | `UInt128` | 0.5676 s | 0.5649 s | -0.5% | | `UInt256` | 0.9354 s | 0.9206 s | -1.6% | | `String` (6 B) | 0.2535 s | 0.1598 s | -37.0% | | `String` (26 B) | 0.2521 s | 0.1630 s | -35.4% | | `String` (56 B) | 0.2689 s | 0.1655 s | -38.5% | The improvements for UInt128 and UInt256 will be there after #114982 is merged. The benefit is largest when many blocks share the same dictionary, because dictionary-position mappings are reused across those blocks. _AI assisted, scratching an itch I've had for a while._ ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Improve aggregation performance by reusing LowCardinality aggregation mappings across blocks. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114993&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114993](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114993+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Support `Merge` tables with plan-based parallel replicas
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/67770 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110972 Lets a `Merge` table be read with parallel replicas, implemented on top of the plan-based parallel replicas (`parallel_replicas_plan_based`). `ReadFromMerge` is opaque to the parallel-replicas plan transformation: it unites the pipelines of its per-table subplans instead of their plans, so the underlying `MergeTree` reads do not exist yet while the plan is transformed. An eligible `ReadFromMerge` is therefore expanded into a plan-level `UnionStep` over those child reads, right before the reads to distribute are collected. A `Merge` then has exactly the shape the transformation already distributes - a union of `MergeTree` reads - so the reads are coordinated across the replicas, and the steps above the `Merge` (aggregation, joins) are distributed as well, without any `Merge`-specific code in the coordinator, in the serialization or in the local plan. The expansion is off by default, gated by the new setting `parallel_replicas_allow_merge_tables`, and takes effect only together with `parallel_replicas_plan_based`. A `Merge` is read by a single replica when one of its children is not a plain `MergeTree` read, when the read is `FINAL`, or when no table matches its regexp. This is an alternative to https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110972, which implements the same feature on the legacy (query-tree-based) path. There, the query text is reshipped and every replica re-analyzes it, which needs a fail-close handshake (`parallel_replicas_designated_table`, `_freshness_checked_tables`, `_merge_child_tables`) to guard against the set of underlying tables differing across replicas or changing between planning and reading. The plan-based path ships a serialized plan fragment with the tables already resolved, so none of that is needed. Tests: three new stateless tests - the core feature and its negative cases (`04907`), the query shapes a `Merge` can be read with, including the `merge` table function, a filter on the `_table` virtual column and reading in order with a limit (`04908`), and `Merge` tables inside JOINs on either side of the join (`04909`). Each of them checks the results against non-parallel execution and asserts through the plan how the query was distributed. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A `Merge` table can now be read with parallel replicas: the reads from the underlying `MergeTree` tables are coordinated across the replicas, and the aggregations and joins above them are distributed too. Enabled by the new setting `parallel_replicas_allow_merge_tables`, which takes effect together with `parallel_replicas_plan_based`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115001&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115001](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115001+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not alias pre-aggregation states of a zero-size aggregate in arrayReduceInRanges
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108781 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108781 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `arrayReduceInRanges` over an array whose elements are all NULL aborts a debug or sanitizer build with `Logical error: 'IAggregateFunction::merge called with the same source and destination state'`: ```sql SELECT arrayReduceInRanges('groupArray', [(1, 64)], arrayMap(x -> (x + NULL), range(64))); ``` Found by the AST fuzzer: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114747&sha=95a67283e1b33c000dba21cddefcd4418c4a2c94&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29 An all-NULL argument collapses the aggregate to `AggregateFunctionNothing`, whose `sizeOfData()` is 0. `Arena::alignedAlloc` advances the arena by `size`, so every zero-byte allocation returns the same address. The function allocates one pre-aggregation state per 64 rows plus one state per range from a single arena, so all of those states alias and both the pairwise level merge and the per-range merge become `merge(p, p)`. The fix allocates `max(sizeOfData(), 1)` bytes for the pre-aggregation states, so they are distinct and every merge still runs. The per-range state needs no padding: that merge only runs when the range spans a whole 64-row block, which is also the condition for a pre-aggregation state to exist, and its one-byte allocation has already advanced the arena. For an aggregate with a non-empty state the allocation is byte-identical to before. I deliberately did not suppress the merge for zero-size states. `sizeOfData() == 0` does not imply that merging is a no-op: `StatelessWindowFunction` is also zero-size and its `mergeImpl` throws. Since the aggregate is caller-supplied, a genuinely empty state cannot be told apart from one whose merge enforces a contract, so skipping the call could drop that enforcement. Two further places with the same allocation pattern are left alone. `ColumnAggregateFunction` can hold zero-size states (the test builds one via `nothingState`) but its `insertMergeFrom` merges across two different arenas. The `Aggregator` merge paths have one reported sighting of the sibling assertion (`mergeAndDestroyBatch`, on #111459) that 15 probes did not reproduce. Release behaviour is unchanged - the assertion compiles out and `Nothing::mergeImpl` is empty.

signals.title: Perf: bulk insert repeated LowCardinality values
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Avoid repeated dictionary work when inserting the same LowCardinality value many times. ## Summary - Add `ColumnLowCardinality::insertManyFrom`. - Read the source dictionary index once. - Translate the value once when dictionaries differ. - Append repeated indexes with `ColumnIndex::insertManyIndexes`. ## Why - The generic `IColumn::insertManyFrom` path calls `insertFrom` once per output row. - For LowCardinality, that repeats the same dictionary lookup and translation. - This keeps the existing result and moves invariant work out of the loop. ## Correctness - `length == 0` remains a no-op. - Shared and separate dictionaries use separate paths. - Tests cover repeated values and index widening from `UInt8` to `UInt16`. - `ColumnIndex::insertManyIndexes` keeps the existing index-widening behavior. ## Benchmark The same binary compares the new bulk path with the old scalar `insertFrom` loop. - `LowCardinality(String)` and `LowCardinality(UInt64)` - Shared and separate dictionaries - Fanouts: `1`, `2`, `4`, `8`, `16`, `64`, `256`, `65536` - Source setup and destination allocation are outside the timed section Run: ```bash ./build/programs/column_insert_many_from \ --benchmark_filter='(BM_insertManyFromLowCardinality|BM_insertFromRepeatedlyLowCardinality)' ``` ## Measured result AArch64 benchmark build, 5-run median CPU time: - Fanout 256: **7.2x–7.9x faster** across `String`/`UInt64` and shared/separate dictionaries. - Fanout 65,536: **324x–634x faster**. - Fanout 1: no meaningful gain, since only one value is inserted.

signals.title: Clean reusable continue-all-prs worktrees
signals.text: Clean reusable worker worktrees before every PR assignment, discarding tracked, untracked, and ignored changes while retaining root-level `build*` directories for incremental rebuilds. When free disk space falls below 100 GiB, remove the oldest managed `tmp` and `build*` directories first, followed by stale managed worktrees if necessary. Cleanup is restricted to registered worktrees under the configured worker base, protects active worker roots, and stops a worker after a cleanup failure. Root-owned files left by containerized integration tests are removed by retrying the same path-scoped cleanup through non-interactive `sudo`; if cleanup still fails, the orchestrator exits instead of repeating the failure in later rounds. A live run reclaimed 47 GiB (95 GiB to 142 GiB free) while preserving all four reusable worker roots. It also verified immediate Ctrl+C termination during cleanup. ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Not for changelog. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115031&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115031](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115031+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Read all summed columns for SELECT FINAL from SummingMergeTree
signals.text: `SELECT ... FINAL` from a `SummingMergeTree` table returned wrong results when the query read only a subset of the columns of the summation. A merge removes a row when the values in **all** of the columns of the summation are zero after summing. The FINAL read applied the same rule, but only over the columns the query happened to read. Two ways to misbehave follow from that: - A query reading a subset of the summed columns removed every group whose visible columns summed to zero, even though an unread summed column made the row survive a real merge — rows silently disappeared. The most common victim is bare `count()`, which reads a single smallest column (plus the internally added sorting key): on a table `(c0 Int8, c1 Int32, c3 UInt64) ENGINE = SummingMergeTree ORDER BY c3` with two overlapping parts where `c0` sums to zero for some keys, `SELECT count() FROM t FINAL` returned 10 instead of 15, and `SELECT c0, c3 FROM t FINAL` lost the same 5 rows. - A query reading none of the summed columns (e.g. only the sorting key) never removed anything, keeping rows that a real merge deletes. The fix always includes all columns that a merge would aggregate into the FINAL read set (and into the set protected from plan-level column pruning), so the removal decision is taken over the same set of columns as in a real merge. This makes `SELECT ... FINAL` agree with `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL` followed by a plain `SELECT`. Note that queries over `SummingMergeTree FINAL` that previously read a subset of the summed columns now read all of them, which is the price of the correct result. Found by the nightly SQLancer `FinalMerge` oracle (`SELECT count() FROM t0 FINAL` returned 9947 before `OPTIMIZE TABLE t0 FINAL` and 9999 after it on the same data): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=5c9f28ed5a2c585ad46bf74d6600cdcf3aa07a9e&name_0=NightlySQLancer&name_1=SQLancer%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%29&name_1=SQLancer ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix wrong results of `SELECT ... FINAL` from `SummingMergeTree` when the query reads only a subset of the columns of the summation: the decision to remove a row whose sums are all zero is now taken over all columns of the summation, as in a real merge, instead of only the columns the query reads. Previously, rows could silently disappear from the result (for example, `SELECT count() FROM table FINAL`). ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)
