signals.title: Add stateless and fuzzer jobs to the WeeklyCFI workflow
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/100419 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112152 The `amd_cfi` build is the only test build with ThinLTO enabled — the same compile profile as official release builds — so besides CFI violations the WeeklyCFI workflow also catches ThinLTO-only behavior differences that no other CI job can see. The latest example is the `__functional` frame-name suppression surfaced by `test_crash_log` in the weekly runs of 2026-07-20 through 2026-08-10 and fixed in #112152. This PR broadens the workflow's coverage: - **Stateless tests** (parallel + sequential lanes, mirroring `amd_debug`). `clickhouse-test` now detects the CFI build from `-fsanitize=cfi` in the `CXX_FLAGS` row of `system.build_options`, so tests that cannot pass in this build profile can carry a `no-cfi` tag (the same generic `no-<flag>` skip mechanism the sanitizer builds use). CFI is deliberately not treated as a sanitizer: it has near-zero runtime overhead, so tests tagged `no-sanitizers` still run under CFI. - **AST fuzzer and BuzzHouse**: fuzzers assert only on crashes, never on exact query output, so the build profile cannot produce false positives there, and fuzzing reaches virtual-call combinations the curated suites never exercise. The fuzzer job configs are shared out into `_common_ast_fuzzer_job_config` / `_common_buzz_fuzzer_job_config`; master and PR workflows are unchanged. Not added, and why: unit tests (`ENABLE_CFI` is incompatible with `ENABLE_TESTS` — ThinLTO is disabled when building tests), performance comparison (it compares against the non-CFI master-head binary, so results are uninterpretable), upgrade/compatibility checks (version and data compatibility are orthogonal to CFI instrumentation), Keeper Jepsen (requires the standalone `clickhouse-keeper` build, which the CFI build omits). **Validation (complete):** the workflow was temporarily switched to a `pull_request` trigger (same approach as #100419) and all ten `amd_cfi` jobs passed on `baf56e50335` — stateless parallel + sequential, integration 4/4, stress, AST fuzzer, and BuzzHouse ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115036&sha=baf56e50335c45adf2afb691d0a1ef72f49c8bc6&name_0=WeeklyCFI)). The schedule-only trigger is restored in the final commit. The first run surfaced two findings, both filed: a probabilistic server crash in gRPC response compression (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115121) and empty `symbols`/`lines` in `system.trace_log` under this build profile (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115122, the two `03150` tests carry `no-cfi` tags pointing at it). Workflow: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/workflows/weekly_cfi.yml ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: Offer the `/`-commands of the client, and name them when misspelled
signals.text: Typing `/` at the beginning of the input now shows the client's own commands (`/clear`, `/help`, `/man`) as as-you-type hints, and typing more of a name narrows the list down. `Tab` completes the command being typed, which is also how they are completed when the instant hints are disabled (`--hints 0`, `--highlight 0`, `--disable_suggestion`). Until now these commands could only be found in the documentation; now the prompt itself lists them. A mistake in the name of a command is reported as such, with the commands it may have meant, instead of being parsed as SQL and reported as a syntax error at the `/`: ``` :) /hepl Exception on client: Code: 36. DB::Exception: Unknown command `/hepl`. Maybe you meant: ['/help']. Type `/` at the beginning of the line to see all the commands. (BAD_ARGUMENTS) ``` An argument given to a command that takes none (`/clear now`) is reported the same way. Batch `clickhouse-client` still parses such input as the SQL it is, exactly like it already does for `help` and `clear`; `clickhouse-local` reports it like the interactive client. The commands come from a single list, `clientSlashCommands`, shared by the hints, the completion and the diagnostics. An offered command replaces the whole typed prefix including the `/`, which `replxx` counts as a word break character and would otherwise leave in place. The offer is off for `keeper-client` and `clickhouse-disks`: they reuse the same line reader, and a leading `/` is the beginning of a path there. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114043 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The `/`-commands of the client (`/help`, `/man`, `/clear`) are now offered by the line editor: typing `/` at the beginning of the input lists them as hints, and `Tab` completes the command being typed. A mistake in the name of a command is reported with the similar commands suggested, instead of being parsed as SQL. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115039&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115039](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115039+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Bucket `timeSeries*ToGrid` samples in runs
signals.text: Based on #114889 — the new changes are the last four commits. The add path of `timeSeries*ToGrid` paid the bucket-index math and a hash-map lookup per sample. Samples arrive sorted by timestamp within a series and a bucket covers many scrape intervals, so the batch add path now works in runs: `classifySampleFast` returns the `(lo, hi]` timestamp range sharing the sample's fate (the bucket's time range, or a range of rejected timestamps — e.g. the whole gap between buckets when `window < step`), a vectorizable scan finds the run of consecutive in-range samples, and the run is appended to the bucket in bulk. One classification, one lookup, one append per run; two comparisons and a store per sample; unsorted input degenerates to the old per-sample cost. `addBatch` is also overridden to split batches into runs of the same aggregation state, hoisting the per-row `typeid_cast`s. The kernel is additionally compiled for x86-64-v4 with runtime dispatch; end-to-end neutral on the AVX2 baseline (the loops are bandwidth-bound), kept as future-proofing. Bit-identical to master on a differential test over all 12 functions: all window/step shapes, `DateTime`/`DateTime64`, `Float32/64`, NaN, duplicate/unsorted timestamps, `Nullable`, `-If`, arrays, two-level/external aggregation, `-State`/`-Merge`, extreme parameters (which keep the `Int128` path). On top of #114889 (100M rows, 1000 series, 16 threads, min of 7): rate 1.18x, rate with `window < step` 1.29x, instant rate 1.24x, deriv 1.24x, changes 1.15x; unsorted and finalize-heavy unchanged. Single-threaded (add path isolated): 1.26-2.09x. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): Process samples of the `timeSeries*ToGrid` aggregate functions in runs of consecutive samples falling into one grid bucket, speeding up the sample-ingestion stage of `timeSeriesRateToGrid` and related functions by 1.2-2x on sorted time series data.
signals.author: nikitamikhaylov

signals.title: Enable CORS in clickhouse-local by default
signals.text: `clickhouse-local` can serve HTTP after `SYSTEM START LISTEN HTTP`, but it normally runs without a config file, so it had no `http_options_response` section and answered the CORS preflight with a bare `204` carrying no `Access-Control-*` headers. A browser therefore refuses every cross-origin request to it - including the Web UI opened from a `file://` URL, whose origin is `null`. Now `clickhouse-local` sets the same default `http_options_response` headers that the `clickhouse-server` configuration ships (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and friends). A configuration file with its own `http_options_response` section still replaces them entirely, and the headers are sent only for requests that carry an `Origin`, exactly as in `clickhouse-server`. Note the implication, which is now documented next to the existing security warning for the listeners: while an HTTP listener is open, any web page you visit can query the local instance over the loopback address and read the results. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `clickhouse-local` now answers CORS preflight requests with the same permissive headers as `clickhouse-server`, so the HTTP interface opened by `SYSTEM START LISTEN HTTP` can be used from a browser out of the box, including the Web UI opened from a `file://` URL. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1522` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Perf: Reuse consecutive HashJoin probe results for fixed-width keys
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Reduce HashJoin probe overhead by reusing lookup results for repeated fixed-width join keys. ### What does this PR do? - Adds a **probe-only** consecutive-key cache for fixed-width HashJoin getters. - Reuses the previous **mapped pointer and hash-table offset** when the next probe key has the same raw bytes. - Keeps build-side insertion on the existing path. - Preserves duplicate right-side row handling through RowRef and RowRefList. - Covers **key32/key64**, packed keys32/64/128/256, and the corresponding two-level variants. - Leaves key8/key16, strings, nullable keys, range joins, and the build path unchanged. - Adds ALL INNER, RIGHT, and FULL correctness coverage. - Covers duplicate and unmatched rows. - Adds packed **keys256** correctness coverage with repeated probe keys. - Adds a run-length sweep, large build-map coverage, and packed keys128/keys256 benchmark cases. ### Why? - **Current path:** calculates the probe key and probes the hash table for every left-side row. - **Typical input:** primary-key ordered or clustered data often has long runs of the same join key. - **Repeated work:** the old path repeats the same key calculation and hash-table lookup for every row in a run. - **New path:** the first row does the normal lookup; later equal-key rows reuse its result. - **Unclustered input:** different keys still use the normal lookup path. - **Safety:** the generic consecutive-key cache is not used because HashJoin needs the real hash-table offset. - **Mapped values:** the cache stores the pointer from the real hash-table cell instead of copying RowRefList. - **Join behavior:** matched rows, duplicate right-side rows, and RIGHT/FULL join flags stay unchanged. ### Performance - **Clustered input:** avoids repeated key calculation and hash-table lookup for equal-key runs. - **Interleaved input:** adds only the key-equality check before the normal lookup. - **Expected benefit:** grows with the number of repeated rows per key. - **Regression control:** run length 1 and interleaved cases measure the no-hit cost. ### Benchmark - **Fixture:** `hashjoin_consecutive_keys`. - **Probe input:** 20M rows per measured query. - **Run lengths:** 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 64, and 10,000 rows per key. - **Small build map:** 2,000 keys. - **Large build map:** 2,000,000 keys. - **Packed keys:** clustered and interleaved cases for keys128 and keys256. - **Join settings:** hash algorithm with table swapping disabled. ### Benchmark results - **CI:** [AMD release performance comparison](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/PRs/115046/843550ba1e290f6f1a34058fb041055c034aa3cc/performance_comparison_amd_release_master_head_4_6/all-queries.html), master vs this PR. - **Input:** 20M probe rows per query. - **Unit:** seconds, lower is better. | Case | Master | PR | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Run length 1 | 0.089 | 0.141 | +58.0% | | Run length 2 | 0.086 | 0.123 | +41.9% | | Run length 4 | 0.086 | 0.115 | +33.6% | | Run length 8 | 0.086 | 0.111 | +28.0% | | Run length 16 | 0.088 | 0.110 | +25.6% | | Run length 64 | 0.087 | 0.112 | +27.9% | | Run length 10,000 | 0.087 | 0.108 | +24.9% | | Large UInt64 map, unclustered | 0.324 | 0.366 | +12.7% | | keys128, unclustered | 0.172 | 0.253 | +47.5% | | keys256, unclustered | 0.367 | 0.397 | +8.0% | - **Note:** This shard includes the run-length sweep and unclustered controls. The clustered large-map and packed-key cases were not recorded in this report.

signals.title: Perf: Coalesce contiguous unmatched ranges in MergeJoin
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/12118 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Avoid materializing a temporary filtered column for dense unmatched ranges in partial_merge RIGHT and FULL JOINs. ### What does this PR do? - Finds unmatched ranges once and keeps their start and length. - Appends dense unmatched ranges directly with insertRangeFrom. - Uses the existing filtered-column path when unmatched rows are too fragmented. - Reuses the range storage between output blocks. - Keeps the existing whole-block path when no right rows were matched. - Adds RIGHT and FULL correctness coverage with nullable and string right columns. - Adds dense and interleaved RIGHT cases to the partial_merge_join performance fixture. ### Why? - The old path calls filter for every right column. - Direct range insertion avoids temporary filtered columns for dense runs. - The range list avoids scanning the same mask again in the direct path. - One insertRangeFrom per range is not good for fragmented masks. - The fallback keeps fragmented cases on the existing path. - The result and row order stay unchanged. ### Performance - Dense unmatched runs use bulk range insertion. - Fragmented masks use the filtered-column path. - The benchmark now materializes right-side UInt64, String, and LowCardinality(String) columns in the outer join cases. - The interleaved case consumes the LowCardinality payload with sum(length(b.label)). - The fixture covers sparse, dense, and interleaved RIGHT and FULL JOIN shapes. ### Benchmark The completed CI comparison for commit 3b5eb1a was against master commit 0fc2db3. These are client_time values in seconds per query from the performance dashboard. The table shows the three new join shapes from that run. | Case | AMD before | AMD after | ARM before | ARM after | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Interleaved ALL RIGHT | 0.0860s | 0.0902s (+4.9%) | 0.0743s | 0.0766s (+3.1%) | | Dense ALL RIGHT | 0.0075s | 0.0079s (+5.3%) | 0.0058s | 0.0056s (-3.4%) | | Dense ALL FULL | 0.0080s | 0.0078s (-2.5%) | 0.0061s | 0.0061s (0.0%) | ### Crossover sweep A local sweep was run with partial_merge, a 1,000,000-row dense right table, and a LowCardinality(String) payload. The query consumes all right-side payload columns. | Average unmatched run | Elapsed | | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 0.928s | | 2 | 0.616s | | 4 | 0.387s | | 8 | 0.232s | | 16 | 0.143s | | 32 | 0.099s | The current cutoff is 8 rows per unmatched range. The 8, 16, and 32 row cases use the direct range path and continue to improve in this sweep. Fixture: partial_merge_join. - Interleaved case: pmj_u64_mult2 ALL RIGHT JOIN pmj_u64_mult3. - Dense cases: pmj_u64_sparse_right ALL RIGHT or ALL FULL JOIN test_u64_right_1000000. - Data: 10,000 sparse left keys and 1,000,000 dense right keys, plus multiples-of-2 and multiples-of-3 tables. - The right tables include payload UInt64, text String, and label LowCardinality(String). The queries aggregate count(), sum(b.k), sum(b.payload), sum(length(b.text)), and sum(length(b.label)). A follow-up run for commit 5da87de was started after the range reuse and fixture updates. It did not reach the performance jobs because Build (arm_tidy) failed in an untouched TableJoin test, so the performance jobs were skipped. Fast test and style check passed.

signals.title: Tag functional tests averaging over 60s under MSan with `no-msan`
signals.text: MSan stateless jobs are the slowest functional-test jobs in CI and sit right at the edge of the 9000 s job timeout. In a recent run the private `Stateless tests (amd_msan, distributed cache, meta in keeper, s3 storage, sequential, 2/2)` job spent 8324 s of its 9000 s budget on tests and was then killed during teardown, even though all 526 tests had passed. MSan is ~5.8× slower than release on the same tests, and the cost is concentrated in a long tail: under MSan, 8 tests take over 180 s each, and the 30 slowest account for ~48% of a sequential shard's runtime. This tags every functional test whose mean duration under MSan exceeds 60 s with `no-msan`, except two tests that would otherwise lose all sanitizer coverage. ### How the set was chosen From `play.clickhouse.com`, over the public MSan stateless checks (`Stateless tests (amd_msan, WasmEdge, parallel, N/M)` and `Stateless tests (amd_msan, WasmEdge, sequential, N/2)`, excluding the flaky-check and selected-tests flavors): ```sql SELECT test_name, count() AS runs, avg(test_duration_ms)/1000 AS avg_s FROM checks WHERE check_name LIKE 'Stateless tests (amd_msan, WasmEdge, %' AND check_name NOT LIKE '%flaky%' AND check_name NOT LIKE '%selected%' AND test_status = 'OK' AND check_start_time >= now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY GROUP BY test_name HAVING runs >= 20 AND avg_s > 60 ORDER BY avg_s DESC ``` 351 tests matched. 30 of them no longer exist in `master` (reverted, split into smaller tests, or removed), leaving 321. One of those, `04062_text_index_json_all_values_ghdata`, already carried `no-msan`; two more remain under MSan to retain their only sanitizer coverage, so 318 files change here. Only `OK` runs are counted, so timeouts and failures do not inflate the averages. ### Initial expected effect The following estimates were calculated before retaining the two sanitizer-coverage tests. | Flavor | MSan test time per commit | Removed | Share | |---|---|---|---| | parallel | 129025 s | 24766 s | 19.2% | | sequential | 11236 s | 4108 s | 36.6% | ### 25 slowest of the tagged tests | Test | Mean under MSan | Runs | |---|---|---| | `03988_cached_read_big_at` | 384.6 s | 9014 | | `03008_deduplication_insert_several_blocks_replicated` | 337.2 s | 9116 | | `03008_deduplication_several_mv_into_one_table_nonreplicated` | 308.8 s | 9118 | | `03008_deduplication_insert_several_blocks_nonreplicated` | 282.6 s | 9118 | | `04039_merge_tree_snapshot_teardown_race` | 275.2 s | 9347 | | `01195_formats_diagnostic_info` | 234.6 s | 9278 | | `02475_bson_each_row_format` | 206.1 s | 9264 | | `00626_replace_partition_from_table_zookeeper` | 202.5 s | 9323 | | `01019_alter_materialized_view_atomic` | 192.5 s | 9340 | | `04062_text_index_json_all_values_ghdata` | 190.4 s | 1806 | | `01721_join_implicit_cast_long` | 182.8 s | 9339 | | `00746_sql_fuzzy` | 180.5 s | 9340 | | `03755_large_primary_key_explain` | 180.2 s | 9337 | | `02943_variant_type_with_different_local_and_global_order` | 180.2 s | 9284 | | `02448_clone_replica_lost_part` | 177.4 s | 9263 | | `02372_analyzer_join` | 176.3 s | 9345 | | `04327_cluster_functions_huge_num_streams_no_crash` | 171.8 s | 9261 | | `01721_join_implicit_cast_long_oldanalyzer` | 168.9 s | 9346 | | `01079_bad_alters_zookeeper_long` | 166.8 s | 9322 | | `01747_system_session_log_long` | 165.9 s | 9014 | | `03208_array_of_json_read_subcolumns_1` | 165 s | 9339 | | `00429_long_http_bufferization` | 160.9 s | 9277 | | `04411_deep_nested_field_to_type` | 156.8 s | 9262 | | `01383_log_broken_table` | 156.4 s | 9340 | | `03326_protobuf_schemas_race` | 155.1 s | 9279 | (319 tests are tagged in total; the full list is the diff.) ### Trade-off A large share of these are the ZooKeeper, replication, mutation and race tests — precisely where MSan is most likely to find real uninitialized-memory bugs. They continue to run under ASan, UBSan and TSan, but this is a genuine reduction in MSan coverage rather than a pure win. An alternative that keeps the coverage is duration-aware sharding of the sequential jobs: the split is currently `crc32(test filename) % total_batches`, which gave one recent shard 8248 s against its sibling's 5514 s (1.50×), so balancing alone would have reclaimed ~23 min on the shard that timed out. ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115050&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115050](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115050+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Perf: Coalesce contiguous runs in ColumnFixedString filtering
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Bulk copy contiguous selected runs while filtering FixedString columns. ### What does this PR do? - Adds **contiguous-run copying** to the mixed-mask path in `ColumnFixedString::filter`. - Keeps the existing fast path for fully selected 64-row blocks. - Uses one resize and one bulk copy for each selected run in the out-of-place path. - Uses one `memmove` for each selected run in the in-place path. - Keeps isolated rows on the existing small-copy path. - Adds correctness coverage for clustered, dense-hole, empty, full, and boundary masks. - Adds out-of-place and in-place benchmark cases. ### Why? - **Current path:** copies every selected fixed string separately for a mixed 64-row mask. - **Dense masks:** one missing row can turn a large contiguous range into dozens of small copies. - **New path:** finds adjacent selected rows and copies each range at once. - **Fragmented masks:** keep the existing small-copy behavior. - **Result:** selected values and row order stay unchanged. ### How is it faster? - **Dense 64-row mask:** 63 selected rows with one hole become two contiguous ranges. - **Out-of-place path:** 63 row-sized resizes and small copies become two resizes and two bulk copies. - **In-place path:** 63 row-sized `memmove` calls become two range `memmove` calls. - **Longer runs:** amortize loop and copy overhead over more FixedString bytes. - **Random and alternating masks:** isolated rows stay on the existing path, so the optimization is focused on masks with useful runs. ### Performance - **Clustered masks:** fewer copy calls and fewer result-size updates. - **Dense masks with one hole:** large ranges are copied around the hole instead of row by row. - **Random and alternating masks:** provide regression-control cases with few useful runs. ### Benchmark - **Fixture:** `benchmark_column_fixed_string_filter`. - **Patterns:** clustered, random, alternating, and dense-with-hole. - **Paths:** out-of-place and in-place filtering. - **Column:** `FixedString(16)`. - **Rows:** 1,048,576. - **Status:** Fixture added. Local benchmark results, 5 repetitions per case: | Path | Pattern | Median | | --- | --- | ---: | | Out-of-place | Clustered | 0.501 ms | | Out-of-place | Random | 3.054 ms | | Out-of-place | Alternating | 1.373 ms | | Out-of-place | Dense with hole | 0.026 ms | | In-place | Clustered | 0.435 ms | | In-place | Random | 3.736 ms | | In-place | Alternating | 2.429 ms | | In-place | Dense with hole | 0.024 ms | <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115051&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115051](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115051+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Perf: Bulk copy selected runs in ColumnVector filtering
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Coalesce contiguous selected rows in the generic ColumnVector filter fallback. ### What does this PR do? - Adds **contiguous-run copying** to the generic mixed-mask fallback. - Keeps isolated rows on `insertSingle`. - Leaves the existing prefix, suffix, and AVX-512 paths unchanged. - Covers both out-of-place and in-place filtering through the shared inserter. - Adds correctness coverage for clustered, dense-hole, empty, full, and boundary masks. - Adds a benchmark for clustered, random, alternating, and dense-with-hole masks. ### Why? - **Current path:** copies every selected value separately for a mixed 64-row mask. - **Dense masks:** adjacent selected rows still take the per-value path. - **New path:** finds adjacent selected rows and copies each range at once. - **Fragmented masks:** keep the existing `insertSingle` behavior. - **Result:** selected values and row order stay unchanged. ### How is it faster? - **Dense 64-row mask:** 63 selected values with one hole become two contiguous ranges. - **Out-of-place path:** 63 `insertSingle` calls become two `insertRange` calls. - **In-place path:** 63 single-value moves become two range `memmove` calls. - **Longer runs:** reduce per-value inserter and loop overhead while copying more data per call. - **Single rows:** the adjacent-bit check keeps isolated selections on the existing cheap path. ### Performance - **Clustered masks:** fewer inserter calls for each selected run. - **Dense masks with one hole:** large ranges are copied around the hole instead of value by value. - **Random and alternating masks:** provide regression-control cases with few useful runs. ### Benchmark - **Fixture:** `benchmark_column_filter`. - **Patterns:** clustered, random, alternating, and dense-with-hole. - **Column:** generic `ColumnUInt128` path. - **Rows:** 1,048,576. - **Status:** Fixture added. Local benchmark results, 5 iterations per case: | Path | Pattern | Median | | --- | --- | ---: | | Out-of-place | Clustered | 0.378 ms | | Out-of-place | Random | 2.154 ms | | Out-of-place | Alternating | 1.231 ms | | Out-of-place | Dense with hole | 0.634 ms | | In-place | Clustered | 0.361 ms | | In-place | Random | 2.052 ms | | In-place | Alternating | 0.461 ms | | In-place | Dense with hole | 0.824 ms | <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115053&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115053](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115053+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Reject invalid event numbers and durations in sequenceMatch patterns
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed an `out_of_range` exception raised as an internal `Code: 1001` error when a `sequenceMatch`, `sequenceCount` or `sequenceMatchEvents` pattern contains the event number `0`, for example `sequenceMatch('(?0)')`. Such a pattern is now rejected with `BAD_ARGUMENTS`. A temporal condition holding a lone sign, such as `sequenceMatch('(?1)(?t>+)(?2)')`, was silently treated as `(?t>0)` and is now rejected with `SYNTAX_ERROR`. ### Description Event numbers are 1-based, but the bound check validated only the upper bound, so `(?0)` passed it. The conversion to a 0-based condition index then underflowed `UInt64` to `SIZE_MAX`, and `std::bitset<32>::set()` rejected that with `std::out_of_range`. Thrown from the aggregate function constructor during analysis, it surfaced as an internal `Code: 1001` error and aborted the server in debug and sanitizer builds. Two further inputs reached the same state: an event number overflowing `UInt64`, and a sign with no digits, `(?+)`. In each case `tryReadIntText` fails after consuming a byte while its pointer overload discards the boolean, so the existing "Could not parse number" check does not fire and the output keeps its initialiser `0`. Adding the missing lower bound validates the parsed value and covers all three at once, error code and message unchanged. The sibling temporal branch shared that parse-success defect and is fixed here too, after review automation raised it: `(?t>+)` was accepted as `(?t>0)`. The duration is now read through the `ReadBuffer` overload so the boolean is available, and rejected when it is false. The position check is kept, because `tryReadIntText` also succeeds while consuming nothing for a leading non-digit, which is what rejects `(?t>)`. Only the sign form leaked; `(?t>-)` and an overflowing duration were already rejected, and `(?t>+5)` still equals `(?t>5)`. All three functions share this parser and were affected; all are covered by new assertions in `00222_sequence_aggregate_function_family`, which fail on an unfixed binary. One imprecision is left as is: an overflowing event number is reported as event number `0`. Found by `AST fuzzer (amd_tsan)`, `bitset set argument out of range` (STID 2508-34fb): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115019&sha=7be817c59e288cab7aa329a76ed1ba65b9d555e9&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_tsan%29. Also seen on `Stress test (arm_tsan)`. Both carrier pull requests are bystanders; the defect reproduces on pristine master.

signals.title: A single test's timeout no longer aborts the whole clickhouse-test run
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/86768 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description **The problem.** `Fast test` on #86768 reported `Failed: 0, Passed: 73, Skipped: 23` yet failed with a synthetic `Server died` leaf. No core, no sanitizer report. [Report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=86768&sha=0927f057854f5e533b8ff833cf200e17db8005c5&name_0=PR&name_1=Fast%20test) | [job log](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/runs/31943974132/job/95177622132) **Root cause.** The server saturated rather than died, so all 24 workers hit the 126 s alarm at once. The first into `timeout_handler` called `stop_tests()`, which `killpg`s our *own* group, shared by every worker and the parent. One test's deadline thus SIGTERMed the whole run, exiting -15, which `ABORTED_RUN_EXIT_CODES` makes the job side relabel `Server died`. The `Code: 76` on `run_r0/status` and the `Code: 159` from `SYSTEM FLUSH LOGS` are downstream of it. **The change.** `timeout_handler` now kills only the timing-out test's own out-of-group clients, via a per-child loop extracted from `cleanup_child_processes`. That broadcast is unchanged, so the whole-run callers are unaffected, as the `--max-failures` paths document. A surviving worker must then report the test, which needs a result built and stamped. The alarm can land before either, so the recovery arm completes what is missing, and `SIGALRM` is blocked across stamping so it cannot run twice: a doubled description matches the leaf pattern too, reporting a nonexistent test. Fast test just has the shortest fuse. This does not fix the saturation. **Validation.** Not SQL-observable. The new `ci/tests/` test drives the real handler and `run_tests_array`, faking `killpg`/`pgrep`: own-group broadcasts 0, the test's own client still killed, `cleanup_child_processes` still broadcasting, one parseable leaf per alarm window. No wall clock. `ci/tests/` is 663/665, both failures pre-existing. **Residuals.** A timed-out test's database and temporary directory survive into the worker's next test, as when the alarm killed the worker outright. An alarm can also be swallowed by an unrelated broad `except Exception`, after which saturation reports `SERVER_DIED`, as master did on every per-test timeout. Both want a private signal type, a larger change. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115061&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115061](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115061+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Document that a MATERIALIZED column calculated from an EPHEMERAL column is not recalculated by a mutation
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114561 ## Problem Nothing documents what a mutation does to a `MATERIALIZED` column that is calculated from an `EPHEMERAL` column. The behaviour is a deliberate trade-off, but a user can only discover it by observing wrong-looking data: ```sql CREATE TABLE test (x Int32, e Int32 EPHEMERAL 0, m Int32 MATERIALIZED x + e) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); INSERT INTO test (x, e) VALUES (1, 7); -- m = 8 ALTER TABLE test UPDATE x = 2 WHERE 1; SELECT x, m FROM test; -- 2 8 <- not 2 + 7 ``` `m` keeps its `INSERT`-time value and from then on does not match its own expression, because `e` does not exist outside the `INSERT` that supplied it and cannot be read back to recalculate `m`. Where a user would look today: - **`ALTER TABLE ... UPDATE`** — does not mention `MATERIALIZED` or `EPHEMERAL` at all. Its only related statement is that updating a column used in the primary or partition key is unsupported. - **`MATERIALIZED`** — says values are "automatically calculated ... when rows are inserted", and says nothing about mutations. - **`EPHEMERAL`** — correctly says such columns are not stored, but does not draw out the consequence for mutations. The mutation does log a warning when it skips a column for this reason, which is accurate and actionable — but it appears only in the server log, at the moment it happens, and is not returned to the client. So the only documentation of this behaviour is an after-the-fact log line. ## Solution Add a `Materialized columns` section to the `ALTER TABLE ... UPDATE` page: a `MATERIALIZED` column whose expression reads an updated column is recalculated, and a sub-section on the `EPHEMERAL` case with the example above, the reason, and the existing advice to re-`INSERT` the affected rows. The example's output was verified verbatim against a local server. Only the English page is edited; localized pages are generated. Documentation only — no behaviour change, and independent of any pending fix in this area: it states what holds on `master` today and would still hold after https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114561. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Documentation (changelog entry is not required)

signals.title: Do not merge patch parts across the data version of an existing part
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/98898 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113998 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `Found patch part ... that intersects mutation with version ...` (`LOGICAL_ERROR`) on tables with lightweight updates. A merge of patch parts could produce a patch whose range of data versions spans the data version of an existing part; that patch can then be neither applied nor skipped, so every later operation on the partition failed and the replication queue stalled. Such merges are no longer assigned. ### Description A patch part is applied to a part either wholly or not at all: `patchHasHigherDataVersion` asserts that the patch's data versions are either all newer or all older than the data version of the part, and throws a `LOGICAL_ERROR` otherwise. Merging patch parts unions their ranges of data versions, so the merged range must not span the data version of any part in the original partition. The merge predicate took that boundary from `getCurrentMutationVersion`, that is from the mutations it still knows about. Those records are not durable, while the data version a mutation gave to the parts is: * `ReplicatedMergeTree` removes a mutation from `mutations_by_partition` when the cleanup thread drops the finished `/mutations` znode, and immediately on `KILL MUTATION`; * `MergeTree` removes it from `current_mutations_by_version` in `clearOldMutations`. Once the record is gone, every patch on either side of the boundary maps to the same version, the pair looks mergeable, and the merge produces a patch that spans a version the parts have already crossed. From then on `DETACH`/`DROP`/`MOVE`/`REPLACE PARTITION`, applying patches and building a mutations snapshot all fail on that partition, and debug and sanitizer builds abort. The fix takes the boundary from the data versions of the parts. For `ReplicatedMergeTree` they come from `virtual_parts`, which is `current_parts` + `queue`, so a version that only a queued `MUTATE_PART` has assigned is seen before that entry is executed — the pending-mutation case, which #113998 addresses from the queue side, is covered as well. The versions are collected only when the table has patch parts, so tables without lightweight updates pay nothing. No assertion is relaxed. The refused merge is never needed: the patch on the older side of the boundary is fully applied, so `clearUnusedPatchParts` drops it, and the patches on the newer side still merge with each other. This does not repair a patch that already spans a version on disk; such a table stays stuck until the patch is removed. The test is deterministic: it keeps the applied patch with `remove_unused_patch_parts = 0`, removes the finished mutation record with `KILL MUTATION`, and forces the merge with `OPTIMIZE ... PARTITION ID '<patch partition>' FINAL`. On master it aborts with the exact message; with the fix the merge is refused, the patches stay separate and the data is correct. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=0fc2db3239a1bd6dd6581f103473834687408b7d&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_tsan%29 The same `LOGICAL_ERROR` accounts for 23 stress-test failures across 8 distinct stacks and every build flavor between 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-16, the most frequent one being a merged patch part reported from `MergeTreeData::MutationsSnapshotBase`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115064&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115064](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115064+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not pop hints on a line displayed programmatically
signals.text: When a query is displayed at once rather than typed — recalled from the history with Up/Down/Ctrl-P/Ctrl-N, found by the incremental (Ctrl-T) or fuzzy (Ctrl-R) history search, pasted, brought back from the external editor, or preloaded — the as-you-type hints no longer appear at its end. With hints visible, the next Up/Down press would navigate the hints instead of the history, so navigating the history quickly was impossible. The hints are shown again as soon as the line is edited. The suppression is armed before the navigation action because replxx repaints (and regenerates the hints) inside `history_move` itself, and the displayed text is additionally pinned afterwards because replxx may throttle that repaint and replay it after the key handler returns (its "rapid refresh" of e.g. a held-down Up key). Verified with a new pty regression test (`04909_client_hints_history_navigation`, 4 cases), which fails on the previous binary in all three suppression cases; the existing `04402_clickhouse_client_autocomplete_inline_hints` (11 cases) and the hint-related expect tests still pass. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114043 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The command line client no longer shows the as-you-type hints on a query recalled from the history (or otherwise displayed at once, e.g. pasted), so pressing Up/Down continues to navigate the history instead of the hint list. The hints appear again as soon as the line is edited. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115065&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115065](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115065+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Support PostgreSQL regexp operators and make psql \d work over the PostgreSQL protocol
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/25757 Disclaimer: I do not like Postgres operators! I think they are ugly. It makes the language similar to Bash and Perl. They use operators instead of functions only because of some design drawbacks related to the index analysis. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Support PostgreSQL-style regular expression match operators: `~` (an alias for the `match` function), `~*` (case-insensitive match), `!~` and `!~*` (negations). The `\d`, `\dt`, `\dv` commands of `psql` now work when connected to ClickHouse over the PostgreSQL compatibility protocol, and a failed query no longer terminates the connection. --- `psql` could not run its `\d` command against ClickHouse over the PostgreSQL wire protocol: ``` alexey-milovidov=> \d ERROR: Query execution failed. DB::Exception: Exclamation mark can only occur in != operator: Syntax error: failed at position 665 (!) (line 10, col 21): !~ '^pg_toast' ... SSL connection has been closed unexpectedly The connection to the server was lost. Attempting reset: Succeeded. ``` This fixes every layer of that incompatibility: - The lexer and the expression parser now understand the PostgreSQL regular expression match operators `~`, `~*`, `!~`, `!~*`, desugaring to `match` and the new functions `matchCaseInsensitive`, `notMatch`, `notMatchCaseInsensitive` (trivial `MatchImpl` variants). The KQL dialect, which previously consumed its own `!~` operator as two error tokens, is adjusted to accept the new single token. - The PostgreSQL wire protocol handler removes the `pg_catalog.` schema qualifier from incoming queries at the token level, mapping references such as `pg_catalog.pg_class` onto the emulated per-session catalog views. - The emulated `pg_class` view now contains the actual tables of the current database (with `relname`, `relnamespace`, `relowner`, `relam`, `relkind`), `pg_namespace` contains the real databases, and a `pg_am` view is added (newer `psql` versions join it). The previous fixed rows are preserved for driver compatibility. - New compatibility functions `pgGetUserById` (alias `pg_get_userbyid`) and `pgTableIsVisible` (alias `pg_table_is_visible`) support the catalog query psql sends. - A failed query now keeps the connection alive: the server sends `ErrorResponse` and returns to the `ReadyForQuery` state, like PostgreSQL. The connection is still closed if some result bytes were already sent for the failed statement, since the output stream could be cut in the middle of a protocol message. The result: ``` psql (18.4, server 26.7.1.1) db_psql_test=> \d List of relations Schema | Name | Type | Owner --------------+-------------+-------+-------- db_psql_test | t_described | table | pguser db_psql_test | t_mt | table | pguser db_psql_test | v_described | view | pguser (3 rows) ``` Known limitation: `\d <name>` (describing a specific table) sends follow-up queries using `OPERATOR(pg_catalog.~)` syntax, `COLLATE pg_catalog.default` and `format_type`, which are not supported yet; the error is now reported without dropping the connection.

signals.title: Hand the connection to the built-in web UI pages over `postMessage`
signals.text: The built-in web UI pages — `/play`, `/docs`, `/dashboard`, `/schema`, `/merges`, `/jemalloc`, `/processors-profile`, `/binary` — take their connection from their own query string, which cannot carry a password: a URL ends up in browser history, `Referer` headers, server access logs and proxy logs. Only `/webterminal` could be handed credentials by the page embedding it, in a `postMessage` message. Every page now speaks that same exchange: ``` page -> host {type: 'clickhouse-hello'} host -> page {type: 'clickhouse-credentials', url, user, password} ``` The page announces itself as soon as it can apply a connection, and the host answers. The page has to speak first because a host that opened it with `window.open` cannot observe when a cross-origin document became ready, and an embedded page would otherwise race its host's `load` handler. Having adopted a connection, each page redoes what it had already loaded with the previous one, so the handover also works when it arrives after the page started querying: `/play` re-probes the credentials, `/docs` rebuilds its cross-link name cache and re-runs the displayed search, `/dashboard` and `/processors-profile` chain their reload behind the load already in flight (two concurrent loads would otherwise duplicate charts, or let a stale failure overwrite a good listing), `/schema` and `/jemalloc` reload, and `/binary` drops its cached tiles and redraws. ## Opening `/docs` from `/play` The Documentation icon in the `/play` sidebar is the first user of the handover. A plain click opens `/docs` through `window.open` — the anchor's `rel=noopener` would sever the handle — and hands the whole connection over, so the documentation search runs against the same server as the same user without the password appearing in a URL. A middle or modifier click keeps the browser's native new-tab handling, which carries `?user=` only, since such a window has no link back to `/play`. ## Security A reply is accepted only from the one window that opened or embeds the page, and only from an exact origin: the page's own, `https://console.clickhouse.cloud`, `https://console.clickhouse-staging.com` or `https://clickhouse.com`. The list is exact rather than a domain suffix on purpose — every ClickHouse Cloud service endpoint is a `*.clickhouse.cloud` host that serves content of its owner's choosing, and a trusted host can aim a page at a server of its own through `url`, which the user may then type credentials into believing it is still their own service. `webterminal.html` gated its own exchange on such a suffix and now uses the same exact list. `url` is optional and defaults to the server the page already points at, but the credentials are replaced wholesale: a message that names only a server cannot attach credentials it did not carry to it, which is what keeps a password filled in by the browser's password manager for this page's origin from following a `url` elsewhere. Outbound, credentials are always sent with an exact target origin, never `'*'`; the readiness announcement carries no secrets, only the fact that the page exists, which its host knows already. Verified in Chromium against a mock endpoint: the `/play` → `/docs` handover, the handover into an iframe for all eight pages, rejection of a handover from an untrusted origin and from a same-origin window that is not the page's host, the wholesale credential replacement, and the exactness of the origin list for all nine pages (`https://myserviceendpoint.clickhouse.cloud`, `https://evil.clickhouse.com`, `http://console.clickhouse.cloud` and `https://console.clickhouse.cloud.evil.com` are all rejected). The committed test asserts that every served page implements both halves of the exchange and that its origin list stayed exact. The protocol is documented in `docs/concepts/features/interfaces/web-ui-embedding.mdx`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The built-in web UI pages (`/play`, `/docs`, `/dashboard`, `/schema`, `/merges`, `/jemalloc`, `/processors-profile`, `/binary`) can now be handed their connection — server URL, user and password — in a `postMessage` message by the page that opened or embedded them, instead of taking it from their own query string, where a password would be recorded in browser history, referrer headers and access logs. `/play` uses this when opening `/docs`, so the documentation search connects to the same server as the same user. A page accepts a connection only from the window that opened or embeds it, and only from an exact list of trusted origins. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115067&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115067](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115067+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Answer text-index materialization from the index read task
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109595 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115037 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109595 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115037 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a text index query silently returning too few rows when a part carries a `skp_idx_<index>.idx` file that `checksums.txt` does not account for. The read path decided which columns to read from file existence while the index reader was assigned from checksum accounting, so the affected part contributed no matches. Both are now answered by the same predicate. ### Description ```sql CREATE TABLE t (k UInt64, s String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k; INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 'alpha'); ALTER TABLE t ADD INDEX tx s TYPE text(tokenizer = 'splitByNonAlpha') GRANULARITY 1; INSERT INTO t VALUES (2, 'alpha'); -- in all_1_1_0/: echo garbage > skp_idx_tx.idx DETACH TABLE t SYNC; ATTACH TABLE t; SELECT count() FROM t WHERE hasToken(s, 'alpha'); -- master: 1, expected 2 SELECT count() FROM t WHERE NOT hasToken(s, 'alpha'); -- master: 1, expected 0 ``` Default settings. The unaccounted file is the corrupted-part shape of #109595; its content is never decoded. Three read-path sites answer whether a text index is materialized in a part. `optimizeDirectReadFromTextIndex` and `getIndexReadTaskForReadStep` ask the index object via `getDeserializedFormat`, which requires the file to be accounted for and decodable. `hasMaterializedTextIndex` instead asked the part for a file on disk via `hasSecondaryIndex`, whose fallback is an unconditional `existsFile` with no accounting gate. An unaccounted file therefore reads as materialized only at that third site: `injectRequiredColumnsRecursively` takes its early return and never injects the base column, no index reader is created, and the virtual column's default expression is evaluated with its input missing. `getReadTaskColumns` already receives `index_read_tasks`, keyed by index name and carrying the index object the reader-assignment site uses. Threading the map through makes the two agree via a map lookup, with no index construction on the read path. `hasSecondaryIndex` is left alone: its mutation and merge callers want the file-existence answer. The reproducer needs one file write, so the test is an integration test (#111922 forbids fabricating part contents in a functional test). I found no pure-SQL carrier: `getDeserializedFormat`'s other two false routes are `isPartTypeCompatible`, where five SQL routes returned ground truth, and `isSystemColumnInvalidated`, which only covers `_block_number` / `_block_offset`, neither referenceable by a text index. The carrier test fails on master and passes with the fix. The `02346_text_index*` and `00990_hasToken*` families are unchanged.

signals.title: Add MergeTree settings `max_table_size_rows`, `max_table_size_bytes_compressed`, `max_table_size_bytes_uncompressed`
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115063 Adds three new `MergeTree`-level settings that limit the total size of a table, for multi-tenant, temporary, and demo services: - `max_table_size_rows` — the maximum total number of rows in active data parts; - `max_table_size_bytes_compressed` — the maximum total size on disk across all active and inactive data parts; - `max_table_size_bytes_uncompressed` — the same for uncompressed bytes. The limits are checked against the current table size at the beginning of `INSERT` and when new data parts are committed to the working set; on exceeding a limit, the query fails with the new `TABLE_SIZE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` error. Inserts done by materialized views (including refreshable ones) and async insert flushes are checked as well, since they go through the same sinks and part commits. The check also triggers on committing the results of background merges and mutations, so a mutation (e.g. an `UPDATE` increasing the table size) will be repeated without finishing while the table exceeds the limit, which is intended. The check is skipped on replicated fetches and on the execution of replication log entries that add data already accepted by another replica (`ATTACH_PART`, `REPLACE_RANGE`), which permits a race condition when parallel inserts into multiple replicas overdraft the limit. Committing empty data parts is always allowed, so the data can be removed from a table that exceeds the limits, e.g. with `TRUNCATE` or `ALTER TABLE ... DROP PARTITION`. The limit on the number of rows is counted only for active data parts, while the limits on the number of bytes are counted across all active and inactive data parts, because their purpose is to limit disk usage (inactive parts are removed in the background, so the observed size can decrease over time). ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add `MergeTree` settings `max_table_size_rows`, `max_table_size_bytes_compressed`, and `max_table_size_bytes_uncompressed` that limit the total size of a table. The limits are checked at the beginning of `INSERT` and when new data parts are committed (including the results of background merges and mutations), but not on replicated fetches. This closes [#115063](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115063). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115069&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115069](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115069+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Look up the SSH key and support ssh-agent in clickhouse-client
signals.text: `--ssh-key-file` can now be specified without a value. In that case the key is looked up the same way as `ssh` does it: - the identity files configured for this host in `~/.ssh/config` and in `/etc/ssh/ssh_config`; - the default identity files, such as `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`; - the keys held by the `ssh-agent`. A key held by the `ssh-agent` is preferred, because it does not need a passphrase. It is also used when `--ssh-key-file` names a key file that the agent holds - an encrypted key that was added with `ssh-add` no longer asks for the passphrase. Signing with the agent is implemented in `SSHAgent`, a small client of the agent protocol, which produces the same `SSHSIG` signature as `SSHKey::signString` does for a local key (for RSA keys it asks the agent for `rsa-sha2-256`, because agents sign with SHA-1 by default and the server rejects that). The client reports the key it has chosen: ``` $ clickhouse-client --user abcuser --ssh-key-file Using the SSH key 'the key of abcuser' from the ssh-agent. ``` Two related changes of the existing behavior: the passphrase is now asked only if the key file is really encrypted (before, `--ssh-key-file` always asked for it), and the message about a key that cannot be imported now names the file. Tests: a new stateless test `04908_ssh_key_file_lookup` covers the default identity file, an `ed25519` key from the `ssh-agent`, and an `ssh-rsa` key from the `ssh-agent` with an empty `~/.ssh`. The existing `test_ssh_keys_authentication` integration tests pass. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `clickhouse-client` accepts `--ssh-key-file` without a value: the key is looked up the same way as `ssh` does it - the identity files configured for the host in `~/.ssh/config`, the default identity files, such as `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, and the keys held by the `ssh-agent`. Authentication with a key held by the `ssh-agent` is now supported, and it does not need a passphrase. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115072&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115072](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115072+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Let the promql dialect keep tokens the SQL lexer rejects
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed PromQL queries with regex label matchers (`=~`, `!~`) being rejected under `--dialect promql`. Closes #115071. --- Under `--dialect promql`, `ParserPrometheusQuery` reads the raw query text and hands it to the PromQL grammar; it walks the SQL tokens only to find where the statement ends. But `tryParseQuery` scans those tokens for lexer errors *before* the parser runs, and `~` is not a SQL token, so the query was rejected before it ever reached the PromQL grammar: ``` $ clickhouse local --dialect promql -q 'up{instance="host1"}' Code: 471. ... The name of a TimeSeries table to use with promql dialect is not specified $ clickhouse local --dialect promql -q 'up{instance=~"host2|host3"}' Code: 62. ... Unrecognized token: Syntax error: failed at position 13 (~) ``` The equality matcher gets through to a missing-setting error; the regex matcher dies at the `~` with a **SQL** lexical error. It is not specific to `-q` — stdin and `--queries-file` fail identically. The grammar itself already has the tokens (`PromQLLexer.g4`: `RE : '=~'`, `NRE : '!~'`), and the same expression works when passed as a string to the table function, which is what makes the limitation easy to miss. `IParser` gains `consumesRawText()`, false by default and overridden by `ParserPrometheusQuery`. `tryParseQuery` skips its two lexical-error rejections for such parsers, since a token the SQL lexer does not recognise is not an error for a parser that reads the text itself. No call site changes, and any future dialect parser in the same position gets the behaviour by overriding one method. This is safe because the lexer does not stop at an unrecognised character — it consumes it and returns an `Error` token (`Lexer.cpp:546`), so statement-boundary detection still finds the terminating semicolon. Kusto solves the same problem with an entire parallel `parseKQLQuery.{h,cpp}`; PromQL needs only the boundary scan, so a virtual on `IParser` seemed proportionate. Happy to go the separate-entry-point route instead if maintainers prefer the consistency. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115073&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115073](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115073+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix gRPC and Arrow Flight listeners for wildcard listen hosts
signals.text: `gRPC` treats `::` and `0.0.0.0` as one family-agnostic wildcard: for either of them it binds a dual-stack `::` socket, and falls back to `0.0.0.0` only on a host without IPv6 (see `add_wildcard_addrs_to_server` in `contrib/grpc`). Listing both wildcard addresses in `listen_host` therefore made ClickHouse create two listeners that bind the very same socket address, and the second one either - failed with `EADDRINUSE`, because the Arrow Flight transport disables `SO_REUSEPORT`, and the exception terminated the whole server: ``` <Error> grpc: Failed to add port to server: No address added out of total 1 resolved for '0.0.0.0:9110' (Failed to add any wildcard listeners: Error in bind for address '[::]:9110': Address already in use Error in bind for address '0.0.0.0:9110': Address already in use) <Error> Application: Code: 1002. DB::Exception: Failed init Arrow Flight Server: Unknown error: Server did not start properly. ``` - or silently shared the port with the first one, because plain gRPC keeps `SO_REUSEPORT` enabled, so each of the two independent servers ended up serving a random half of the connections, and a listener configured for `0.0.0.0` accepted IPv6 connections as well: ``` <Information> Application: Listening for gRPC protocol: [::]:9100 <Information> Application: Listening for gRPC protocol: 0.0.0.0:9100 LISTEN 0 4096 *:9100 users:(("clickhouse",pid=3851032,fd=55)) LISTEN 0 4096 *:9100 users:(("clickhouse",pid=3851032,fd=56)) ``` Only one gRPC and one Arrow Flight listener is created for a group of wildcard `listen_host` values now, which is what the transport does internally anyway. Also, `listen_try` is honored for the protocols that bind their listening socket when they are started rather than when they are created. `EADDRINUSE` from gRPC or Arrow Flight was reported from the plain `server.start()` loop, outside of the `createServer` handler that implements `listen_try`, so it was fatal even with `listen_try` (and with `listen_reuse_port`) enabled - which contradicts the documented behavior of listening to at least one of the addresses without quitting. Not addressed here: plain gRPC still keeps `SO_REUSEPORT` enabled, so a gRPC port that is already taken by a different process is silently shared instead of reported. Making that consistent with `listen_reuse_port` for both gRPC and Arrow Flight is a possible follow-up. For the record, gRPC and Arrow Flight are not available as composable protocols (the `protocols` section): the composable stack is a Poco `TCPServer` with a chain of `TCPServerConnectionFactory` layers that receive an already accepted socket, while gRPC and Arrow Flight own the listening socket, the HTTP/2 framing, TLS and their own event loop, so they can neither be a layer nor sit under `tls` / `proxy1`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix the server failing to start when `listen_host` contains both `::` and `0.0.0.0` and `arrowflight_port` is configured, and fix two gRPC listeners silently sharing one port in the same configuration. `listen_try` now also covers the gRPC and Arrow Flight protocols, which bind their listening socket when they are started. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115074&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115074](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115074+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not report "Server died" when only the liveness check failed
signals.text: Do not report "Server died" when only the liveness check failed <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110479 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110479 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `Stateless tests (amd_tsan, flaky check)` on #110479 @ `038667a9c024` reported a single failing leaf `Server died` while its own aggregate said `Failed: 0, Passed: 3872`. The server did not die: no `<Fatal>` line, no sanitizer report, empty `dmesg`, clean shutdown. The `--hung-check` liveness probe failed and the run was aborted. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110479&sha=038667a9c024695126415fe5f37b76f7a06662fa&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%20flaky%20check%29 Root cause: `tests/clickhouse-test` collapses every in-band abort cause into `STOP_TESTING_EXIT_CODE = 2`, and the job side appends `Server died` for that code unconditionally. Master already carved two causes out of code 2 for this reason; this is the third. This adds `HUNG_CHECK_EXIT_CODE = 5` and `FailureReason.LIVENESS_CHECK_FAILED`, with the leaf `Server liveness check failed` at status FAIL. All four sites that conclude `SERVER_DIED` from a failed probe are changed; the site concluding it from a `<Fatal>` line is untouched, and its neighbour becomes an `elif` of it so fatal evidence is never downgraded. The stop cause travels through one locked first-writer-wins carrier, replacing a `global_time_limit_reached` flag. The leaf names the observation, not a diagnosis: `check_server_liveness` also fails on a non-200 *response*. It is a NEW CIDB `test_name`. The aggregate stays FAIL, so bugfix validation still counts a hang as a repro. Not claimed: a remaining `Server died` row still does not prove a death. Code 2 is generic, and a worker seeing a `<Fatal>` line reaches the parent through `stop_tests()`, exiting 143 - correct there, but decided outside the carrier. Validation: +50 tests asserting the process exit code end to end - the same command exits 2 on master and 5 here. Each changed site has a mutation arm reddening a named case. `ci/tests`: 705 passed, 655 on master. Successor to #112952, not an extension: that PR deliberately excludes exit code 2. Both touch the same region of `functional_tests_results.py`, so the second to merge needs a rebase.

signals.title: Announce the connection endpoint once when the client asks for a password
signals.text: `clickhouse-client` printed `Connecting to ...` twice whenever it had to ask for a password: ``` $ clickhouse client --host clickhouse.new --secure --user alexey-milovidov ClickHouse client version 26.8.1.1. Connecting to clickhouse.new:9440 as user alexey-milovidov. Password for user (alexey-milovidov): Connecting to clickhouse.new:9440 as user alexey-milovidov. Connected to ClickHouse server version 26.8.1. ``` Neither `--password` nor `--ask-password` was given, so the client did not know whether the user has a password at all and connected without one. The server answered `REQUIRED_PASSWORD`, and the retry loop in `Client::main` set `ask-password` and called `connect` again, which prompted for the password and announced the very same endpoint a second time. Now an endpoint is announced only when it differs from the one announced last, and the announcement is forgotten after a successful connection, so a fallback to another port and a reconnect later in the session are still announced. Added `04909_client_password_prompt_announces_endpoint_once.expect`, which fails on the current `master` binary with `The endpoint was announced twice.` and passes with this change. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `clickhouse-client` no longer prints the `Connecting to ...` message twice when it asks for a password interactively. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115081&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115081](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115081+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Report cancellation instead of leaving an in-place set unbuilt
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114463 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107619 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'in'` error when a query with `partial_result_on_first_cancel = 1` was cancelled while the set of an `IN (subquery)` was still being built. ### Description Follow-up to https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114463, asked for in its review. That pull request makes a cancelled mutation report `ABORTED` instead of stopping its nested pipelines silently; the review asked whether the same silent stop is still reachable through the other two interactive-cancel callbacks. I measured both. One is, one is not. **Reachable: `partial_result_on_first_cancel`.** For the first cancel, `TCPHandler::processCancel` only sets `stop_read_return_partial_result` and deliberately does not cancel the query through the process list, so the callback returns a bare `true` (`TCPHandler.cpp:897-898`). `CompletedPipelineExecutor::execute` then cancels the nested set-build pipeline and its poll loop returns normally, so `CreatingSetsTransform::generate` never runs `Set::finishInsert`, while `FutureSetFromSubquery::build` has already moved the source plan out. A caller that evaluates its filter in the same call passes the unbuilt set to `FunctionIn`. On master (`f45871c7cfa`), one cancel during ```sql SELECT count() FROM t WHERE 1 IN (SELECT number FROM numbers(10000000) WHERE sleep(1) = 0) SETTINGS partial_result_on_first_cancel = 1, optimize_use_implicit_projections = 1, optimize_trivial_count_query = 0 ``` reports ``` Code: 49. DB::Exception: Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'in' ... (LOGICAL_ERROR) ``` through `FunctionIn` (`in.cpp:116`) <- `VirtualColumnUtils::filterBlockWithExpression` (`:162`) <- `MergeTreeData::getMinMaxCountProjectionBlock` (`:10463`) <- `optimizeUseAggregateProjections` (`:630`). A debug or sanitizer build aborts on it. **Not reachable: `clickhouse-local`.** Its callback cancels the query through the process list element (`LocalConnection.cpp:191-194`), so the nested pipeline fails instead of stopping silently. The same query interrupted with `SIGINT` reports `Code: 394. DB::Exception: Query was cancelled` on master, with `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` confirming the plan is the `minmax_count` projection. That installer is untouched here. `FutureSetFromSubquery::buildSetInplace` now records whether the cancel callback fired and, if the set was left uncreated, reports `QUERY_WAS_CANCELLED` instead of returning to a caller that cannot distinguish a cancelled build from a completed one. Both conditions are required on purpose, so a set build that stops for a reason other than a cancellation keeps the behaviour it has today. Measured over the routes that stop such a pipeline early: `set_overflow_mode = 'break'`, `transfer_overflow_mode = 'break'` and `read_overflow_mode = 'break'` all still reach `CreatingSetsTransform::generate`, which finishes the set, and the query returns its result; `set_overflow_mode = 'throw'` still reports `SET_SIZE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. For `partial_result_on_first_cancel` this means such a query now fails with `QUERY_WAS_CANCELLED` rather than with the logical error. There is no partial answer to return instead: the cancellation lands during analysis, before a row is produced, and an incomplete `IN` set would silently change the result. The mutation path keeps reporting `ABORTED` as #114463 makes it: its callback throws before this check is reached, which names the mutation the way `MergeTask::checkOperationIsNotCanceled` does and covers every nested pipeline a mutation runs, not only `buildSetInplace`. The ordered variant `buildOrderedSetInplace` needs nothing: #107924 made it build against a clone of the source plan and publish only a created set, so a silently stopped ordered build just skips index analysis. Out of scope, found while measuring this and reported here rather than fixed: a *time limit* with `break` reaches the same logical error without any cancellation, because the limit stops the set-build pipeline the same way. On master, ```sql SELECT count() FROM t WHERE 1 IN (SELECT number FROM numbers(1000)) SETTINGS optimize_use_implicit_projections = 1, optimize_trivial_count_query = 0, max_execution_time = 0.0001, timeout_overflow_mode = 'break' ``` reports `Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'in'` too. The check added here deliberately does not cover it: `break` asks for a truncated result rather than an error, so what a partially built `IN` set should do - report the limit, or silently use the rows read so far, as `set_overflow_mode = 'break'` already does - is a semantic decision, and it is not what this pull request is about. Happy to open an issue or a follow-up for it. New test `04909_cancel_in_subquery_set_build_partial_result`. It asserts up front that the `minmax_count` projection is the plan for the predicate shape under test, so it cannot pass without exercising the synchronous filter evaluation, and both of its wait loops fail loudly rather than cancelling something else. The oracle is the reported outcome, not the survival of the server, so it is live on release builds too. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115083&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115083](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115083+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
