signals.title: Fix PostgreSQL-protocol authentication for users that also have an ssh_key
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/76839 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix authentication over the PostgreSQL wire protocol for users with several authentication methods: a user that also had an `ssh_key` method (or any other method that stores no password) was rejected with `Invalid user or password` even when the correct password for its `scram_sha256_password` method was supplied, and a wrong SCRAM salt was sent to the client when the SCRAM method was not the last one (e.g. for a user with `scram_sha256_password` followed by `sha256_password`). A user with multiple authentication methods, one of which is `ssh_key`, could not authenticate over the PostgreSQL protocol at all (in either order of the methods), while the same user authenticated fine over the native, MySQL, and HTTP protocols. Reproduced on 26.7.3.19 and current master. Anyone who adds a public SSH key to their user (e.g. for the SSH endpoint) silently loses PostgreSQL access with a misleading "wrong password" error. Two defects, both fixed (each order of methods hits at least one of them): 1. `checkScramSHA256Authentication` did not check the type of the authentication method it verifies the client proof against, and `IAccessStorage::authenticateImpl` calls it for every method of the user. For methods that store no password hash (e.g. `ssh_key`), the empty hash was passed to `hmacSHA256` as the HMAC key; `EVP_MAC_init` fails for a null key, so the check threw `OPENSSL_ERROR` (`Authentication failed: Code: 454. DB::Exception: EVP_MAC_init failed`) instead of returning false, aborting the whole authentication instead of trying the next method of the user. Now it returns false for non-SCRAM methods, the same way `checkMySQLAuthentication` handles non-MySQL-compatible methods. 2. `ScrambleSHA256Auth::authenticate` in the PostgreSQL handler sent the salt of the *last* authentication method of the user instead of the salt of the SCRAM method, so the client derived a salted password that could never match the stored verifier: an empty salt when `ssh_key` was last, or an unrelated random salt when e.g. `sha256_password` was. Now it sends the salt of the first `scram_sha256_password` method. Verified before/after with `psql` against a local server; added an integration test covering both method orders, the `scram_sha256_password` + `sha256_password` combination, and wrong-password rejection. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115084&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115084](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115084+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix Arrow Flight Basic authentication for clients sending unpadded Base64
signals.text: The Arrow Flight server rejected clients that send the `authorization: Basic <credentials>` header with the Base64-encoded credentials not padded with `=`. The Go Flight client does exactly that — for example, the ADBC Flight SQL driver with the plain `username`/`password` options performs the `AuthenticateBasicToken` handshake this way, so connecting to ClickHouse failed with a meaningless error: ``` UNKNOWN: [FlightSQL] Unexpected error in RPC handling (Unknown; AuthenticateBasicToken). Vendor code: 2 ``` The cause: `Poco::Base64Decoder` requires padding by default and throws `Poco::DataFormatException`, which escaped `AuthMiddlewareFactory::StartCall` (it only caught `DB::Exception`) into gRPC, which converted it to the generic `UNKNOWN` status above. The fix: - Decode the credentials with the `BASE64_NO_PADDING` option, which accepts both padded and unpadded input, so Go-based Flight clients (including ADBC) can authenticate. - Convert a failed Base64 decode into a proper `AUTHENTICATION_FAILED` exception, reported to the client as an `Unauthenticated` Flight error with a clear message. - Catch the remaining exception types in `StartCall` so no exception can escape into gRPC and produce the meaningless `Unexpected error in RPC handling` status. Verified end-to-end with `adbc_driver_flightsql` 1.12.0: connecting with plain `username`/`password` and running a query now works, while padded Basic credentials, Bearer tokens, and wrong-password errors behave as before. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Arrow Flight server: accept `Basic` authentication credentials encoded in Base64 without padding, as sent by Go-based Flight clients such as the ADBC Flight SQL driver, and return a proper authentication error instead of a generic `Unexpected error in RPC handling` when the `authorization` header is malformed. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115085&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115085](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115085+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix loading suggestions in the embedded client (SSH interface and Web terminal)
signals.text: The embedded client (the SSH interface and the Web terminal) did not load autocompletion words, so TAB completion and as-you-type hints did not work there. The suggestions were loaded through a separate `LocalConnection` created from a bare context, whose constructor creates a new `Session` and authenticates as the `default` user with an empty password. Inside a real server this is wrong twice: - On any server where `default` has a password or does not exist, the authentication fails, so no completions from `system.completions` are ever loaded — and the error message is written to the server's stderr, invisible to the user. - On servers where `default` can log in with an empty password, the words were loaded with the grants of `default` instead of the logged-in user, leaking names of databases, tables and columns the user is not allowed to see (`system.completions` filters by the querying user's access rights). Now the embedded client loads suggestions synchronously through its main, already-authenticated connection. It is idle at that point, and the embedded client always waits for suggestions to load before showing the prompt anyway. Errors are reported to the user's terminal instead of the server's stderr. Added integration tests for both interfaces: an interactive SSH PTY session and a `/webterminal` WebSocket session, each checking that a table the user can see is TAB-completed while a table the user has no grants on is not. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix autocompletion (hints and TAB completion from `system.completions`) in the embedded client used by the SSH interface and the Web terminal: suggestions were loaded through a separate connection that authenticated as the `default` user with an empty password, which failed on servers where `default` has a password, and otherwise leaked names of entities the logged-in user has no access to. Suggestions are now loaded through the session's own connection. - [ ] Documentation entry for user-facing changes <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115086&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115086](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115086+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Reload a persisted `url()` table with the storage its creation selected
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104437 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a server that refuses to start after a table was created with `CREATE TABLE ... AS url('http://host/**/', ...)` while `allow_experimental_url_wildcard_from_index_pages` was enabled. Loading such a table's metadata re-evaluated the experimental check and failed with `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED`, aborting startup. ### Description Reported by @ bacek on #104437, where `Stress test (amd_tsan)` failed with `Cannot start clickhouse-server` after a fuzzer created `url('/**/', JSONEachRow, 'x int')`. No fuzzer is needed: enable the setting, create such a table, restart with the default. Root cause is one defaulted parameter. `ITableFunction::execute` declares `bool is_insert_query = false`; `CREATE ... AS url(...)` passes `true` explicitly (`InterpreterCreateQuery.cpp:2403`), while metadata replay (`DatabaseOnDisk.cpp:117`) passes nothing. `TableFunctionURL::getStorage` computes `use_web_wildcard = !is_insert_query && ...`, so the two take opposite branches for the same stored table: creation builds a plain `StorageURL` and never reaches the experimental check, replay builds `StorageObjectStorage` and does. The check is dead at creation and live only on replay, and metadata loading rethrows. The fix treats a definition arriving with stored columns as a persisted one being replayed, so it resolves to the storage creation selected. The check is not suppressed, it becomes unreachable because the correct branch is taken. Suppressing it would instead enable index-page expansion with the setting disabled and give the table a read-only storage. `ENGINE = URL` was already fixed this way in 64abbdd31d85b15 ("Gate `URL` wildcard experiment check to creation"). Behaviour change: a persisted glob `url()` table that today rebuilds as `StorageObjectStorage` after a restart now rebuilds as the `StorageURL` its creation built. Both carriers are covered by the one change and both are tested: explicit structure, and `structure = 'auto'` via `StorageTableFunctionProxy` (the surface of an earlier `test_url_wildcard_schema_inference` failure). `urlCluster` cannot persist a table. The creation-time check in `getActualTableStructure` is deliberately untouched, since a columns-less `CREATE` reaches it before `execute`. Querying `url()` directly still requires the setting. Out of scope: the check stays dead at creation, so `CREATE` with a glob still succeeds with the setting off. `ytsaurus()` has the same problem by another mechanism. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=104437&sha=bee15ffc5ec3d2a9b5479bd1fbc197ac6458eebc&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_tsan%29 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115095&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115095](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115095+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Emit IF EXISTS when formatting ALTER ... MATERIALIZE INDEX/STATISTICS/PROJECTION
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114171 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed the formatting of `ALTER TABLE ... MATERIALIZE INDEX`, `MATERIALIZE STATISTICS` and `MATERIALIZE PROJECTION`, which dropped the `IF EXISTS` clause, so the formatted query was not the query that was parsed. Also rejected four `ALTER ... STATISTICS` AST JSON payloads that the SQL parser cannot produce and that formatted into a different command. ### Description `ParserAlterQuery` accepts and records `IF EXISTS` for `MATERIALIZE INDEX`, `MATERIALIZE STATISTICS` and `MATERIALIZE PROJECTION`, but `ASTAlterCommand::formatImpl` never emitted it, so formatting a parsed query produced a different query than the user wrote. The 11 sibling blocks in the same function all emit the clause already. Exactly these three of the 15 scalar `ASTAlterCommand` members fail a format-and-reparse preservation probe on master. The clause is not consumed for these three today, so no execution outcome changes. It is still user-visible: `system.mutations.command` reports exactly this formatted text, and so does the mutation entry persisted to ZooKeeper and disk. It surfaced as an `Inconsistent AST formatting` logical error in `Stateless tests (amd_debug, parallel)` from `02864_statistics_ddl.sql:194` ([CI report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114171&sha=105deb1ebf1fbc5dc4c3749df97ed590c3b9b30e&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_debug%2C%20parallel%29)). That run adds a tree hash over `if_exists`, and a member that is hashed but not formatted makes the round-trip check in `executeQuery.cpp` diverge and abort in debug builds. For `MATERIALIZE STATISTICS` the emission goes inside the column-list branch: the `ALL` form carries a null `statistics_decl`, and `MATERIALIZE STATISTICS IF EXISTS ALL` would reparse as the statistic on a column literally named `ALL`. The parser reads `IF EXISTS` and `IN PARTITION` only in that column-list branch, so on the `ALL` form neither is reachable from SQL, but both are constructible in AST JSON and both format into a different command. `readJSON` now rejects them for `MATERIALIZE STATISTICS` and `DROP/CLEAR STATISTICS`. Two were already wrong on master: `if_exists` formatted as `CLEAR STATISTICS IF EXISTS ALL` and reparsed as a column named `ALL`, and a `partition` was dropped, widening the mutation from one partition to every partition. Validation: the round-trips are pinned in `04126_parser_alter_query_variants` with the `ALL` forms asserted byte-unchanged, the rejections in `04350_ast_json_parser_impossible_field_combinations`. Every new assertion fails on a pre-fix binary.

signals.title: Fix arrayROCAUC and arrayAUCPR returning order-dependent results for NaN scores
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104763 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `arrayROCAUC` and `arrayAUCPR` (and their aliases `arrayAUC` and `arrayPRAUC`) returning a different result for the same data depending on the order of the array elements when a score was `NaN`. A `NaN` score now makes the result `NaN`. Closes [#104763](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104763). ### Description Closes: #104763. **The problem.** These are pure functions of a set of (score, label) pairs, so permuting the pairs must not change the result. With a `NaN` score it did: `arrayAUCPR([nan, 0.5], [1, 1])` returned `nan` while `arrayAUCPR([0.5, nan], [1, 1])` returned `1`. No error was raised, so the metric was silently wrong. **Root cause.** Two independent defects in `FunctionArrayAUC::apply`, both reachable from a single `NaN`: 1. The descending-score comparator passed to `std::sort` is not a strict weak ordering when a score is `NaN` (every comparison with `NaN` is false, so incomparability is not transitive), so the sorted order, and the traversal with it, follows the input order. 2. `threshold` is seeded from the first sorted element so the first iteration never increments the area, but `nan != nan` is true, so the guard fires with `tp = fp = 0`, and the Precision-Recall precision term becomes `0 / 0`. **The change.** `apply` returns `NaN` if any score is `NaN`, before sorting. That removes both defects at once, and `std::sort`'s precondition then holds for every input reaching it. `NaN` in, `NaN` out matches `sum`, `avg`, `arraySum` and `corr`, and `arrayROCAUC` already used `NaN` for its undefined cases. Beyond the reported `arrayAUCPR` case this also fixes `arrayROCAUC`, both aliases, the `scale` argument and the 3- and 4-argument `partial_offsets` forms, all affected the same way. The intentional value change: any `NaN`-containing input now returns `NaN` instead of an order-dependent number, including the all-`NaN` case, where `arrayROCAUC` returned `1` or `0` depending on the label order. Infinities are ordered normally, so they are unaffected and have regression tests. A `NaN` label was already order independent. Rejecting `NaN` with an exception would be backward incompatible, so I did not pick it unilaterally. If a hard error is preferred, I will switch. Requested in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104763#issuecomment-5312328708.

signals.title: Do not read the master-only system.parts.files column in 04550_restore_fsync_after_insert

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111378 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115088 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `04550_restore_fsync_after_insert.sh` (added by #111378) read the `files` column of `system.parts` to size the encrypted-incremental-restore fsync assertion. That column was added by 476e9fcb3bb3f26 in January, after 25.8 forked, so the automated 25.8 backport #115088 fails at runtime even though the cherry-pick applied cleanly and the script is byte-identical: ``` Code: 47. Unknown expression identifier `files` in scope SELECT files FROM system.parts WHERE ... AND (`table` = 't_restore_fsync_enc'). (UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER) Code: 32. Attempt to read after eof: value cannot be parsed as UInt64 for query parameter 'files'. ``` CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115088&sha=980e9739e2ff0687cec113ed6460d38af75034f6&name_0=BackportPR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_asan%2C%20distributed%20plan%2C%20parallel%2C%201%2F2%29 The count the assertion wants is how many files RESTORE copies and must therefore fsync. The test already measures exactly that for its first table, with `SELECT path FROM system.parts` plus `find`. This drops the `system.parts.files` read and feeds the encrypted arm the same count. The two tables have identical schema, data and part-layout settings, so their parts hold the same file set; the assertion gets stronger, since the physical count also covers `checksums.txt`, `columns.txt` and the zero-byte `arr.bin` that the checksums map does not enumerate. `.reference` is unchanged. Validation: on the official 25.8 binary the old test reproduces both errors above and the new one runs to completion. On master the encrypted restore performs 20 `FileSync` events against a required 18, and the two arms' part file lists are identical on both branches (18 files on master, 15 on 25.8), so the reuse does not depend on a master-specific layout. Disabling `fsync_after_insert` on the encrypted table still fails the test, so the assertion is not vacuous. 50/50 runs green with randomized settings. Note that #115088 cannot pick this up by regeneration: the backport tree is built from #111378's merge commit, so a regenerated backport carries the same broken line.

signals.title: Disable distributed index analysis with projections (wrong results)
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Disable distributed index analysis with projections (wrong results) Parts are identified by name, but projection parts share the projection's name across all parent parts, so analysis collapsed them into one entry and then filtered out valid parent parts, dropping rows. Skip distributed index analysis for projection parts (analyze locally); proper support needs parent part name + projection name on the wire. Note, that the problem not only for applied projections: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/7604e8de0caf5940d9e66872bcfb8dffcc602c5b/src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/optimizeUseNormalProjection.cpp#L617-L637 But for any tables with usable projections, since we try to filter out parts based on the analysis from projections as well: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/7604e8de0caf5940d9e66872bcfb8dffcc602c5b/src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/projectionsCommon.cpp#L418

signals.title: Accept LowCardinality(UInt64) as a dictionary simple primary key
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104539 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `CREATE DICTIONARY` failing with `Incorrect type of ID column: must be UInt64, but it is LowCardinality` when the simple primary key is declared as `LowCardinality(UInt64)` and `dictionary_validate_primary_key_type` is enabled. Closes #104539. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104539 With `dictionary_validate_primary_key_type = 1`, declaring a simple primary key as `LowCardinality(UInt64)` is rejected: ``` Code: 36. DB::Exception: Incorrect type of ID column: must be UInt64, but it is LowCardinality. (BAD_ARGUMENTS) ``` With the setting off (the default) the same dictionary is created, loads, and answers `dictGet`/`dictHas`/`SELECT *` correctly, with the key normalized to plain `UInt64`. So valid input is rejected. **Root cause.** `StorageDictionary::getNamesAndTypes` compared the raw outer `TypeIndex` of the declared key type against `TypeIndex::UInt64`. For `LowCardinality(UInt64)` that yields the wrapper's index, not the payload's. `LowCardinality` is a physical-representation wrapper, not a distinct logical type, so the validator answered a logical question with a physical predicate. **The change** unwraps one `LowCardinality` level before the comparison, for both the test and the message. The declared simple-key type is already advisory everywhere else: `getKeyTypes()` returns `{UInt64}` unconditionally and every other simple-key site constructs `DataTypeUInt64` directly, which is why the setting-off path already worked. This is the only site in `src/` that type-tests the declared key type. **Exactly one type changes behaviour:** `LowCardinality(UInt64)` becomes accepted. `Nullable(UInt64)` and `LowCardinality(Nullable(UInt64))` stay rejected, since a NULL key is meaningless for a lookup; one-level unwrap gives that for free, and the new test pins it so a later switch to `removeLowCardinalityAndNullable` cannot silently widen it. `LowCardinality(String)` also stays rejected, as a plain `String` key is rejected by design; its message now names the payload. The setting's default (`false`) is unchanged and nothing valid today becomes invalid, so no `SettingsChangesHistory.cpp` entry applies. Noted, not addressed here: `LowCardinality` keys are only constructible on `LAYOUT(FLAT())`, because `DictionaryStructure::getAttributes` strips `Nullable` but not `LowCardinality` and `AttributeUnderlyingType` has no `LowCardinality` member, so other layouts fail earlier with `UNKNOWN_TYPE` regardless of this setting.

signals.title: Fix compiled `if`/`multiIf` on a negative `Time` value
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `if` and `multiIf` returning a large positive value instead of a negative one when a `Time` branch is combined with `Time64`, `DateTime` or `DateTime64` and the expression is JIT-compiled. ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114168 (found there in review; a separate mechanism) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103390 A negative `Time` value read through a JIT-compiled `if`/`multiIf` comes back as a huge positive number: ```sql SELECT if(number % 2 = 0, toTime('-01:00:00'), toTime64('00:00:00', 3)) FROM numbers(1); -- executions 1-3: -01:00:00.000 -- execution 4+: 999:59:59.000 ``` No `SETTINGS` clause is needed to hit this: `compile_expressions` defaults to `1` and `min_count_to_compile_expression` to `3`, so the 4th execution of the expression in a session silently changes the answer. `enable_time_time64_type` also defaults to `1`. The wrong value is ticks `4294963696` = `2^32 - 3600`, i.e. the negative `Int32` tick count zero-extended to 64 bits. Root cause: `typeIsSigned` in `src/DataTypes/Native.cpp` did not list the `Time` family, so the widening cast emitted by `FunctionIfBase::compileImpl` asked whether `Time` is signed, got `false`, and LLVM emitted `zext` where `sext` was required. `Time` is `DataTypeNumberBase<Int32>` and is the only member of the date/time family that widens on this path, which is why the defect is specific to it. `Time64` is included in the same predicate for correctness of the contract: `isDecimal()` matches only `TypeIndex::Decimal32..256` and so does not cover `TypeIndex::Time64` - the same reason `isDateTime64()` is listed separately. No wrong-result carrier reaches the `Time64` half today, so it is not given a test that could not fail. Validation: five wrong-result carriers plus a `Nullable(Time)` case are covered by the new test. The reference values were taken from the non-compiled path on an unpatched binary, so the oracle is independent of this change. With the predicate token removed the test fails on 7 of 13 lines; non-negative `Time`, large-negative `Time`, and `DateTime64` controls are unchanged. 50/50 runs under settings randomization pass.

signals.title: Fix THERE_IS_NO_COLUMN for DISTINCT with an aggregate projection
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112168 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `THERE_IS_NO_COLUMN` ("Cannot find column in source stream") for `SELECT DISTINCT expr(k) ... ORDER BY k` on a table that has an aggregate projection grouped on `k`. Closes #112168. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112168 `SELECT DISTINCT v * 2 FROM t ORDER BY v` works on an ordinary table, but throws as soon as `t` carries an aggregate projection grouped on `v`: ``` Code: 8. Cannot find column `__table1.v` in source stream, there are only columns: [multiply(__table1.v, 2_UInt8)]. (THERE_IS_NO_COLUMN) ``` **Root cause.** `DistinctStep` passes its input header through (`updateOutputHeader` assigns `input_headers.front()`), so that header carries the DISTINCT columns *plus* anything a later step needs, here the `ORDER BY` source column. The aggregate-projection matcher was handed only `DistinctStep::getColumnNames()`, so `foldActionsByProjection` emitted a subtree without the extra column, and the splice that must reproduce the step's full header then failed inside `ActionsDAG::makeConvertingActions`. Only `optimize_use_projections = 0` worked around it, because this pass is gated on `optimize_projection` rather than on `query_plan_enable_optimizations`. **The change** passes the step's output header names, the set the replacement subtree is actually required to produce. Matching then declines by itself when a required column is not computable from the projection keys, so those queries fall back to the ordinary read; queries whose extra column is a function of the projection keys keep using the projection. Names are taken verbatim without de-duplication, since `makeConvertingActions` consumes one input position per result column and `checkBlockStructure` compares positionally. **Validation.** Both directions on a debug build. Each arm compares the `optimize_use_projections = 1` result against the `= 0` result, asserting the value set rather than an ordering that `ORDER BY` on a column outside the DISTINCT list leaves ambiguous. Arms cover the reported query, a filter, an `ORDER BY` column the projection cannot produce, a two-key projection, partial projection data, `LowCardinality` and `Nullable` keys, and a repeated DISTINCT expression. Each also asserts via `EXPLAIN` that the projection is still selected where usable and declined where not, so a silent fallback cannot pass as a correct result.

signals.title: Web terminal: do not connect before the host page supplies the credentials
signals.text: A `/webterminal` page embedded in a host page - `play.html`, or the ClickHouse Cloud console - is loaded without credentials in its URL and receives them from the host page over `postMessage`, on the iframe's `load` event. It nevertheless opened a connection of its own at startup, before that message could arrive, so every embedded terminal authenticated twice: first with an empty password, which can only succeed for a passwordless user, and then, a moment later, with the credentials from the host page, after the first WebSocket had been closed and replaced. The visible symptom is `Connecting...` printed twice - `attemptConnect` announces every attempt, and whether the first line is erased before the second is printed depends on timing. Behind it are a wasted WebSocket, a guaranteed-failing authentication, and, for a passwordless user, an established session that gets torn down right away. The page now waits for the credentials instead of connecting on its own. A host page that never sends them - it does not implement the protocol, or its origin is not trusted - would leave a terminal that neither connects nor prompts, so the page says that it is waiting and Enter hands the login over to the interactive prompt; credentials arriving after that no longer hijack what the user is typing. The pages opened as a normal tab, or with a `user` URL parameter, keep connecting immediately. The wait became a state of the page's own state machine, which makes the `waitingForCredentials` and `initialAutoAuth` flags, and the `ws.onclose` branch they served, unnecessary. The new `tests/integration/test_webterminal_startup` follows the existing `test_play_reconcile_startup`: it fetches `/webterminal` from a real server and runs the page's real script in a Node `vm` with a stubbed terminal and `WebSocket`, then drives each flow and asserts which connections were opened and what was displayed. Against this branch all 34 checks pass; against `master` 23 fail, including `announces the attempt exactly once -- actual: 2`. It also pins the paths that must keep connecting immediately, the prompt after a rejected password, and that credentials from an untrusted origin, from a trusted host over plain HTTP, or from a window that is not the parent are ignored - the wait is now the only way into an embedded session, so a hole in either check would hand the terminal to a foreign page. Reported by a user of clickhouse.new, where the console drives the terminal through exactly this embedded flow. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105191 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115067 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A web terminal embedded in another page, such as the SQL console or `play.html`, receives its credentials from that page and no longer opens a connection of its own before they arrive. Previously it connected twice - once with an empty password, then again with the real credentials - and printed `Connecting...` twice. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115148&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115148](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115148+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Reduce the per-arm work of 04895_parquet_dictionary_source_prefetch_lifetime
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114668 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114668 (the use-after-free this test guards). @ PedroTadim asked for the per-arm work of this test to be trimmed. `04895` runs at 93.5% of the flaky check's 180 s per-arm cap on `Stateless tests (amd_asan_ubsan, flaky check)`: p50 141.5 s, p99 165.9 s, max 168.3 s over 50 arms in 21 days of public CIDB, so about 12 s of headroom. No duration breach yet, so this is headroom rather than a live failure. The fixture is larger than the mechanism needs. The detector requires many concurrent queued read ranges alive at throw time, and what supplies them is the row group count plus `input_format_parquet_local_file_min_bytes_for_seek = 1` and the 32 download / 32 parsing threads. None of that depends on payload size. Scaling `numbers()` and `output_format_parquet_row_group_size` by the same factor of 10 keeps the row group count at exactly 397 while cutting the file from 19,785,515 to 2,356,314 bytes. I did not shrink `repeat('y', 400)`: it is a single distinct value, so it is RLE_DICTIONARY encoded to about 0.25 B/row. `key` is 97.5% of the file and `val` 2.5%, and cutting the string width from 400 to 40 moves total bytes by only 18%. Validation. Against a binary with the `resetReadBuffer` override removed, the trimmed test fails 20/20 with the pure-virtual abort at `Prefetcher.cpp:116` in `readSync`, and passes 20/20 with the fix. Because both the trimmed and the untrimmed fixture saturate at 20/20 there, I lowered the thread counts until redness became fractional to get resolution: at 8 threads the trimmed fixture reddens 30/40 versus 4/40 untrimmed, so the trim makes the detector more sensitive, not less. All three oracles are unchanged and were each shown able to redden, `.reference` is untouched, and 50 randomized runs pass. <details> <summary>Measured duration, ASAN, trimmed vs current</summary> `tests/clickhouse-test`, randomized settings, 12 arms each against the same server: | arm | min | p50 | p90 | max | |---|---|---|---|---| | trimmed | 20.03 s | 20.84 s | 21.34 s | 21.90 s | | current | 21.14 s | 22.90 s | 23.49 s | 23.65 s | The serial gain is about 9% because the roughly 2000 row group reads per arm are deliberately kept. The gain grows with concurrency, which is the regime the flaky check runs in, since `allow_oversubscription` is False there and every worker runs the same test: | concurrent copies | trimmed p50 | current p50 | saving | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 11.43 s | 12.51 s | 8.6% | | 8 | 12.31 s | 15.16 s | 18.8% | | 16 | 12.87 s | 19.44 s | 33.8% | | 20 | 13.66 s | 22.67 s | 39.7% | Server side, reload phase IO drops from 54.24 MiB to 13.99 MiB at an identical 1985 row group reads. These are local numbers on one box and do not predict a contended CI runner, so there is no timing assertion in the test. </details>

signals.title: Show file sizes next to artifact links in CI reports
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114722 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114803 Reimplements #114722 (reverted in #114803 because it duplicated the existing size-tracking functionality). Every link to an uploaded file now shows its size, e.g. `clickhouse-common-static_26.8.1.1332_amd64.deb (1.2 GiB)`, in both places file links appear: the widget on a job page and the expanded info row of any result. Instead of recording a new per-link size map at upload time, the size is taken from the `StorageUsage` data already attached to each result's `ext`: `uploaded_details` is a `{basename: bytes}` map, and a link's last path component is exactly that basename, so `json.html` looks the size up directly. This makes the rendering change purely a `json.html` one — no `s3.py`, `result.py`, or private-proxy link-rewrite changes are needed. Links with no recorded size (a link to another report, or any report produced before this change) render exactly as before; `json.html` has to be deployed for existing report URLs to pick up the rendering change. This PR also slims down the workflow-level report: when a job's result is embedded as a sub-result of the workflow result, only the `ext` keys the report renders per row are kept (`labels`, `hlabels`, `storage_usage`). The rest — notably the heavy decimated host `metrics` timeline — is dropped, as it is only needed on the job's own report, which is uploaded separately with the full `ext`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required)

signals.title: Do not serve min/max from an unusable minmax_count projection bound
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111938 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `min` and `max` returning a wrong value when the implicit `_minmax_count_projection` answered them from a part-level bound that is not a real row value: a `NULL` in a `Nullable` sorting key, a `NaN` in a float key, or a `Tuple` bound assembled component-wise. Such a query now reads rows instead of using the projection. ### Description `getMinMaxCountProjectionBlock` answers `min(col)`/`max(col)` from part-level bounds, feeding each straight into an aggregate state. That is only correct when the bound is a real row value, ordered as the aggregate orders it. Three ways it is not: - **NULL** (as reported): keys sort NULLS LAST so the top index entry is a NULL while `max` skips NULLs, and the `POSITIVE_INFINITY` pruning sentinel materializes as a SQL NULL. - **NaN**, no `Nullable` involved: the writer sorts NaN above every number while `max` skips it, so `Float64 ORDER BY k` over `(1),(200),(nan)` gives `nan`. - **Component-wise synthesis**, no NULL or NaN: `getExtremes` runs per column, so a `Tuple` bound envelopes each component's extreme and need not be any row. This breaks `min` too. Worse than the reported `NULL` is the silent shape: when the true maximum shares a part with a NULL, `max` returns the largest of the other parts, `4` instead of `200`. The fix declines the implicit projection for such a query, reusing the escape hatch this function already has earlier (`return {}` when a part has no final mark). A part whose bound pair is one repeated degenerate value stays exempt, since skipping it is the right contribution; for an index bound that exemption also requires a final mark, without which the index samples granule starts only and a repeated pair proves nothing. I rejected skipping only the poisoned part, which is the silent shape above, and changing the write path, since the sentinel is needed for `IS NULL` pruning and existing parts would stay broken. The new test covers each class across nullable, low-cardinality, tuple and float keys, ASC and DESC, one and several parts, and a part with no final mark. Issue #104412 is a different defect here, verified unaffected.

signals.title: Fix wrong count and wrong DELETE when a NULL expression sits under NOT
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112242 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112242 Requested by @ nihalzp in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112242#issuecomment-5312306258 (reported by @ zlareb1). ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results when a `WHERE` clause contained a `NULL` expression under a `NOT`, for example `SELECT count() FROM t WHERE NOT (id >= 20 AND NULL)`. Index analysis treated such a condition as provably true for the whole range, so the filter was skipped: `count()` returned rows the query rejects, and `ALTER TABLE ... DELETE` with that condition removed rows it should have kept. ### Description ```sql CREATE TABLE t (id UInt32) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; INSERT INTO t SELECT number FROM numbers(40); SELECT count() FROM t WHERE NOT (id >= 20 AND NULL); -- returned 40, correct is 20 ``` Reading the rows returned 20, so `count()` and the row set disagreed on one predicate. A mutation was worse: `ALTER TABLE t DELETE WHERE NOT (id >= 38 AND NULL)` deleted all 40 rows, although the predicate is `NULL` for `id` 38 and 39, so those two had to survive. **Root cause.** `cloneDAGWithInversionPushDown` pushes `NOT` to the leaves. For `NOT (id >= 20 AND NULL)`, De Morgan turns the `and` into an `or` and pushes the inversion into both children; the all-NULL leaf is not recognized, so the tail wraps it in a literal `not()`, which `RPNBuilder` complements classically into "provably true for every row". Both steps hold only in two-valued logic: `NOT NULL` is `NULL`, which `WHERE` must reject. **The change.** Before the node dispatch, an all-NULL node absorbs the inversion instead of receiving a `not()` wrapper, the same idiom the neighbouring `materialize` and trivial-cast branches use. It still folds to "never true" downstream, correct because `NULL` is not `TRUE`, and a non-negated `x AND NULL` keeps its exact fast path. Absorbing the inversion substitutes the operand's type for the `not()` result type, so the guard is confined to `boolean_context`, the existing flag for positions where the caller discards the value. In a value position a negation would otherwise change type and drop valid rows. The all-NULL test needs both a column and a type check: `toInt64OrNull('x')` is typed `Nullable(Int64)`, while `if(id % 2, NULL, NULL)` has no constant column. <details> <summary>Validation</summary> Debug build of the base commit vs the same build with the change. | probe | base | with change | correct | |---|---|---|---| | `count() WHERE NOT (id >= 20 AND NULL)` | 40 | 20 | 20 | | same with `toInt64OrNull('x')` | 40 | 20 | 20 | | same with `CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(UInt8)')` | 40 | 20 | 20 | | same with `if(id % 2, NULL, NULL)` | 40 | 20 | 20 | | same with `materialize(NULL)` | 40 | 20 | 20 | | `numbers(100) WHERE NOT (number = 5 AND NULL) LIMIT 10` | 9 | 10 | 10 | | minmax skip index, same predicate | 40 | 20 | 20 | | `ALTER DELETE WHERE NOT (id >= 38 AND NULL)`, survivors | `[]` | `[38,39]` | `[38,39]` | | `count() WHERE id >= 20 AND NULL` | 0 | 0 | 0 | | `numbers() WHERE number > 0 AND NULL LIMIT 10` | 0 fast | 0 fast | 0 fast | | value position, `ifNull(NOT materialize(CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(Int64)')), 0)`, rows | 40 | 40 | 40 | | same with `Nullable(Float64)`, rows | 40 | 40 | 40 | The new test fails on the base build, passes with the change, and passed 50/50 randomized runs. Deleting any one of the three parts of the guard makes it fail again on exactly the arms that part covers: the column test covers `toInt64OrNull` and `CAST`, the type test covers `if(id % 2, NULL, NULL)`, the `boolean_context` test covers the two value-position arms. The unbounded `numbers()` lines pin the positive direction, which an earlier attempt at this fix turned into a hang. The projection, `KeyCondition` and minmax test families were run on both builds: the same 23 tests fail either way, all on ZooKeeper and distributed connections unavailable in this sandbox, none mentioning the exact-count projection or `KeyCondition`. </details>

signals.title: Enable the consecutive-keys cache for fixed-size aggregation keys
signals.text: The `keys128` and `keys256` aggregation methods had `consecutive_keys_optimization = false`, so aggregating data whose keys arrive in long runs of equal values (e.g. anything grouped by a fixed-size key that is a prefix of the table sort order) paid a full hash-and-probe per row. Enabling the existing `LastElementCache` for these methods (including the two-level variants) skips the hash table entirely within a run, at the cost of one wide key compare per row; the aggregator's adaptive hit-rate machinery already disables the cache on random keys, verified by a random-key `keys256` microbenchmark showing no regression (3.88 s baseline vs 3.82/3.88 s). On clustered keys (runs of ~200k equal `Tuple(UInt64, UUID)` values, 400M rows) this saves ~10% of aggregation CPU. Session: ad94609b-7b39-4f96-af16-7947efc50974 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Aggregation by fixed-size keys of 17-32 bytes (the `keys128`/`keys256` methods, e.g. `GROUP BY` a `UUID` or a `Tuple(UInt64, UInt64)`) now uses the consecutive-keys cache, making aggregation of sorted or clustered data up to 10% faster; the cache disables itself adaptively on random keys.

signals.title: Carry the join analyze mode into a SQL SECURITY view's context
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` losing the join statistics of a view declared `SQL SECURITY DEFINER` or `SQL SECURITY NONE` whose body contains a JOIN. In debug and sanitizer builds the query aborted with the logical error `JoinStep analyzed without the analyze mode`. ### Description The assertion is at `JoinStep.cpp:268`. In release it is compiled out, and the report is then built from statistics the join was never told to collect. `join_analyze_mode` is a `Context` member field, not a setting, and only `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` arms it. `Context::createCopy` carries it, which is why a bare JOIN, a plain view and an `INVOKER` view all report correctly. But `StorageInMemoryMetadata::getSQLSecurityOverriddenContext` rebuilds the context from the *global* one for `DEFINER` and `NONE`, then hand-carries a curated list of caller state onto it, and `join_analyze_mode` was missing from that list. The view's inner joins were planned with the mode off, and the walker then reached them. The fix carries the field across that rebuild: one line, above the `NONE` early return so it covers both branches, beside the existing `setNormalizedQueryHash` carry which exists for the same reason. It is inert unless `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` armed the outer context, and it cannot weaken the barrier the rebuild creates, because the mode selects diagnostic statistics, not identity or access rights. The failure is deterministic in six lines of SQL. New test `04926` covers `DEFINER`, `NONE`, a `DEFINER` view joining an `ENGINE = Join` table (the sibling assertion at `JoinStep.cpp:490`), and an `INVOKER` control. It asserts the statistics arrived rather than that nothing aborted, since a no-abort check passes vacuously in release. Unpatched, the first three arms abort and the control passes; with the fix all four pass, 50/50 under randomized settings. Two residuals. A second fuzzer shape reaches the same assertion through `prometheusQuery` with no view involved; it did not reproduce on either binary, so it is not root-caused. A deserialized remote plan also never sets the mode, but `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` refuses distributed plans. Found by the AST fuzzer: - https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114038&sha=cc2993d762348f09f324efc04cc1c8f43819da3e&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29 - https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114867&sha=f4c473e73f752fa079dc3caec5b0151adefe91e6&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29

signals.title: Add a test for lazy materialization over a shadowed constant
signals.text: Adds a regression test for https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112209. With `query_plan_enable_optimizations = 0` the first optimization pass never runs, so the chain below the sort keeps an `ExpressionStep` whose DAG re-materializes the constant of a constant `SELECT` item while still taking a same-named input (a `COLUMN` node named `2_UInt8` next to an `INPUT` of that name). Lazy materialization lives in the second pass, which that setting does not gate, so it split such a DAG; `ActionsDAG::split` renamed the node promoted to the lazy half (`avoid_duplicate_inputs`) to `2_UInt8_0`, while the re-stacked `Sorting` step still resolved `2_UInt8` by name, and `PartialSortingTransform` failed at pipeline build with `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK`. The query was fixed indirectly by https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112326, which added `hasInputNameShadowedByComputedNode` and declines such plans upfront. That change was written for the row-policy `CAST(x, ...) AS x` shape and its test `04654_lazy_materialization_shadowed_input_name` covers only that variant, so this test pins the constant `SELECT` item with `ORDER BY ALL` as well. Verified: it throws on 26.8.1.203 (`ecb9cf7b997`) and passes from `f45cb411cbc` on. signals.title: Fix flaky 04896_orfill_merge_group_by_overflow_any under randomized index_granularity_bytes
signals.text: `04896_orfill_merge_group_by_overflow_any` fails on master whenever the stateless-test runner randomizes `index_granularity_bytes` down to a small value: ``` Code: 117. DB::Exception: Projection p is specified in setting force_optimize_projection_name but not used. (INCORRECT_DATA) ``` The runner's own diagnosis isolated the culprit to `--index_granularity_bytes 21597` (182/182 runs failed with it, 249/249 passed without randomization). Projection `p` stores five aggregate states per row, so its parts are several times wider than the parent table's three `UInt64` columns. With adaptive granularity on and a small `index_granularity_bytes`, the parts of `p` get cut into more granules than the parent parts — 5 marks against 2 at `--index_granularity_bytes 21597` — so `optimizeUseAggregateProjections` discards `p` as "not better than the original table with 2 marks", selects `p2` instead, and `force_optimize_projection_name = 'p'` throws. This fix turns adaptive granularity off for the table so that `p` and the parent table are cut into the same number of granules and `p` stays selectable. The test does not depend on granularity in any other way, and `index_granularity` itself stays randomized. Verified locally on `aarch64`: the test reproduces the failure deterministically before the change under the CI settings, and matches its reference after the change under the full CI setting set as well as across a sweep of `index_granularity_bytes` / `index_granularity` / `min_bytes_for_wide_part` values. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=39e9002316ee472caf62fbb837832c776f10c06f&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28arm_binary%2C%20parallel%29 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114740 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required)

signals.title: Do not fan out the single-row output of an aggregation without keys
signals.text: After `AggregatingStep`, the pipeline was unconditionally resized to `max_threads` output streams. For an aggregation with `GROUP BY` keys that is what enables downstream parallelism, but an aggregation without keys produces at most one row: fanning that single row out to `max_threads` streams cannot create any parallelism — the only chunk still goes to one stream — while every downstream step instantiates `max_threads` processors that are created, scheduled and profiled for nothing. `AggregatingStep::transformPipeline` now keeps a single output stream when `params.keys` is empty (the same way it already does when results must be produced in order of bucket number). For example, `EXPLAIN PIPELINE SELECT count() FROM t` loses the `Resize 1 → <max_threads>` node and the `× <max_threads>` fan-out of every subsequent transform (see the update of `00172_early_constant_folding`). This was found while profiling tiny instant PromQL stat queries of the shape `sum(a) / sum(b)` over `TimeSeries` tables, where the emitted SQL contains several keyless aggregations and the fan-out multiplied the pipeline size; the effect is generic and this change is independent of the PromQL transpiler. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115171 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): An aggregation without `GROUP BY` keys no longer fans its single-row output out to `max_threads` streams, so queries whose plan continues after such an aggregation get a much smaller pipeline (fewer processors to create, schedule and profile) without losing any parallelism.
signals.author: nikitamikhaylov

signals.title: Emit smaller SQL for PromQL binary operators over single-series operands
signals.text: Instant stat queries like `sum(a) / sum(b)` were dominated by query compilation: the transpiler emitted an 11-step WITH chain with per-side rename steps, duplicate-check aggregations and a parallel-hash `INNER ANY JOIN` — for operands that each hold at most one row. Three changes shrink the emitted SQL: aggregation operators alias the transformed group directly instead of appending a rename-only step (every PromQL aggregation loses one WITH step); binary operators whose side joins on the bare `group` column skip the per-side rename and duplicate-check steps (group uniqueness is the grid contract); and when both operands are provably aggregated to the constant zero group (aggregation without `by`/`without` — at most one row with an empty label set), the equality join is replaced by a CROSS JOIN, which preserves PromQL vector-matching semantics for this case exactly (an empty side yields an empty result) and never takes the parallel-hash path. `sum(a)/sum(b)` goes from 11 to 7 WITH steps and from ~192 to ~28 pipeline processors, 13 → 9 ms median server-side (measured over 120 runs per side with alternating server restarts). Shapes with grouping modifiers (`on`, `ignoring`, `group_left`, `group_right`) and vector-matched division keep the general path; results are byte-identical to the previous emission on both analyzers, including empty operands, division by zero, NaN operands and comparison operators with `bool`. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115170 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): PromQL binary operators over operands aggregated to a single series (for example `sum(a) / sum(b)` in stat panels) are transpiled to much smaller SQL without join machinery, reducing their latency by about a third; all PromQL aggregations also emit one CTE step less.

signals.title: Add a preliminary DISTINCT to UNION DISTINCT
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115104 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114550 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115104 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114550 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `A UNION DISTINCT B` now deduplicates each branch in parallel before merging them, the same way its `SELECT DISTINCT * FROM (A UNION ALL B)` rewrite already did. Previously every row funnelled through a single `DistinctTransform`, so the query did not scale with `max_threads`. ### Description `A UNION DISTINCT B` and `SELECT DISTINCT * FROM (A UNION ALL B)` are the same query but got different pipelines: the rewrite deduplicates each branch before the merge, `UNION DISTINCT` did not. **Root cause.** The union branch of `Planner::buildPlanForUnionNode` (and its old-analyzer twin in `InterpreterSelectWithUnionQuery::buildQueryPlan`) added one `DistinctStep` with `pre_distinct = false`. `DistinctStep::getTraits` sets `returns_single_stream = !pre_distinct`, so that one step both merged to one stream and deduplicated. The `SELECT DISTINCT` path adds two steps. **The change** adds a `pre_distinct = true` step before the existing one, in both planners. `liftUpUnion` then clones it into each branch, which is how the rewrite gets its per-branch distinct. No new setting, no change to `DistinctStep` or any pass. Scoped to `UNION_DISTINCT`: `INTERSECT`/`EXCEPT DISTINCT` share the `is_distinct` branch, but `IntersectOrExceptStep` already resizes every branch to one stream and `liftUpUnion` does not handle it, so a preliminary step there is overhead. Their plans are unchanged. **Measured** (release build, 8M rows/branch, 2000 distinct values, best of 7, `query_duration_ms`): | max_threads | before | after | |---|---|---| | 1 | 60 ms | 61 ms | | 8 | 44 ms | 13 ms | | 16 | 59 ms | 9 ms | The rewrite scores 13 ms / 8 ms here, so the two forms now agree. With all-distinct data the preliminary step is overhead, at the cost the rewrite already pays. A preliminary DISTINCT keeps one hash table per stream, and this one carries the same `max_rows_in_distinct` / `max_bytes_in_distinct`, so exactly as in the rewrite those limits now bind per stream as well as globally; both overflow modes measured identical to the rewrite. The new test asserts the plan shape, not timing, and checks results against the rewrite across `Nullable`, `LowCardinality`, `Array`, aggregate-state and coerced-type branches, chains, `LIMIT`/`LIMIT BY` and size limits. <details> <summary>Interaction with #114550 (measured)</summary> #114550 "Deduplicate the final DISTINCT in parallel" attacks the same bottleneck from the other side and edits the same two functions. Measured on its head `1e783f46`, same fixture and method: | arm | t1 | t8 | t16 | |---|---|---|---| | master | 60 ms | 44 ms | 59 ms | | #114550 alone | 57 ms | 22 ms | 17 ms | | this PR alone | 61 ms | 13 ms | 9 ms | | #114550 + this PR | 60 ms | 11 ms | 7 ms | #114550 parallelizes the final dedup; this PR reduces how many rows reach it. They stack, and #114550 alone does not close the reported gap. It keeps `pre_distinct = false` at the union site, so the conflict is textual only - whoever merges second rebases. </details>

signals.title: Bound submodule cache population so it cannot kill the Config Workflow job
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114811 `Config Workflow` computes the workflow matrix, so when it dies no build and no test job is ever scheduled. On a submodule cache miss it clones 141 submodules inside its own `timeout=600` budget, and when that does not finish praktika SIGTERMs the job, silently dropping the whole matrix: the public `26.5` run at `f724d2da9360` recorded 4 checks against 102-155 on healthy commits. 7 occurrences over 7 refs in 30 days, including a release branch and three backport PRs. The function's error path is already deliberately non-fatal (`Status.OK`, cache hash left unset, dependent jobs clone from GitHub). That handler is not new here: it arrived with the cache itself in April, and a job-level SIGTERM is the one route that bypasses it. So this bounds the clone with `timeout -s KILL`, letting an overrun land in that existing handler, and sizes the job cap for its actual work: - step budget 600s, above p99 494.5s and the slowest population that currently succeeds (517s) - job cap `SUBMODULE_CACHE_POPULATE_TIMEOUT_SEC + 600`, i.e. 1200s by default, above 600 + 44 (tar and upload) + 184 (rest of the job) = 828s Deriving the cap keeps it above the step bound when that bound is overridden per repository; if the two were equal the job watchdog would fire first and re-inflict the failure above, so a test in `ci/tests/test_config_job_no_cidb.py` pins that ordering. `retries` is dropped because `Shell.check` applies `timeout` per retry, not as a total. A transient failure now costs a cache population instead of a retry: a lost population is non-fatal by design, and no retry occurred in any failing run. Verified by driving the real function both ways: a below-clone budget leaves the job alive with the hash unset, a generous one still populates the cache. YAML regeneration is byte-identical.

signals.title: Perf: Optimize PromQL histogram quantile grids
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Reduce repeated per-grid histogram state work in PromQL `histogram_quantile`. ### Summary The current PromQL lowering builds an `le` array for every input series and runs `quantilePrometheusHistogramForEach`. This repeats histogram map work for every grid position. This PR passes one scalar `le` value and the complete values grid to a new internal aggregate: ``` old: quantilePrometheusHistogramForEach(q)(le_array, values) new: quantilePrometheusHistogramArray(q)(le, values) ``` The new aggregate keeps one cumulative-value vector per bucket bound, sorts bounds once, and evaluates the complete grid from that packed state. ### What changed? - Added `quantilePrometheusHistogramArray` for PromQL lowering. - Avoided the constant `le` `arrayResize` and repeated per-position map work. - Added `Float32`, `Float64`, and nullable grid support. - Kept `-State` and `-Merge` support. - Kept the existing scalar `quantilePrometheusHistogram` aggregate unchanged. - Added memory tracking for temporary finalization arrays. ### Benchmark The performance fixture uses: - `histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[60s]))` - 400 histograms, 20 buckets, 300 samples per bucket - 2.4M input samples A direct aggregate comparison isolates aggregation work. Local arm64 run, `max_threads = 1`, three runs per case, including process startup: | Workload | Existing `ForEach` | Packed grid | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 2,000 histograms, 12M values | 2.72 s | 0.82 s | **3.3x faster** | | 4,000 histograms, 24M values | 1.44 s | 0.70 s | **2.1x faster** | Fixture: `tests/performance/promql_histogram_quantile.xml`. ### Correctness and validation Coverage includes Float32/Float64, nullable and different-length arrays, an empty first row, NaN or missing bounds, missing `+Inf`, and serialized `-State/-Merge` results. Also validated: - focused aggregate translation unit with `-Werror`; - stateless query output against the reference; - direct aggregate and merge output; - Python syntax for the integration test; - `git diff --check`. ### Notes This aggregate is internal and is only emitted by the PromQL converter. This overlaps with #114704 in the histogram quantile lowering area. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115199&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115199](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115199+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: PromQL/TimeSeries: optimize vectorized two-input tag transformations
signals.text: ### Description This removes one unnecessary pair hash lookup per row from vectorized two-input TimeSeries tag transformations. `transformTags2(groups1, groups2, ...)` is used by `timeSeriesCopyTag` and `timeSeriesCopyTags`. PromQL `group_left` and `group_right` use these functions when labels are copied during vector matching. The old code transformed each unique `(group1, group2)` pair once, then walked every input row again and rebuilt the pair key to find the result slot. The new code stores that compact slot during the first pass and remaps all slots to final groups after tag registration. It also uses `try_emplace` and keeps the pair map sparse. The pair deduplication and final-tag deduplication behavior is unchanged, including cases where different input pairs produce the same final tags. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry Avoid repeated pair hash lookups in vectorized two-input TimeSeries tag transformations. #### Correctness coverage - Added vectorized `timeSeriesCopyTag` coverage with repeated input pairs. - Added vectorized `timeSeriesCopyTags` coverage where different input pairs collapse to the same final tag group. - Sorted the multi-result `groupUniqArray` assertions so they do not depend on hash-table iteration order. #### Benchmark coverage - 200,000 unique pairs over 2,000,000 rows. - 32 repeated pairs over 20,000,000 rows and 100 blocks. - PromQL aggregation plus `group_left` and `group_right` workloads. The standalone loop benchmark over 200,000 rows showed the following results: | Unique input pairs | Before | After | Speedup | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 0.74 ms | 0.67 ms | **1.10x** | | 10,000 | 1.23 ms | 1.06 ms | **1.16x** | | 200,000 | 7.44 ms | 6.84 ms | **1.09x** | Each result is the median of 5 process runs. Each process warmed up for 3 rounds and measured 9 samples for each implementation. #### Validation - `git diff --check` - `xmllint --noout tests/performance/promql_tags_transform.xml` - Focused vectorized TimeSeries queries using the available ClickHouse binary - C++ syntax compilation for `ContextTimeSeriesTagsCollector.cpp` <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115200&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115200](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115200+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115061 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `Build profile diff` failed on #115061 with a message naming only the `gh` argv ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115061&sha=9a8c54a155a55828cef1e38c76a31aca80038099&name_0=PR&name_1=Build%20profile%20diff), [job log](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/runs/32027518805/job/95431729878)): ``` CalledProcessError: Command '['gh', 'api', 'repos/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/commits?sha=a3f55f04… ``` Two things discarded the reason. `_list_commits_page` used `check=True`, and `CalledProcessError.__str__` renders only argv, so the captured `stderr`/`stdout` carrying the HTTP status were never read. The message then went through `md_code`, a table-cell *name* formatter (`MAX_NAME_LEN = 100`), which cut the tail. So 404, 403 and 5xx produced the same 102-character string, and the walk makes up to 60 calls without naming which one failed. Report it instead: exit code and endpoint first, then `stderr` and `stdout` each capped at 300 characters with an elision marker, in the field order `GH.get_output_with_retries` uses. `TimeoutExpired` is caught in the same place. `timeout=120` is kept deliberately - `gh` bounds connect and TLS handshake but not a stalled response body (measured 240 s unbounded), so the shared praktika helper, which passes no timeout, would unbound a bounded call site. `md_message` is added beside `md_code` for the comment path, bounded head+tail so the end of a message survives. `md_code` and `MAX_NAME_LEN` are untouched, so its 17 name callers are byte-identical. The bound matters beyond `gh`: a cluster query failure reaches the same handler carrying its whole inlined SQL, measured at 54952 characters against GitHub's 65536 limit. The `gh api` failure itself is environmental and out of scope: the byte-identical call succeeds 25 times out of 25 by hand. Validated with a throwaway harness, 30 assertions plus three mutation arms each reverting one hunk: 404, 403 and 5xx give three distinct messages where they gave one, and the success path, the `extend_master_shas` fail-close and the single-attempt contract are unchanged. `ci/tests/`: 711 passed, its 2 failures pre-existing on master. No committed test, per `.claude/CLAUDE.md`: `ci/tests/test_build_profile_diff_job.py` was removed in #114675. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115201&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115201](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115201+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Sum the adaptive aggregation seal normalization assertion over the three arms
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115034 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115034 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `04676_adaptive_aggregation_replicated_argument`, which I added in #115034, is flaky: as of 2026-08-17 20:00 UTC it had failed 22 times across 22 unrelated pull requests against 1341 passes, roughly 1.6%, and it is still firing. Every failure is one of three assertion lines flipping `1` to `0`, for example `+normalized nullable 0`. [Sample report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108431&sha=61e924073e8505f78ac3e3438e2a180a07c740df&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_debug%2C%20distributed%20plan%2C%20s3%20storage%2C%20parallel%29) (`Stateless tests (amd_debug, distributed plan, s3 storage, parallel)` on #108431). The test asserted `AdaptiveAggregationSealNormalizations > 0` separately for each of its three argument representations. That counter fires in `Aggregator::sealPendingChunks` only when the batches one producer buffered together disagree at an argument position, which needs two batches buffered in one producer, both representations reachable, and one producer holding blocks of both kinds. The test pins only the second; the others are a read pool decision and thread scheduling, so a non-zero count for a single query is not an engine guarantee. Randomization is not the cause: it also reproduces with randomization off and with `enable_lazy_columns_replication 0`. This sums the counter over the three arms instead, which is the property the engine does guarantee, and changes nothing else. The three queries stay separate, so each keeps its own value comparison and its own abort site; the `sealed chunks` assertion, the six value lines and the tags are untouched. Within one run the test no longer proves that every representation reached the normalization. `04654` already asserts the sibling `AdaptiveAggregationSealedChunks` in aggregate. Validation: in one interleaved loop the old form failed twice while the new form passed 300 of 300. Of 600 runs, 6 had an arm at zero and all 6 still had a non-zero total. With #115034's fix reverted the new form aborts 20 of 20 with `Bad cast from type DB::ColumnReplicated to DB::ColumnVector` in `sealPendingChunks`. 50 runs with randomized settings and 50 without both pass. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115204&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115204](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115204+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Perf: optimize PromQL dropMetricName for fixed metric names
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113721 **Description** `dropMetricName` currently runs a `GROUP BY`, `any(values)`, and duplicate-series check every time it removes `__name__`. For a selector with an equality matcher on `__name__`, all input series have the same metric name. Input groups are already unique, so removing that tag is injective. The extra aggregation and duplicate check cannot find a collision in this case. **Implementation** - Track a conservative `metric_name_is_constant` flag from `__name__` equality matchers. - Carry it through range functions, offsets, subqueries, unary operators, simple vector functions, and label updates that do not rewrite `__name__`. - Clear it when `__name__` is rewritten, dropped, or converted to a scalar. - Use projection-only subqueries in `dropMetricName` when the flag is true. - Keep the existing duplicate-series path for regex, negative matchers, and rewritten metric names. This is separate from [#113721](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113721). That PR handles PromQL unary-negation collisions between different metric names. This PR only skips work when such a collision is impossible, and leaves the strict duplicate-series behavior unchanged for all other cases. **Tests** - Added stateless coverage for fixed metric names, simple vector functions, offsets, regex matchers, and `label_replace`. - Compiled all changed PromQL translation units with clang. - Ran `git diff --check`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Optimize PromQL metric-name dropping for selectors with a fixed metric name. **Benchmark** Raw SQL benchmark for the generated `dropMetricName` subqueries on Apple arm64 with ClickHouse 26.8.1.1. Each query generated 100,000 unique groups, used `max_threads = 1` and `FORMAT Null`, and was run 30 times: | Path | Median | p90 | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Projection-only | 0.087 s/query | 0.091 s/query | | Duplicate-check | 0.140 s/query | 0.162 s/query | The projection-only path is 1.61x faster, with 38% lower median latency. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115206&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115206](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115206+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
