signals.title: Perf: Optimize PromQL or for exact groups
signals.text: ## What changed - add a fast path for the PromQL set operator `or` - use it when both inputs already match on the original `group` column - send those inputs directly to the existing `FULL ALL JOIN` merge - keep `on(...)`, non-empty `ignoring(...)`, `on()`, and other transformed matching keys on the current general path - treat empty `ignoring()` like default matching when both groups are already exact ## Why this is safe `VECTOR_GRID` guarantees one row per `group`. The fast path is enabled only when `transformGroupASTForBinaryOperator()` returns the bare `group` identifier on both sides, so the matching key is already unique and exact. This includes normal matching and empty `ignoring()` after both inputs have already dropped `__name__`. `on(...)`, `on()`, non-empty `ignoring(...)`, and other transformed matching keys keep the existing general path. The general `or` path currently reads the left grid for a `countForEach` aggregation and then reads it again for the final merge. The fast path removes that aggregation, the RHS masking join, the materialized left CTE, and the second left-grid read. The final merge still uses the existing element-wise left-side preference for overlapping samples. ## Benchmark These benchmarks use the same **8,000-series / 300-sample** workload. Higher QPS means higher throughput for the same query. ### End-to-end PromQL Setup: `tests/performance/promql_set_operators.xml`, **10 measured runs** per server. | Query | Baseline | Patch | Relative | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | exact-group `or` | 146.8 ms | 128.9 ms | **1.14x speedup (-12.2%)** | | exact-group `or`, repeat | 157.6 ms | 134.5 ms | **1.17x speedup (-14.7%)** | | `or on(instance)` control | 143.9 ms | 145.9 ms | **0.99x (1.4% slower)** | | `or on(instance)` control, repeat | 155.5 ms | 158.1 ms | **0.98x (1.7% slower)** | The exact-group case is **1.14x to 1.17x faster** across the two runs. The control stayed within noise. ### Focused SQL lowering Setup: persistent server, **20 measured runs**, `max_threads=4`, **8,000 rows / 4,000 groups / 300-step arrays**. | Workload | General full lowering | Exact full merge | Relative | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Full lowering | 28.1 QPS | 56.5 QPS | **2.01x throughput (+101%)** | Both forms returned **1,128,000** present samples. ## Tests - add grouped `or` coverage where both sides have already dropped `__name__`, including empty `ignoring()` - cover different missing timestamps and compare the result with Prometheus - add `tests/performance/promql_set_operators.xml` with an exact-group query and an `or on(instance)` control - document that the merge helper expects unique `VECTOR_GRID` groups ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): PromQL `or` expressions with an exact group key skip redundant matching stages and generate smaller SQL.

signals.title: Remove a duplicate decimal rescaling helper that did not check for overflow
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114886 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a signed integer overflow when a `Decimal` argument passed to `prometheusQuery` or `prometheusQueryRange` had to be rescaled to the table's timestamp scale. Such an argument returned an unrelated timestamp, or made the query attempt a huge allocation, instead of reporting `DECIMAL_OVERFLOW`. ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer, check `AST fuzzer (arm_asan_ubsan)`, STID `3715-3c49` ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109480&sha=480e82b8b2a16cdfa145b984a2270ef95cf3d518&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%29)): ``` src/Core/DecimalFunctions.h:444:55: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 9007199254740990976 * 1000000 cannot be represented in type 'long' ``` Reached from ordinary table-function argument parsing. Root cause is duplication rather than a missing check. `DecimalUtils::convertTo(to_scale, decimal, scale)` was a second implementation of decimal-to-decimal rescaling and the weaker of the two: it multiplied by the scale multiplier with a plain `*`, and narrowed through `Decimal::convertTo` (a bare `static_cast`) before multiplying. `convertDecimals` already did this correctly, promoting to the wider native type first, guarding the multiply with `common::mulOverflow`, and range-checking when narrowing. `FunctionsConversion.h` and `KeyCondition.cpp` both document no-wrap as this helper's contract, so the unguarded overload was the outlier. It is removed here and its four call sites go through `convertDecimals`, making the `src/` diff a net reduction. Without the fix a release build silently returns a wrapped timestamp (`toDecimal64(10000000000, 3)` against a `DateTime64(9)` table gives `1702-05-02 18:12:06.290448384`); for `prometheusQueryRange` the wrapped bounds inflate the step count until the query attempts an 8 GiB allocation. Validation: the UBSan abort reproduces on master and is gone after the change; 12 in-range values covering all three scale directions, both source widths and the exact `Int64` boundary are byte-identical before and after; new test `04926`. Known residual, not addressed here: `common::mulOverflow` does not detect `Int128`/`Int256` overflow (`base/base/arithmeticOverflow.h` says so), so a `Decimal128` rescale can still wrap. That is pre-existing, unreachable from these call sites (all `Int64`-native), and not regressed here. signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115163 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Requested by @ thevar1able in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115163#issuecomment-5318430318: `Build profile diff` ran on changes involving no builds. His PR changes only `utils/exclude-authors.txt`, yet the job ran, found no profile data for the head and posted nothing. `digest_config` answers two questions: which changed files affect a job, and may its result be reused. `4e62df6112628621` gave this job a focused digest; `e64133b542327753` removed it to stop a cache hit skipping the job, whose output is a comment about one concrete commit. That also made the job always affected, and `only_docs` in `filter_job.py` compensated for docs-only diffs only. This splits the two. `Job.Config` gains `enable_cache` (default True, and in `drop_fields`, so no existing job's digest changes), honoured at both cache seams. The job gets its focused digest back plus `enable_cache=False`: the digest decides whether to run it, the flag keeps every selected run running. Whether the build can produce data for this head arrives through `requires=["Build (arm_release)"]`, covering the build's sources, submodules, docker image and packaging. `only_docs` and its gate are deleted. Side effect: no longer always affected, the job stops rescuing `Build (arm_release)`, so that build is skipped on build-free diffs too. Those two jobs are the whole newly-skipped set, and this already happens on the `only_docs` path today. `Generate LLVM Coverage Diff Report`, asked about in the same comment, has no such hole: it is a `Result` inside `llvm_coverage_job.py`, already gated on build affectedness. One pre-existing limitation is widened, not fixed: a skip and a cache hit look identical to the runner, so the comment writer does not run on a skip and the comment can outlive the head it describes. That already holds for docs-only PRs. Verified: `ci/tests/` passes, `praktika yaml` produces no diff, every job's config digest is byte-identical, and each new assertion reddens under a mutation. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115221&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115221](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115221+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: PromQL/TimeSeries: materialize tags only for unique groups
signals.text: ## What changed - collect unique group IDs before looking up their tags - materialize and transform tags once per unique group - keep the existing dense and sparse group mapping paths - remap all rows back to the transformed groups ## Why The vectorized `transformTags()` path looked up tags for every input row before deduplicating group IDs. Repeated rows therefore created repeated tag entries even though the transformation only needed to run once per group. This change deduplicates the group IDs first, then looks up and transforms tags only for those unique groups. The existing first-seen ordering and row remap stay the same. ## Tests - add repeated dense group coverage with row order - add repeated sparse group coverage with row order - run the new queries against the existing ClickHouse local binary ## Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ## Changelog entry: Avoid repeated tag materialization for duplicate group IDs in vectorized TimeSeries transformations.
signals.author: fallintoplace

signals.title: Perf: use compact presence masks for PromQL set operators
signals.text: ## Summary The PromQL `and`, `or`, and `unless` lowering only needs to know whether a value is present at each step. The compact presence mask is now built with: ```sql groupBitOrForEach(arrayMap(x -> isNotNull(x), values)) ``` Because `isNotNull()` produces a `UInt8` 0/1 value, bitwise OR is exactly the presence reduction needed by the set operators. The aggregate state is a zero-initialized `UInt8`, avoiding the generic `max(UInt8)` initialized-state bookkeeping. ## What changed - Use `Array(UInt8)` presence masks instead of `Array(UInt64)` counts. - Use `groupBitOrForEach` for the per-step presence reduction. - Share the mask expression between `and`, `or`, and `unless`. - Keep the existing NULL filtering and join behavior. - Cover all three operators in the plan-shape test. - Keep the original 8,000-series baseline workload. - Add a sparse fan-in workload with 1,000 matching groups and four physical replicas per group, with `replica` excluded by `on(instance)`. This targets the general set-operator path. The exact-group fast path is separate. ## Checks - Verified that `groupBitOr` is registered for integer inputs and that the `ForEach` combinator accepts array arguments. - Updated the plan-shape checks for `and`, `or`, and `unless` to require `groupBitOrForEach` and reject `countForEach`. - Existing end-to-end set-operator coverage continues to exercise mixed, NULL, and missing-step behavior. ## Benchmark The checked-in workload contains two variants, each using 300 query steps: - Baseline: 8,000 series with one series per matching group. - Sparse fan-in: 8,000 series with four replicas per matching group and staggered 50% sample presence. Queries match on `instance` while retaining `replica` in the physical labels. The second variant exercises the actual per-step presence reduction across multiple rows in each `on(...)` group. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Use compact presence masks for PromQL set operators.

signals.title: CI: report why the LLVM coverage diff report was not generated
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112832 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112832 (touches the same files, so expect a merge conflict; it is not a fix for this) ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `ci/jobs/scripts/generate_diff_coverage_report.sh` produces no report directory in four cases: no coverable C/C++ files changed, no coverage data for the changed files, current coverage empty for them, and a hard failure under `set -euo pipefail`. `llvm_coverage_job.py` inferred all four from one bit, `_diff_report_dir.exists()`, and reported three of them as "No C/C++ source files changed" at three sites. Two are green runs where C/C++ files did change, so the job states the opposite of what happened. On a tool failure it also set the `Print Uncovered Code` sub-result to `OK` for analysis that never ran. Observed on PR #115101, which changed `src/Functions/array/arrayAUC.cpp`: the `gh api` compare call returned `gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)`, and the job made both false claims. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115101&sha=c00b1800c1fcae2cb2138af592a9b3e79b4c8275&name_0=PR&name_1=LLVM%20Coverage The script now names its outcome in `ci/tmp/diff_outcome.txt` before every `exit 0`, and the job reports the outcome it is told plus the script's exit status. It also drops a false claim that "LBC analysis will run separately" when current coverage is empty (`print_uncovered_code.py` reads only `current.changed.info`, empty in that state), and echoes each `gh api` compare endpoint, since `gh` reports a failure as a bare `HTTP 404` naming no resource. A script failure still stays RED, and no currently-green outcome becomes red. One behavioural change beyond the labels: `print_uncovered_code.py` now runs only for the two outcomes that produced this run's own coverage slice, so the others cannot report an earlier run's numbers. This does not fix the 404, which looks environmental: replaying both compare calls with 25 victims' own commit values gave 25/25 success, and OK and FAIL runs interleave in the same hours. `ci/tests/test_llvm_coverage_gate.py` grows from 12 to 70 cases: one per outcome, a harness running the real script under stubbed tools, and cases executing the job's own call site and each dispatch it selects. 48 fail on master. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115225&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115225](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115225+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Name the join algorithms that were tried in the "can't execute" error
signals.text: When no enabled join algorithm can run a JOIN, the planner threw: ``` Can't execute any of specified algorithms for specified strictness/kind and right storage type ``` It named neither the algorithms that were tried nor the JOIN that failed, even though both are available at the throw site. Setting `join_algorithm` to something narrower for memory reasons and then writing an `ASOF JOIN` left you with nothing to act on. It now reads: ``` None of the algorithms enabled by the 'join_algorithm' setting [grace_hash] can execute this ASOF INNER JOIN with the given right table storage type ``` Algorithm names are printed through `SettingFieldJoinAlgorithmTraits::toString` rather than `toString(JoinAlgorithm)`. The latter returns the uppercase enum spelling, `GRACE_HASH`, which the setting parser rejects, so the names in the message can now be pasted straight back into `join_algorithm`. The message deliberately does not list the algorithms that would work. `tryCreateJoin` has no capability table, the rules live implicitly across its per algorithm branches, so naming them here would add a copy of knowledge that is already in the documentation and would rot quietly the next time an algorithm gains or loses support. Also updates a comment in `02242_join_rocksdb.sql` that quoted the old wording. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): When no join algorithm enabled by the `join_algorithm` setting can execute a `JOIN`, the error message now names the algorithms that were tried and the strictness and kind of the JOIN that failed, instead of reporting only that none of them worked.

signals.title: Do not use the trivial count optimization when the aggregate argument contains arrayJoin
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115123 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115123 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results for `SELECT count(arrayJoin(arr))` with the default `optimize_trivial_count_query = 1`. The stored row count was returned instead of the number of array elements, and on `file()` and `url()` the query returned `0`. Also fixed with `enable_analyzer = 0`, where a constant argument such as `count(arrayJoin([10, 20]))` was affected. Closes #115123. ### Description Requested by @ PedroTadim on the issue (["the fix for this seems small. Can you do it?"](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115123#issuecomment-5315767329)); reported by @ konsta-danyliuk. `applyTrivialCountIfPossible` replaces the whole table read with the stored row counter. It checks that the aggregate is `count` by type, then never inspects `count`'s argument. `arrayJoin` multiplies rows above the source read, so the aggregate observes `sum(length(arr))` rows rather than `totalRows()`, and the expansion is dropped along with the read. Measured on 3 rows / 6 elements: `count(arrayJoin(A))` returned `3` instead of `6`. The fix refuses the optimization when the argument contains `arrayJoin`, using the same `hasFunctionNode(..., "arrayJoin")` guard six sibling optimizations already use for this property. The guard sits **before** `select_query_info.optimize_trivial_count = true`: for `file()`, `url()` and object storage `totalRows()` is `nullopt`, so the function returns `false`, but the flag has already been written and those storages count in `read()`, so they returned `0`. Placing the guard after the flag write fixes MergeTree while leaving `file()` at `0`, so the test asserts the `file()` value too. The old analyzer decides trivial count in `TreeRewriter`, so it needs its own guard: one clause on the existing query-shape filter, alongside the `GROUP BY` / `HAVING` / `FINAL` disqualifiers, covering both of its eligibility paths. It compares the canonical function name, so `arrayJoin` and its registered alias are recognised regardless of `normalize_function_names`. With `normalize_function_names = 0` the alias is not executable on the old analyzer at all - every shape I tried throws `FUNCTION_IS_SPECIAL` on unpatched master, independently of this optimization - so declining surfaces that existing error instead of a silent row count. Not bundled: rewriting `count(arrayJoin(A))` to `sum(A.size0)` would be faster, but that is an optimization on top of a wrong-results fix. <details><summary>Carriers and over-guard checks (measured, base vs patched)</summary> Fixture: 3 rows, `sum(length(A))` = 6. | case | base | patched | |---|---|---| | `count(arrayJoin(A))` on MergeTree | 3 | 6 | | `count(unnest(A))` (alias) | 3 | 6 | | `count(arrayJoin(A) + 1)`, `arrayJoin(arrayMap(...))` (nested) | 3 | 6 | | `count(arrayJoin(arrayJoin([A,B])))` | 3 | 11 | | `count(arrayJoin(A))` on `file()` / `url()` | **0** | 6 | | `count(arrayJoin(M))` Map / `(T)` Array(Tuple) | 3 | 5 | | `count(arrayJoin(LC))` Array(LowCardinality) | 3 | 7 | | `count(arrayJoin(A))` via `remote()` | 3 | 6 | | `count(arrayJoin(A))` ReplacingMergeTree FINAL | 6 | 6 | | `count(arrayJoin([10,20]))`, `enable_analyzer = 0` | 3 | 6 | | `count(arrayJoin([n,n]))` partitioned, `analyzer = 0` | 3 | 6 | Object storage reads the same flag at `StorageObjectStorage.cpp:720`, so it takes the `file()`/`url()` path; with no S3 endpoint here that row is read from the code, not measured. Unchanged, and asserted so: `count()`, `count(*)`, `count(1)`, `count(n)`, `count(nullable)`, `ARRAY JOIN` as a clause, `countIf(arrayJoin(...))`, `count(DISTINCT arrayJoin(...))`, the sparsity-filter sibling, and a `count()` whose unrelated subquery contains `arrayJoin` (both visitors stop at nested query nodes). Controls: rejecting any non-empty argument list flips `count(n)` off the optimization; moving the planner guard below the flag write fails the `file()` arm alone; guarding only the first old-analyzer path fails the partitioned arm alone. Every stateless test referencing `optimize_trivial_count` was run, including those combining it with `enable_analyzer = 0`. The only failures need a dataset or a listener this sandbox cannot provide (`test.hits`, `127.0.0.2:9000`) and fail identically on unpatched master. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115227&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115227](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115227+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix the Upgrade check silently validating against a stale previous release
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description The Upgrade check starts a previous release, then upgrades to the build under test. `tests/ci/get_previous_release_tag.py` picks that baseline, and can silently pick one far too old. On PR #114376 commit `e1cb0dee5e9` it picked `v25.1.4.53` for a `26.8.1.1` build; that old server aborted on shutdown, reported as `Received signal 6` unrelated to the PR. Two commits earlier it resolved `v26.7.3.19`. 4 of 47 recent runs were affected. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114376&sha=e1cb0dee5e9bd972e9bbbdd8cd8d971ad1e39ee1&name_0=PR&name_1=Upgrade%20check%20%28amd_release%29 Root cause: when no candidate on a page could be used, an unbounded `while not found:` advanced to page 2, 3 and answered from there. `/releases` returns entries roughly newest-created first, not in version order, and each later page's newest release is older than the previous page's newest (measured across all 9 pages), so page 1 holds the newest release overall. The only diagnostic was `logger.debug` under `basicConfig(level=INFO)`. This resolves from the first page only. A candidate still needs an uploaded package, so a release whose packages are still publishing keeps falling back to the previous patch release, now logged at WARNING rather than DEBUG. Three cases now raise: a first page with no usable candidate, a page shorter than the 100 requested, and an answer that is its page's oldest entry, which cannot show that no newer release precedes it. `upgrade_runner.sh` turns those nonzero exits into a job failure. No C++ change is needed: the abort is a use-after-free in `25.1`, fixed in `2920d338ea4` (#81473, released in `v25.6.1.3206`), so master and every active release branch carry the fix. The resolver had no tests. The new ones sit under `ci/tests/`, the only tree the CI Tests job collects, per the `test_download_release_packages.py` precedent, and the resolver joins the cache digest of both jobs using it. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112974 (hardens the API helper; edits the same digest list, so whichever merges second rebases). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115228&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115228](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115228+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not build statistics for non-physical columns
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114791 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK` on every `INSERT` into a table that declares `STATISTICS(...)` on an `ALIAS` or `EPHEMERAL` column, which made such tables read-only. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114791 `CREATE TABLE t (a UInt64, b UInt64 ALIAS a + 1 STATISTICS(basic)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY a` is accepted, and then every `INSERT` fails `Code: 10 ... Not found column b in block`, so the table is read-only. `materialize_statistics_on_insert` defaulting to `true` in 26.8 exposed it. **Root cause.** The `ColumnsStatistics` constructor collects every column with a non-empty statistics description without checking how the column is stored, and the insert path builds those with `build`, which does `block.getByName`. An `ALIAS` column is computed on read and never appears in the written block, so the lookup always throws. Merges use `buildIfExists` and skip absent columns, which is why they kept working. Such statistics are already unsupported in `addImplicitStatistics` and `ALTER ... ADD STATISTICS`. **The change.** Exclude non-physical columns where statistics are collected, deriving the property from the column's default kind. `build` stays strict, because its type-mismatch check is a deliberate diagnostic. A newly issued `MATERIALIZE STATISTICS <col>` naming such a column is still rejected before enqueue. An already queued one instead skips the column, so a command persisted by a pre-upgrade server drains rather than retrying forever inside the background task; the skip does not need the statistics description to survive, which also covers a column carrying only implicit `auto_statistics_types` entries that the same `ALTER` drops. `ALL` skips such a column and stays usable. **Deliberately unchanged.** The declaration stays accepted but inert: every candidate rejection site is also the ATTACH/startup or replica-addition path, so a check there would stop existing affected tables from loading. `DROP STATISTICS` stays permissive and recovers such a table. Validated by writing an affected table with a pre-fix binary and loading it with the fixed one. The drain is covered by `02864_statistics_ddl` under the default analyzer and `test_mutations_analyzer_override` under the old one. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115231&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115231](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115231+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: CI: do not authenticate an unused robot token in the Codex code review
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113059 The `Code Review` job died on `gh auth login` for 10 pull requests in the 24 h to 2026-08-17, losing the automated review for those heads. A fork PR cannot re-run it, so recovery needs a fresh push. ``` ERROR: Codex review failed after 3 attempts: CalledProcessError: Command '['gh', 'auth', 'login', '--with-token']' returned non-zero exit status 1. ``` - report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113059&sha=83188f6442a4f2d7e4376efe54c2bf3bad32dd50&name_0=PR&name_1=Code%20Review - log: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/PRs/113059/83188f6442a4f2d7e4376efe54c2bf3bad32dd50/code_review/job.log `_run_codex_once` authenticated a robot token before every attempt, under `check=True`, but the Codex backend never uses it: `enable_gh_auth=True` has the runner authenticate the app up front, and the prompt runs every agent `gh` call with `GH_CONFIG_DIR` unset. Across the 25 job logs that reached the agent, 246 of 246 executed `gh` calls unset it and none used the scoped robot directory, so that login could only fail the job. In those same logs `/ci/robot-ch-test-poll-copilot` answered `HTTP 401: Bad credentials` on 27 of 27 attempts, the oldest on 2026-08-03, and `/ci/robot-ch-test-poll-1-copilot` never did. Two robots over three attempts rotate as `[X, Y, X]`, so the healthy one gets a single attempt when the shuffle puts the dead one first, and one transient GraphQL 503 there fails the job. This removes that login and its temporary `GH_CONFIG_DIR` from the Codex attempt, so it runs on the app identity it already used and retries serve agent failures. `_run_copilot_once` keeps its login, which the Copilot CLI does use. signals.title: Improve the performance of `MODIFY TTL`
signals.text: `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY TTL` currently rewrites every part of the table, which on a large table means reading and writing all of its data just to change when rows expire. Very often the new TTL is the old one shifted in time - the retention period is extended or shortened, e.g. `create_time + INTERVAL 300 DAY` becomes `create_time + INTERVAL 10 DAY`. In that case every row's expiry time moves by the same constant number of seconds, so the parts do not have to be rewritten at all: it is enough to shift the expiry timestamps ClickHouse already stores per part. This pull request adds that fast path, and the result for the user is that such a `MODIFY TTL` completes almost instantly instead of taking minutes or hours: ```sql CREATE TABLE test_fast_ttl (`id` UInt32, `name` String, `create_time` DateTime) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id TTL create_time + toIntervalDay(300); INSERT INTO test_fast_ttl SELECT number, 'AAA', date_sub(day, 100, now()) from numbers(100000000); -- Before ALTER TABLE test_fast_ttl MODIFY TTL create_time + INTERVAL 10 DAY; -- 0 rows in set. Elapsed: 25.564 sec. -- After ALTER TABLE test_fast_ttl MODIFY TTL create_time + INTERVAL 10 DAY; -- 0 rows in set. Elapsed: 0.046 sec. ``` There is nothing to enable and no new syntax: the optimization is applied automatically inside the `MATERIALIZE TTL` mutation that `MODIFY TTL` already produces, and a plain `ALTER TABLE ... MATERIALIZE TTL` benefits from it as well. The observable result is exactly the same as before - the same rows expire and the parts end up with the same TTL bounds - only the work is avoided. Per part, the mutation now does one of the following: - the part is fully expired under the new TTL - it is replaced with an empty part; - no row of the part is expired yet - the part is cloned (its data files hardlinked) and only its stored TTL bounds are shifted; - otherwise - the part is rewritten exactly as before. The fast path is only taken when it is provably equivalent to the rewrite. It requires that the unconditional rows TTL (`TTL <expr>`) is the only TTL of the table, and that the old and the new TTL are the same date/time column shifted by constant fixed-length intervals, so that `new_ttl(row) - old_ttl(row)` is one constant for every row. Calendar `MONTH`/`YEAR` intervals, `DAY`/`WEEK` intervals in a time zone with daylight saving time, and row-dependent expressions are all rejected. The proof is redone for each part against the TTL expression (and time zone) that the part's stored timestamps were actually computed under, so a part that lags the table metadata, or was written by an older server, falls back to the regular rewrite rather than being shifted unsoundly. The same applies to the boundary cases of the stored timestamps themselves: a part containing a row whose TTL timestamp is exactly `1970-01-01 00:00:00` UTC (which ClickHouse treats as "no TTL"), a shift that would move some timestamp onto that value, and a part whose stored TTL is already fully expired (which the regular rewrite drops wholesale, even when the new TTL is longer) all take the regular rewrite. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY TTL` no longer rewrites the table's data when the new TTL is the old one shifted by a constant amount of time (the same date/time column plus fixed-length intervals), which is the common case of extending or shortening the retention period. Fully expired parts are replaced with empty ones and the rest are cloned with only their stored TTL metadata shifted, which makes such an `ALTER` nearly instant. Cases where the shift is not provably constant - calendar month/year intervals, day/week intervals in a time zone with daylight saving time, or row-dependent TTL expressions - fall back to the regular rewrite. `ALTER TABLE ... MATERIALIZE TTL` benefits from the same optimization. <!--- Directly edit documentation source files in the "docs" folder with the same pull-request as code changes or Add a user-readable short description of the changes that should be added to docs.clickhouse.com below. signals.title: Mongo queries (wire protocol + dialect)
signals.text: Adds two ways to run MongoDB queries against ClickHouse: - a **wire protocol endpoint** (`mongo_port`), so MongoDB drivers and tools such as `pymongo` and `mongosh` can connect to ClickHouse as if it were a MongoDB server; - a **query dialect** (`SET dialect = 'mongo'`), so MongoDB shell syntax can be sent over the usual ClickHouse interfaces. A Mongo database maps onto a ClickHouse database, a collection onto a table, a document onto a row, and a nested field onto an `a.b` column. A collection created by the first `insert` gets one column per field of the first inserted document. The supported commands are `insert`, `find`, `count`, `update`, `delete`, `create`, `drop`, `createIndexes`, `listDatabases`, `listCollections`, `isMaster` and `saslStart`; only the `PLAIN` authentication mechanism is supported, because it is the only one that provides the cleartext password ClickHouse needs. Both are experimental and cover a subset of MongoDB. They are meant for pointing an existing MongoDB application at ClickHouse without rewriting its queries, not as a MongoDB replacement. The limitations are listed in `docs/en/interfaces/mongo.md`. Task: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/58394 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a MongoDB-compatible wire protocol endpoint (the `mongo_port` server setting) and a MongoDB query dialect (`SET dialect = 'mongo'`) for basic collection operations.

signals.title: Fix: max_execution_timeout_leaf with parallel replicas
signals.text: `max_execution_time_leaf` and `timeout_overflow_mode_leaf` settings are now effective for queries with parallel replicas. The optimization is deliberately conservative. signals.title: Cascades cost-based optimizer for distributed query plans
signals.text: A Cascades-style cost-based optimizer that chooses distribution strategies for the multi-stage distributed query plans of #106020. It explores alternatives in a memo (a shared store of equivalent plan fragments) with top-down, goal-directed search and picks the cheapest plan satisfying the required distribution and sorting properties, inserting exchange operators (plan steps that move rows between nodes) as needed. Implemented: - **Join strategies**: shuffle hash join, broadcast hash join (with `ReplicatedRead` — every worker repeats the same read of a small table instead of a network broadcast, assuming shared storage where all workers see the same data), replicated join (a small deterministic join is recomputed identically on every node over such reads, so its result never crosses the network; nested joins compose; `ANY` joins are excluded because the kept row depends on the build order), local join. - **Aggregation strategies**: two-phase (partial + merge), shuffle by group keys, local; `distributed_aggregation_memory_efficient` and `distributed_plan_force_shuffle_aggregation` are honored. - **Top-N**: two-stage distributed top-N (per-node bounded sort, sorted-merge gather, coordinator limit); disabled under `exact_rows_before_limit`, which needs the full row count. - **Read strategies**: parallel N-way read, replicated read, local read. For `FINAL`, #108148 (already in master) taught the rule-based distributed plan to split a `FINAL` read into disjoint primary-key-range buckets where that is safe; Cascades now reuses that machinery, so `FINAL` no longer forces a serial read here either. The coordinator ships each bucket's marks in the `read_bucket` task parameters. - **`IN (subquery)`**: follows the `rewrite_in_to_join` setting like the rest of the planner (the forced join form is removed). In the default set form the set-building subqueries are planned separately and distributed like any other query. - **Properties and enforcers**: distribution (node count, replication, partitioning columns with equivalence classes and the types the keys are cast to before hashing) and sorting; when a plan alternative lacks a required property, an enforcer inserts the step that provides it (`Gather`/`Shuffle`/`Broadcast`/`ScatterExchange`, `Sort`). - **Transformations**: join commutativity (only for semantics-preserving joins: `INNER ALL`, `CROSS`, `SEMI`/`ANY`/`ANTI`; never `ASOF`, and never `ANY` under `join_any_take_last_row`), two-phase aggregation split, two-stage top-N split. - **Cost model**: `work`, `network`, and `sequential` components, each priced as wall-clock per node: a shuffle moves 1/N of the data per node, a broadcast payload is ingested once by every receiver in parallel, and a gather funnels every row through one endpoint, so its transfer stays undivided and pays a per-row cost. A hash-table build counts as parallel work (`parallel_hash` shards it across threads); a fixed per-exchange overhead keeps small inputs local. A table read is priced on its scan volume - the rows the primary key keeps - not on its output estimate, so a filter off the sorting key cannot make a replicated re-read look free. Standalone filters (e.g. `HAVING`) are estimated from column NDVs with join-key equivalence classes; join estimates are clamped to join kind and strictness semantics; exchange costs use per-row byte widths measured from the parts' column sizes (followed through renames, not derived from types). All weights and calibration constants are overridable at query time. What this improves over the rule-based distributed planner, on TPC-H plans. The rule-based planner broadcasts a small table when its read is below `distributed_plan_max_rows_to_broadcast`, but it often cannot size the result of a join, so a small join result (`nation x region`, 5 rows after the region filter) is scattered across nodes, joined there, and shuffled again (repartitioned across nodes) by the next join key. It also often inserts a shuffle at join and aggregation boundaries even when the rows are already divided by the right key. Cascades estimates sizes through joins, knows which partitioning already holds, compares broadcast against shuffle by cost for each join, and recomputes a small deterministic join on every node when that is cheaper than moving its result. On TPC-H SF100 over 8 nodes (same binary, same run window; times are server-side means of the hot runs) the join-heavy queries improve: | Query | Rule-based -> Cascades | What changed in the plan | |---|---|---| | Q21 | 7.66 s -> 5.34 s | The four `supplier x nation` joins compute their small results once and broadcast them, so `lineitem` is not shuffled to meet them. | | Q09 | 4.07 s -> 2.47 s | `part` and `nation` are read in full by every node, so `lineitem` and `supplier` are not shuffled to meet them. | | Q08 | 2.39 s -> 0.99 s | `nation x region` (5 rows) is recomputed by every node; `part` is read in full per node, so `lineitem` is not shuffled to join it. | | Q02 | 2.14 s -> 0.84 s | The `supplier x nation x region` chain is recomputed by every node, so only `partsupp` and `supplier` are shuffled. The top-100 sort becomes two-stage, sending at most 100 rows per node. | | Q05 | 2.05 s -> 1.12 s | The whole dimension side (`orders x customer x nation x region`) is recomputed by every node over full local reads; `lineitem` joins it in place with no shuffle at all. | | Q17 | 2.72 s -> 1.78 s | The small per-part average is broadcast to every node, so the outer 600M-row `lineitem` read is not shuffled. | | Q11 | 0.49 s -> 0.26 s | `supplier x nation` is computed once and broadcast; `partsupp` joins it in place. | | Q12 | 0.76 s -> 0.59 s | The filtered `lineitem` rows (~30K of 600M) are gathered once and broadcast; nothing is shuffled. | The remaining queries change less. Summed over all 22 queries, hot server time drops from 36.8 s to 28.8 s (about 22% lower). The remaining regressions are the `IN (subquery)` queries Q18 (2.43 s -> 2.85 s) and Q20 (2.24 s -> 2.99 s). With the forced join rewrite removed, both run their `IN`s as sets in both modes, and the sets built are identical; the difference is in the plans around them. Cascades picks replicated-read shapes that rescan moderate tables on every node, which loses here for a structural reason: the main reads are filtered by `x IN <set>`, and the set contents do not exist at costing time, so the model cannot credit a shuffle-based plan for how few rows survive the set filter, while the replicated read's full scan is paid regardless. Two follow-ups: a cost-informed choice of the `IN` form, and set-filter selectivity from the subquery's output estimate. `EXPLAIN pretty = 1, estimates = 1` shows the chosen plan with a row estimate and the accumulated cost for each step. Also in this PR, two improvements to the shared bucketed-read machinery (they benefit the rule-based path too): the `FINAL` layer split no longer depends on the coordinator's core count, and a many-partition `FINAL` split groups its layers into the target task count instead of falling back to a serial read. Design, a worked example on TPC-H data (a simplified 3-table query traced through the memo), and current limitations are documented in `src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/Cascades/ARCHITECTURE.md`. Plan-shape tests cover the actual TPC-H queries (`03836_tpch_join_order_plans`), and focused tests pin the cost-model contracts (e.g. `04869_cascades_read_cost_granule_volume`, `04838_cascades_filter_selectivity`). Disabled by default. Requires the analyzer; remote execution requires the stateless-worker configuration, while `distributed_plan_execute_locally = 1` runs the stages in-process without it: ```sql SET enable_cascades_optimizer = 1, make_distributed_plan = 1; ``` For tests, `param__internal_cascades_cluster_node_count` overrides the cluster size, `param__internal_cascades_cost_config` overrides the cost model configuration, `param__internal_join_table_stat_hints` injects table statistics, `param__internal_cascades_task_limit` lowers the task budget (it can never raise it). Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106020 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added an experimental Cascades cost-based optimizer for distributed query plans, enabled by `enable_cascades_optimizer = 1` together with `make_distributed_plan = 1`. It chooses between shuffle, broadcast, replicated, and local join strategies, two-phase, shuffle, and local aggregation, two-stage distributed top-N, and parallel and replicated reads by estimated cost, inserting exchange operators as needed. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation written in [/docs](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/tree/master/docs) <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1593` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Feature: Enable overlay databases for server.
signals.text: Enables server-side `Overlay` databases. An `Overlay` database is a read-only facade that exposes the union of the tables of several underlying databases, resolving each table name through the listed sources in order (the first source that has the table wins). DDL on the facade is rejected — it has no storage of its own — while `SELECT` and pass-through `INSERT` resolve to the underlying source table. Reading or writing through the facade requires the corresponding grant on both the facade database and the underlying source, and the facade's row policies are combined with the source's. Previously an `Overlay` database existed only as the implicit default database of `clickhouse-local`. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/52764 <!--- A technical comment, you are free to remove or leave it as it is when PR is created The following categories are used in the next scripts, update them accordingly utils/changelog/changelog.py tests/ci/cancel_and_rerun_workflow_lambda/app.py --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Allow creating `Overlay` databases. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=86768&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/86768](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F86768+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Add replica_host configuration for DatabaseReplicated
signals.text: <!--- Disable AI PR formatting assistant: true --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add `replica_host` configuration parameter for DatabaseReplicated to specify advertised hostname for replica communication, independent from server bind address. Resolves #88378 ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) ### Details Currently, DatabaseReplicated uses `interserver_http_host` or the system hostname, which may not be routable from other replicas. This PR adds a new `replica_host` configuration parameter that allows administrators to explicitly specify the advertised hostname for DatabaseReplicated communication. Resolves #88378 ## Changes 1. **New Configuration Parameter**: `replica_host` - Optional parameter in `config.xml` - Takes precedence over `interserver_http_host` and system hostname 2. **Fallback Chain**: ``` replica_host (highest priority) ↓ interserver_http_host ↓ getFQDNOrHostName() (lowest priority) ``` 3. **Automatic Migration**: - When configuration changes (e.g., adding `replica_host`), automatically updates ZooKeeper if UUID and TCP port match - Prevents startup failures when only the advertised hostname changes - Rejects changes if UUID or port differ (different instance/misconfiguration) 4. **Implementation**: - Added `Context::getReplicaHost()`, `setReplicaHost()`, `hasReplicaHost()` - Modified `DatabaseReplicated::getHostID()` to use fallback chain - Added `parseHostID()` helper for UUID and port validation - Server.cpp reads `replica_host` from config on startup ## Configuration Example ```xml public.example.com 0.0.0.0 9000 ``` ## Backward Compatibility Fully backward compatible: - Optional parameter (no behavior change if not configured) - Existing `interserver_http_host` continues to work - Automatic migration prevents startup failures during config updates

signals.title: Fix logical error in getMinMaxTime() when Nullable DateTime column has all NULLs
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/92834 When a `MergeTree` table has a `Nullable(Date)` / `Nullable(DateTime)` / `Nullable(DateTime64)` column in its partition key and a part contains only `NULL` values in that column, querying `system.parts` threw: `Part minmax index by time is neither DateTime or DateTime64`. Root cause: for an all-`NULL` part, `ColumnNullable::getExtremesNullLast` returns `POSITIVE_INFINITY` (a `Field::Types::Null` sentinel) for the minmax bounds. `getMinMaxTime` only handled `UInt64` (`DateTime`) and `Decimal64` (`DateTime64`) field types, so the `Null` field fell through to the `throw`. Changes: - In `getMinMaxDate` and `getMinMaxTime`, short-circuit to an empty range when either hyperrectangle bound is `Null` (all-`NULL` parts, and mixed `NULL` / non-`NULL` NullLast parts where only the upper bound is `Null`). - In `getMinMaxTime`, require **both** bounds to have the expected `Field` type (`UInt64` for `DateTime`, `Decimal64` for `DateTime64`) before calling `safeGet`, and return an empty range for any other type instead of throwing `LOGICAL_ERROR` — mirroring the guard in `getMinMaxDate`. - In `checkPartitionKeyAndInitMinMax`, first select a non-`Nullable` `Date` / `DateTime` / `DateTime64` partition-key column exactly as before, and only when the key has no non-`Nullable` candidate at all (an all-`Nullable` date/time key) fall back to unwrapping `Nullable` and `LowCardinality(Nullable(...))` via `removeLowCardinalityAndNullable` (`allow_nullable_key` permits the `LowCardinality` wrapper too, and the minmax writer unwraps `LowCardinality` before taking extremes, so its index bounds look exactly like the plain `Nullable` case). This preserves the previous selection for mixed keys such as `(d Date, nd Nullable(Date))` (still chosen from the non-`Nullable` `d`), while populating `min_*` / `max_*` for all-`Nullable` keys instead of leaving them silently empty. The fallback is restricted to new-syntax tables, so old-syntax `ENGINE = MergeTree(date, ...)` tables keep rejecting a `Nullable(Date)` date column at creation. - Add a stateless test `04822_minmax_index_nullable_datetime_all_nulls` covering the `#92834` reproducer; all-`NULL` / mixed-`NULL` / non-`NULL` cases for `Nullable(Date)` / `Nullable(DateTime)` / `Nullable(DateTime64)` partition keys; the mixed non-`Nullable` `Date` + `Nullable(Date)` and `DateTime` + `Nullable(DateTime)` selection; and `LowCardinality(Nullable(Date))` / `LowCardinality(Nullable(DateTime))` partition keys (non-`NULL` and all-`NULL`). Scope / not covered here: this PR only removes the user-visible exception. It rescues `NULL` bounds and stale minmax slots whose `Field` storage is incompatible with the expected date/time kind. A stale minmax slot after `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN ... AFTER` that happens to point at a non-date column sharing the same `Field` storage (a reordered `UInt64` read as `DateTime`, or a plain `Decimal64` read as `DateTime64`) is still read as a date/time and can surface a misleading `min_*` / `max_*` value rather than an empty range. Fully refreshing the cached per-part `minmax_idx_*_column_pos` after a column reorder is the deeper fix; it needs per-part column-order persistence to stay concurrency-safe with concurrent `SELECT`s and is left for a follow-up. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed an exception when querying `system.parts` `min_time` / `max_time` / `min_date` / `max_date` for `MergeTree` parts whose cached date/time minmax slot contains `NULL` bounds or a `Field` storage type incompatible with the expected date/time bound (for example, an all-`NULL` `Nullable(Date)` / `Nullable(DateTime)` / `Nullable(DateTime64)` partition-key column). ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)

signals.title: clean orphans from keeper snapshots
signals.text: This change makes ClickHouse Keeper able to recover from snapshots that contain orphaned nodes — nodes whose parent is absent from the snapshot. Before this change, such a snapshot made Keeper fail to start with an opaque internal error thrown by `updateValue` ("Could not find key"). This pull request replaces that with a clear, opt-in recovery path: - By default (`keeper_server.remove_orphaned_nodes_on_startup` = `false`), Keeper still refuses to load a snapshot with orphaned nodes, but now throws an actionable `CORRUPTED_DATA` exception that reports the number of orphaned nodes and how to enable recovery. - When `keeper_server.remove_orphaned_nodes_on_startup` = `true` and `keeper_server.digest_enabled` = `false`, the orphaned nodes and all of their descendants are removed during startup, ACL usage counters and ephemeral bookkeeping are updated, and stale `numChildren` counters on surviving nodes are corrected, so Keeper can load the snapshot. Cleanup is strictly a startup recovery operation. A snapshot deserialized while the server is already running — for example, a follower applying a leader snapshot in `KeeperStateMachine::apply_snapshot` — is applied as-is and is never modified, so a follower cannot diverge from the rest of the cluster. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ClickHouse Keeper now throws an actionable `CORRUPTED_DATA` error reporting the number of orphaned nodes (nodes whose parent is missing) when loading a snapshot that contains them, instead of failing with an opaque internal error. With the new setting `keeper_server.remove_orphaned_nodes_on_startup` set to `true` and `keeper_server.digest_enabled` set to `false`, such orphaned nodes (and their descendants) are removed during startup so Keeper can load the snapshot. The cleanup is performed only on startup, never while the server is running. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)

signals.title: Randomize tests with DETACH/ATTACH table before query execution
signals.text: Add `reattach_tables_before_query_execution` and `reattach_tables_before_query_execution_probability` settings that enable randomly detaching and reattaching tables used in a query before its execution. This is a testing-only feature designed to find bugs related to table reattachment. Before executing a query, the system collects all tables referenced in the AST, and for each eligible table (stores data on disk, supports detaching, has no action locks or dependencies), it performs a `DETACH` followed by `ATTACH`. Changes: - Add `supportsDetachingTables` virtual method to `IDatabase` (overridden to `false` for engines that do not support non-permanent `DETACH TABLE`: `DatabaseDictionary`, `DatabaseReplicated`, `DatabaseSQLite`, `DatabaseBackup`, `DatabaseFilesystem`, `DatabaseHDFS`, `DatabaseS3`, `DatabaseURL`, `DatabaseRemote`, `DatabaseDataLake`, `DatabaseMaterializedPostgreSQL`) - Add `has`/`hasAny` methods to `ActionLocksManager` for checking existing locks (skipping expired `weak_ptr` entries) - Add table collection visitor and reattach logic in `executeQuery` (runs after AST validations, process list admission, and external tables initialization; skips `EXPLAIN`, transactions, internal/non-initial queries, and CTE name collisions) - Fix off-by-one in `MergeTreeDeduplicationLog::dropOutdatedLogs` (don't drop the active log) and add `sync` call in shutdown - Add `no-random-detach` tag to tests incompatible with this feature - Add `--no-random-detach` and `--reattach-tables-probability` options to `clickhouse-test` - Add `02461_reattach_tables` test Continuation of #55943. Continuation of #42336 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Build/Testing/Packaging Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add `reattach_tables_before_query_execution` and `reattach_tables_before_query_execution_probability` settings that randomly `DETACH` and `ATTACH` tables used in a query before its execution. This is a testing-only feature that helps find reattachment-related bugs. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Introduces new pre-execution mutations (internal `DETACH`/`ATTACH`) in `executeQuery`, which can affect table availability and concurrency behavior if enabled; guarded by new experimental settings but touches core query execution paths. > > **Overview** > Adds experimental settings `reattach_tables_before_query_execution` and `..._probability` to optionally **DETACH and ATTACH back** eligible tables referenced by a query immediately before execution, including AST table discovery that accounts for CTE scoping, privilege checks, dependency/lock checks, and safety skips (e.g. `system`, non-disk storages, dynamic-structure columns, transactions, `EXPLAIN`, internal/non-initial queries). > > Extends `IDatabase` with `supportsDetachingTables()` and marks multiple database engines as not supporting non-permanent detach; adds `ActionLocksManager::has/hasAny` helpers to avoid detaching tables with active action locks. Updates the test runner and stress tooling to randomize this behavior (with `--no-random-detach` and probability control), adds a new `02461_reattach_tables` test, and tags many existing tests to opt out where DETACH/ATTACH would add flakiness/overhead. Also fixes `MergeTreeDeduplicationLog` cleanup to avoid dropping the active log and ensures writer `sync()` on shutdown. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit a369371ff61cb1934815ea1e8caf7debd83c98c4. signals.title: Fix hang in `--queries-file` / `-q` when stdin is a pipe with no data
signals.text: `ClientBase` eagerly called `isStdinNotEmptyAndValid` to check for trailing stdin data on every `INSERT`. That helper calls `!std_in.eof()`, which performs a blocking `read(0, ...)`. When stdin is a pipe that is open but has no data and no `EOF` (common in CI, Docker, stress tests, and `--queries-file` invocations), the read blocks indefinitely and the client hangs until it is killed by timeout. Concretely, this caused an exception (signal 11 after timeout) in the stress test `03538_analyzer_scalar_correlated_subquery_fix`: the process hung on `read(0, ...)` and was killed. The fix replaces the eager blocking probe with a non-blocking one: `poll(timeout=0)` first asks "does stdin appear to have data right now?", and only when it does we fall through to `isStdinNotEmptyAndValid` to confirm and consume it. This: - avoids the hang on open empty pipes — `poll` returns 0 immediately; - preserves deterministic rejection of `inlined data + stdin` mixed input — when stdin actually contains data (the case asserted by `04064_inline_insert_data`), `poll` returns `POLLIN` and we still throw `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`; - is best-effort by design: a slow producer pipe (e.g. `(sleep 1; echo) | clickhouse-client ...`) may not have written by the time `poll` runs, in which case the trailing stdin payload is ignored. This is preferable to the alternative of a hard hang, and is documented in the helper. Covered cases (`is_async_insert_with_inlined_data`, `is_inline_insert_data`, and the appending-stdin path in `sendData`) all go through the same probe so the hang is closed for `--queries-file`, `-q`, and `--inline-insert-data` modes. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=b9e68f4b9b0b33c7db43b00afb3eff4ff2050694&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_debug%29 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a hang in `clickhouse-client` for `INSERT` queries in `--queries-file`/`-q`/`--inline-insert-data` mode when stdin is an open pipe with no data and no `EOF` (common in CI, Docker, and stress tests). ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=96494&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/96494](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F96494+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Optimization of `GROUP BY` in the presence of `ORDER BY` and `LIMIT`
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Optimize `GROUP BY ... ORDER BY ... LIMIT` and `GROUP BY ... LIMIT` queries by maintaining a bounded heap during aggregation to prune groups that cannot appear in the result, significantly reducing memory usage and execution time for high-cardinality grouping. Controlled by the `enable_group_by_top_k_optimization` setting. Based on the initial implementation by [Dmitriy Terenichev](https://github.com/Dmitry909) ([#78553](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/78553)). Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/72610 Query shapes that benefit from this optimization: - `SELECT key, agg() FROM t GROUP BY key ORDER BY key ASC LIMIT N` -- single key, full ORDER BY match - `SELECT key, agg() FROM t GROUP BY key LIMIT N` -- single key, no ORDER BY - `SELECT k1, k2, agg() FROM t GROUP BY k1, k2 ORDER BY k1, k2 ASC LIMIT N` -- composite keys, full ORDER BY match - `SELECT k1, k2, k3, agg() FROM t GROUP BY k1, k2, k3 ORDER BY k1, k2, k3 ASC LIMIT N` -- 3+ keys, full match - `SELECT k1, k2, agg() FROM t GROUP BY k1, k2 ORDER BY k1 ASC LIMIT N` -- composite keys, ORDER BY is a prefix of GROUP BY - `SELECT k1, k2, k3, agg() FROM t GROUP BY k1, k2, k3 ORDER BY k1 ASC LIMIT N` -- prefix 1 of 3 - `SELECT k1, k2, k3, agg() FROM t GROUP BY k1, k2, k3 ORDER BY k1, k2 ASC LIMIT N` -- prefix 2 of 3 - `SELECT k1, k2, agg() FROM t GROUP BY k1, k2 LIMIT N` -- composite keys, no ORDER BY - `SELECT URL, count() FROM t GROUP BY URL ORDER BY URL ASC LIMIT N` -- String keys - `SELECT URL, count() FROM t GROUP BY URL LIMIT N` -- String keys, no ORDER BY Not supported (optimization is skipped): - `ORDER BY agg()` (ORDER BY aggregate function, not a GROUP BY key) (handled by [another PR](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/98607)) - `WITH TOTALS`, `HAVING`, `GROUPING SETS`, `CUBE`, `ROLLUP` - `LIMIT WITH TIES` - ~~Non-final aggregation (distributed partial aggregation)~~ - `max_rows_to_group_by` is set - `rows_before_limit_at_least` mode (exact count) - queries having collators in ORDER BY - ORDER BY columns that are not a leading prefix of GROUP BY keys <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=96630&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/96630](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F96630+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix JSON/XML format statistics race condition with parallel replicas
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `rows_read` and `rows_before_limit_at_least` reported as 0 or stale in JSON/XML format output when a query with `LIMIT` reads from remote connections (parallel replicas or the `remote` table function). ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) No documentation changes needed — this is a bug fix with no user-facing API changes. --- ## Summary - When parallel replicas are used with `LIMIT`, `rows_read` in JSON/XML output is reported as 0 - Root cause: race condition where `finalizeImpl` writes statistics BEFORE `PipelineExecutor::finalizeExecution` collects remaining progress from connection draining - Fix: two-phase output format finalization — statistics are written AFTER all progress has been collected - The same drain also delivers late `ProfileInfo` packets that update the `rows_before_limit_at_least` / `rows_before_aggregation` counters, so the deferral covers the whole trailer, and the native-protocol `ProfileInfo` sent to the client is refreshed from the post-drain counters ## Approach Split the output format's finalization so statistics are written AFTER `finalizeExecution` collects all remaining progress: - **Phase 1** (during pipeline, in `finalizeImpl`): Write everything EXCEPT the trailer after the `rows` field (`rows_before_limit_at_least`, `rows_before_aggregation`, the `"statistics"` section) and closing delimiter - **Phase 2** (after `finalizeExecution`): Re-read the rows-before-* counters, write the trailer and close the document via a finalize callback ### Key changes: - `IOutputFormat`: Added `hasDeferredStatistics`, `writeDeferredStatisticsAndFinalize`, `completeDeferredStatistics` mechanism; `snapshotRowsBeforeCounters` re-reads the shared counters before the deferred trailer is written - `PipelineExecutor`: Added `setFinalizeCallback` called at end of `finalizeExecution` after progress collection - `CompletedPipelineExecutor`: Sets the finalize callback to invoke `completeDeferredStatistics` - `JSONRowOutputFormat`, `XMLRowOutputFormat`, `JSONColumnsWithMetadataBlockOutputFormat`: Override deferred statistics methods; the whole trailer (`rows_before_limit_at_least`, `rows_before_aggregation`, `statistics`) is deferred to phase 2 (`JSONUtils::writeRowsBeforeAndStatistics` factors out the shared writer) - `ParallelFormattingOutputFormat`: Propagates deferred statistics through the parallel formatting pipeline - `LazyOutputFormat` / `PullingOutputFormat`: `getProfileInfo` re-snapshots the rows-before-* counters, so the `ProfileInfo` packet sent to native-protocol clients (TCP `clickhouse-client`, gRPC, `LocalConnection`) carries the post-drain values — by the time it is sent, the executor thread has been joined and the counters are final - New failpoint `tcp_handler_sleep_before_secondary_query_trailing_packets` delays a secondary query's trailing `Totals` / `Extremes` / `ProfileInfo` / `Progress` / `EndOfStream`, making the race deterministic for tests Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/85785 ## Test plan - [x] Build succeeds (Release) - [x] Test `00365_statistics_in_formats` passes - [x] JSON format tests pass (`00159_parallel_formatting_json_and_friends_1/2`, `00378_json_quote_64bit_integers`, `00685_output_format_json_escape_forward_slashes`, `01447_json_strings`, `01449_json_compact_strings`, `01486_json_array_output`, `02554_format_json_columns_for_empty`) - [x] XML format tests pass (`00307_format_xml`, `02122_parallel_formatting_XML`) - [x] `03918_statistics_in_formats_parallel_replicas` — forward guard: parallel-replicas `rows_read` matches the single-node value - [x] New deterministic reproducer `04603_rows_before_limit_parallel_replicas_late_packets` — fails without the fix (failpoint forces the trailing packets into the drain window); checks `rows_read` under parallel replicas and `rows_read` + `rows_before_limit_at_least` through the `remote` table function, over HTTP (server-side formatting) and native TCP (client-side formatting), across `JSON`, `JSONColumnsWithMetadata`, and `XML` - [ ] CI: Run with parallel replicas to verify `rows_read` is no longer 0 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches query pipeline execution, cancellation, and output formatting/finalization paths; while scoped to statistics/progress reporting, it changes timing and thread-synchronization and could affect query completion/cancellation behavior under parallel replicas. > > **Overview** > Fixes a race where JSON/XML output could report `rows_read=0` with parallel replicas + `LIMIT` by ensuring final `Progress` packets (drained after cancellation/early completion) are incorporated before statistics are emitted. > > This introduces **two-phase output finalization**: `IOutputFormat` can defer writing statistics/closing delimiters (`hasDeferredStatistics`/`writeDeferredStatisticsAndFinalize`), and `PipelineExecutor` now supports a `setFinalizeCallback` invoked at the end of `finalizeExecution()` after collecting remaining progress; `CompletedPipelineExecutor` wires this to `IOutputFormat::completeDeferredStatistics()`. > > Cancellation/draining logic is tightened to preserve trailing progress and avoid blocking hard cancels: `PipelineExecutor` triggers a `PartialResult` cancel on normal completion, `ISource::cancel` skips `onCancel` for `PartialResult` but allows later escalation, `RemoteSource` adds explicit cancel-reason upgrades and aborts drain via `RemoteQueryExecutor::abortDrain`, and `RemoteQueryExecutor::finish()` drains until all replica connections complete while swallowing expected cancel exceptions. Adds a stateless regression test `03918_statistics_in_formats_parallel_replicas` to assert `rows_read > 0` across JSON/XML formats over TCP/HTTP. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 5818266286a7645dcf1b57212bf9b3214cfd2ec8. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY --> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=96978&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/96978](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F96978+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Push join key filters into MergeTree index during recursive CTE evaluation
signals.text: When a recursive CTE joins against a `MergeTree` table, each recursion step previously scanned the entire table, because the join condition (e.g. `ON e.from_id = t.current_id`) was not pushed into `MergeTree`'s key condition. This change analyzes the recursive query's join tree to find equi-join conditions between the CTE working table and real tables. Before each step it reads the join-key values from the working table and injects them as an `IN (...)` predicate directly into the `WHERE` clause of each recursive `QueryNode` that joins against the CTE (the original `WHERE`/`HAVING`/`QUALIFY` clauses are snapshotted at construction and restored after each step, so nothing accumulates across steps). The planner then lowers this predicate into `ReadFromMergeTree`'s key condition. The injected set is bounded by the new setting `recursive_cte_max_in_filter_cardinality`, and injection fails closed to a plain scan whenever it could otherwise change results — when the generated set would exceed `max_rows_in_set`/`max_bytes_in_set`, cannot be materialized under `max_memory_usage`, or the `IN` predicate cannot be resolved for the join-key type. Parallel replicas are disabled for the recursive step queries to avoid stale cached `GLOBAL JOIN` tables returning incorrect results; the forcing mode `allow_experimental_parallel_reading_from_replicas = 2` raises `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED` for the recursive part rather than silently downgrading. For a table with ~1M rows and 10 recursion steps, `read_rows` drops from ~10M to ~120. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/75026 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `WITH RECURSIVE` queries that use `ON` or comma equi-joins against `MergeTree` tables can now use the primary key index, reducing the number of rows read per recursion step. The optimization is controlled by the new setting `recursive_cte_max_in_filter_cardinality`. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) No separate documentation page is needed — this is a transparent performance improvement. The only user-visible addition is the setting `recursive_cte_max_in_filter_cardinality`, which is documented at the source level in `src/Core/Settings.cpp`. <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches recursive CTE execution and query settings, and dynamically injects `additional_table_filters`, which could affect correctness/performance for some JOIN patterns despite being scoped to recursive steps. > > **Overview** > Improves recursive CTE performance by detecting equi-join conditions between the CTE working table and real tables, then **pushing join-key values into `additional_table_filters`** (built as `IN (...)` predicates) on each recursive step so MergeTree reads can use the primary-key index; user-provided `additional_table_filters` are merged rather than overwritten. > > Also **disables parallel replicas** for recursive CTE step queries to avoid incorrect results from reused cached GLOBAL JOIN tables, and adds a stateless test (`03924_recursive_cte_join_index`) asserting both correct output and low `read_rows` for explicit `INNER JOIN` and comma-join forms. > > <sup>Written by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot) for commit 37f26180bfa2189247b6862712551c7ecc41ed18. This will update automatically on new commits. Configure [here](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY --> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=97254&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/97254](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F97254+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Validate IN tuple/subquery column count mismatch in analyzer
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/74442 The analyzer (`resolveFunction`) now validates that the number of elements on the left side of `IN` matches the number of columns in the right-side subquery. Previously, constant folding could optimize away the `IN` expression and silently hide the mismatch: for example, `(1, 1) IN (SELECT 1)` wrapped in a subquery with a constant-false outer `WHERE` succeeded silently. Now it correctly throws `NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS_DOESNT_MATCH` during analysis. A single `Tuple` column on the right side is still accepted, since `FunctionIn` compares the whole left-side value against it; `LowCardinality` and `Nullable` wrappers are unwrapped before the check. Covered by the new test `03380_in_tuple_subquery_column_count`, including the original reproducer from the issue. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Detect column count mismatch between a tuple and a subquery in the `IN` clause during analysis, preventing constant folding from silently hiding the error. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=97540&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/97540](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F97540+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
