signal.title: Serialize an empty polygon with zero rings (canonical WKB)
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110701 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110701 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed non-canonical WKB serialization of an empty polygon: `wkb(POLYGON EMPTY)` now emits `numRings = 0` instead of a spurious single zero-point ring, so a WKB round-trip of a standard empty polygon is identity-preserving. ### Description An empty polygon is stored internally with one empty outer ring (`[[]]`), so `wkb()` emitted `numRings = 1` with a zero-point `LinearRing`, producing a non-canonical form (`01030000000100000000000000`) that stricter WKB consumers may reject. Other empty geometries (LineString, MultiLineString, MultiPolygon) already serialized with a zero element count. `WKBPolygonTransform::dumpObject` (src/Common/WKB.cpp) now emits zero rings for a single-empty-ring polygon, matching the canonical form `010300000000000000`. This canonicalizes only the `wkb()` bytes and covers both freshly parsed values and rows already stored as `[[]]` by older builds. The in-memory Polygon value is left unchanged, so `readWKTPolygon('POLYGON EMPTY')` still returns `[[]]` and SQL value equality, joins, and `GROUP BY` over empty polygons are unaffected. This PR is scoped to WKB. `wkt()` streams through `boost::geometry::wkt` and prints `POLYGON()` for a zero-ring polygon (the same shape it uses for other empty geometries, e.g. `MULTIPOLYGON()`); making `wkt()` emit `POLYGON EMPTY` is a separate concern and is not addressed here.

signal.title: Add a preliminary DISTINCT to UNION DISTINCT
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115104 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114550 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115104 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114550 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `A UNION DISTINCT B` now deduplicates each branch in parallel before merging them, the same way its `SELECT DISTINCT * FROM (A UNION ALL B)` rewrite already did. Previously every row funnelled through a single `DistinctTransform`, so the query did not scale with `max_threads`. ### Description `A UNION DISTINCT B` and `SELECT DISTINCT * FROM (A UNION ALL B)` are the same query but got different pipelines: the rewrite deduplicates each branch before the merge, `UNION DISTINCT` did not. **Root cause.** The union branch of `Planner::buildPlanForUnionNode` (and its old-analyzer twin in `InterpreterSelectWithUnionQuery::buildQueryPlan`) added one `DistinctStep` with `pre_distinct = false`. `DistinctStep::getTraits` sets `returns_single_stream = !pre_distinct`, so that one step both merged to one stream and deduplicated. The `SELECT DISTINCT` path adds two steps. **The change** adds a `pre_distinct = true` step before the existing one, in both planners. `liftUpUnion` then clones it into each branch, which is how the rewrite gets its per-branch distinct. No new setting, no change to `DistinctStep` or any pass. Scoped to `UNION_DISTINCT`: `INTERSECT`/`EXCEPT DISTINCT` share the `is_distinct` branch, but `IntersectOrExceptStep` already resizes every branch to one stream and `liftUpUnion` does not handle it, so a preliminary step there is overhead. Their plans are unchanged. **Measured** (release build, 8M rows/branch, 2000 distinct values, best of 7, `query_duration_ms`): | max_threads | before | after | |---|---|---| | 1 | 60 ms | 61 ms | | 8 | 44 ms | 13 ms | | 16 | 59 ms | 9 ms | The rewrite scores 13 ms / 8 ms here, so the two forms now agree. With all-distinct data the preliminary step is overhead, at the cost the rewrite already pays. A preliminary DISTINCT keeps one hash table per stream, and this one carries the same `max_rows_in_distinct` / `max_bytes_in_distinct`, so exactly as in the rewrite those limits now bind per stream as well as globally; both overflow modes measured identical to the rewrite. The new test asserts the plan shape, not timing, and checks results against the rewrite across `Nullable`, `LowCardinality`, `Array`, aggregate-state and coerced-type branches, chains, `LIMIT`/`LIMIT BY` and size limits. <details> <summary>Interaction with #114550 (measured)</summary> #114550 "Deduplicate the final DISTINCT in parallel" attacks the same bottleneck from the other side and edits the same two functions. Measured on its head `1e783f46`, same fixture and method: | arm | t1 | t8 | t16 | |---|---|---|---| | master | 60 ms | 44 ms | 59 ms | | #114550 alone | 57 ms | 22 ms | 17 ms | | this PR alone | 61 ms | 13 ms | 9 ms | | #114550 + this PR | 60 ms | 11 ms | 7 ms | #114550 parallelizes the final dedup; this PR reduces how many rows reach it. They stack, and #114550 alone does not close the reported gap. It keeps `pre_distinct = false` at the union site, so the conflict is textual only - whoever merges second rebases. </details>

signal.title: Fix optimize_distributed_group_by_sharding_key wrong result for JOIN
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111087 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111274 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111087 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111274 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a wrong result with `optimize_distributed_group_by_sharding_key` when grouping a distributed `JOIN` by a column from the other join side that shares the sharding key's name (e.g. `GROUP BY r.k` over a `LEFT JOIN` where `r.k` is not the distributed table's sharding key). Such groups can span shards, so the per-shard aggregation shortcut is no longer applied for them, avoiding duplicate group keys with split aggregate values. ### Description `optimize_distributed_group_by_sharding_key` lets `StorageDistributed` skip the cross-shard merge when the `GROUP BY` key equals the sharding key, assuming each group's rows live on a single shard. In the new analyzer, `isShardingKeySuitsQueryTreeNodeExpression` matched the grouping expression against the sharding key by column name only (table qualifiers are stripped when building the comparison DAG). So a right-side column `r.k` in a distributed `LEFT JOIN` that merely shares the left table's sharding-key name `k` wrongly triggered the shortcut. Unmatched left rows are padded with `r.k = 0` on every shard, so the `r.k = 0` group spans shards and per-shard partial aggregates were returned unmerged, producing duplicate group keys with split values (silent wrong result). The fix skips the shortcut when the grouping/DISTINCT/LIMIT BY expression references any column that is not from the distributed table's own table expression, reusing the existing `hasUnknownColumn` helper. `GROUP BY` over the distributed table's actual sharding key is unaffected. Only the new analyzer path was affected; the old analyzer compares qualified identifier names and was already correct. Issue #111274 (`optimize_skip_unused_shards = 1` duplicating every group of a distributed self-join on an expression sharding key `intHash64(k)`) is the same root cause and is fixed by the same guard: `GROUP BY negate(r.k)` over a global self-join references `r.k` from the broadcast side, whose required column matches the sharding key name after qualifier stripping. Verified locally on master: the self-join returned 1000 rows (500 groups duplicated, each with an empty aggregate copy) and returns the correct 500 with this fix.

signal.title: Memoize supportsOptimizationToSubcolumns in FunctionToSubcolumnsPass
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113202 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109188 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113202 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109188 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Analysis of a query over a `Merge` table no longer costs a full traversal of every child table per query-tree node. `optimize_functions_to_subcolumns` now computes each storage's answer once per pass run instead of once per node, which restores analysis time to being proportional to the query size alone. Closes #113202. ### Description `IStorage::supportsOptimizationToSubcolumns` reads like a flag, but wrapper storages answer it by traversing what they wrap: `StorageMerge` overrides it with a full `traverseTablesUntil` over every child (added in #109188), re-creating the database iterators per call, and `DatabaseTablesSnapshotIterator` copies the table map. `FunctionToSubcolumnsPass` reads that predicate from two helpers reached from four **per-query-tree-node** call sites, *before* consulting the function name. A query with N function nodes over a `Merge` with T children therefore pays N traversals of T tables even when nothing is rewritable. `position` is not in the 13-name rewritable set, so `merge_table_large_query` (1504 `position` calls, 500 children) paid ~750k child visits for a rewrite that cannot fire. The answer is a property of the storage, so it is memoized in an `unordered_map<const IStorage *, bool>` on each visitor, for one pass run. `TableNode` pins the `StoragePtr` and no `updateStorage` caller runs inside a pass, so the key cannot go stale, and nothing is cached across queries or DDL. All twelve carriers of the predicate are pure configuration reads, so only the number of computations changes. Measured on one Debug binary with the perf test's fixture by flipping `optimize_functions_to_subcolumns` (`QueryAnalysisMicroseconds`, medians of 5 interleaved runs): before 90 807 off vs 403 557 on (4.44x); after 99 388 vs 99 853 (1.005x). The same query over a plain `MergeTree` does not move on either build, and the result is byte-identical in all four cells. A new stateless test asserts the memoized answer matches a fresh one on the supporting and fail-closed arms, including two storages that disagree within one query. Left alone deliberately: `DistanceTransposedPartialReadsPass` (same predicate per node, but name-checked first and setting-gated) and the `DatabaseTablesSnapshotIterator` copy (a documented snapshot semantic in every database engine). #109188 was backported to 26.6.2, so 26.6.2+ and 26.7+ carry it. Root cause reported by @ egor-click.

signal.title: Document that a MATERIALIZED column calculated from an EPHEMERAL column is not recalculated by a mutation
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114561 ## Problem Nothing documents what a mutation does to a `MATERIALIZED` column that is calculated from an `EPHEMERAL` column. The behaviour is a deliberate trade-off, but a user can only discover it by observing wrong-looking data: ```sql CREATE TABLE test (x Int32, e Int32 EPHEMERAL 0, m Int32 MATERIALIZED x + e) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); INSERT INTO test (x, e) VALUES (1, 7); -- m = 8 ALTER TABLE test UPDATE x = 2 WHERE 1; SELECT x, m FROM test; -- 2 8 <- not 2 + 7 ``` `m` keeps its `INSERT`-time value and from then on does not match its own expression, because `e` does not exist outside the `INSERT` that supplied it and cannot be read back to recalculate `m`. Where a user would look today: - **`ALTER TABLE ... UPDATE`** — does not mention `MATERIALIZED` or `EPHEMERAL` at all. Its only related statement is that updating a column used in the primary or partition key is unsupported. - **`MATERIALIZED`** — says values are "automatically calculated ... when rows are inserted", and says nothing about mutations. - **`EPHEMERAL`** — correctly says such columns are not stored, but does not draw out the consequence for mutations. The mutation does log a warning when it skips a column for this reason, which is accurate and actionable — but it appears only in the server log, at the moment it happens, and is not returned to the client. So the only documentation of this behaviour is an after-the-fact log line. ## Solution Add a `Materialized columns` section to the `ALTER TABLE ... UPDATE` page: a `MATERIALIZED` column whose expression reads an updated column is recalculated, and a sub-section on the `EPHEMERAL` case with the example above, the reason, and the existing advice to re-`INSERT` the affected rows. The example's output was verified verbatim against a local server. Only the English page is edited; localized pages are generated. Documentation only — no behaviour change, and independent of any pending fix in this area: it states what holds on `master` today and would still hold after https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114561. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Documentation (changelog entry is not required)

signal.title: Add INSERT ... RETURNING (non-atomic, user-supplied SELECT)
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add `INSERT ... RETURNING (SELECT ...)` to run a user-supplied SELECT after INSERT and return its result in one round-trip. Closes #21697. **Backward-incompatible change:** `RETURNING` is now a reserved keyword and can no longer be used as an unquoted implicit column alias (e.g. `SELECT 1 returning`). Use `AS returning` or a quoted identifier instead. --- Closes #21697 ## Summary Draft implementation of `INSERT ... RETURNING` for ClickHouse. The INSERT runs first using the existing pipeline; if it succeeds, a parenthesized `RETURNING (SELECT ...)` subquery runs in the same session and its result set is returned to the client in one round-trip. This is intentionally **not** Postgres-style atomic `RETURNING`. The user supplies the trailing SELECT and owns the `WHERE` clause used to identify inserted rows. ## Syntax For `INSERT VALUES` and `INSERT FORMAT`, `RETURNING` appears **before** the data clause (parser constraint: bytes after `VALUES`/`FORMAT` are raw input): ```sql INSERT INTO t (id, name) RETURNING (SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = 123) VALUES (123, 'foo'); INSERT INTO t RETURNING (SELECT count() FROM t WHERE batch_id = 'X') FORMAT JSONEachRow {"batch_id":"X", ...} ``` For `INSERT SELECT`, `RETURNING` appears **after** the source query: ```sql INSERT INTO t SELECT * FROM src RETURNING (SELECT count() FROM t WHERE batch_id = 'X'); ``` The parenthesized subquery is required (distinct from Postgres column-list `RETURNING id, name`). ## Semantics - INSERT runs first with its existing pipeline untouched. - If INSERT throws, the RETURNING SELECT does not run. - If INSERT succeeds, a select interpreter is built for the trailing subquery using the same Context; its pipeline is returned as the statement result. - The trailing SELECT inherits session, user, and settings. It can reference any table and use the full SELECT grammar. - Client receives **one result set** (the RETURNING SELECT's), not an INSERT ack plus a result set. ## Limitations (documented, not bugs) - **Not atomic.** Concurrent writers can land rows between INSERT completion and SELECT execution. - **No automatic "the rows I just inserted."** User provides the SELECT and owns its `WHERE`. - **Replication lag is visible** on Replicated tables unless consistency settings are used. - **Incompatible with `async_insert=1`.** Returns `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`. - **No special MV interaction.** MVs fire on INSERT; RETURNING SELECT is a normal SELECT. - If INSERT succeeds but RETURNING SELECT fails, inserted data is **not rolled back**. ## Backward-incompatible change `RETURNING` is added to the parser's reserved-keyword list (same list as `FROM`, `WHERE`, `SETTINGS`, etc.) to prevent it from being consumed as an implicit table alias in `INSERT ... SELECT ... FROM tablename RETURNING (...)`. As a side-effect, `RETURNING` can no longer be used as an unquoted implicit alias anywhere in ClickHouse SQL: ```sql -- Before: worked (returning was a plain identifier) SELECT 1 returning SELECT * FROM t returning -- After: must use AS or quoting SELECT 1 AS returning SELECT * FROM t AS returning ``` ## Implementation - **Parser** (`ParserInsertQuery.cpp`): parse `RETURNING` + parenthesized SELECT; placement rules above. - **AST** (`ASTInsertQuery.h`): `returning_select` field; clone/format updated. - **Interpreter** (`InterpreterInsertQuery.cpp`): reject `async_insert`; wrap completed INSERT pipeline with RETURNING via `DelayedSource`. - **Pipeline** (`buildInsertReturningPipeline.cpp`): run INSERT to completion, then build SELECT pipeline; native push inserts swap to RETURNING SELECT after data is received. - **executeQuery** / **TCPHandler** / **LocalConnection** / **ClientBase**: inlined-data wrap, native-protocol push path, query-log accounting, process-list propagation. - **Docs**: section added to `insert-into.md` ## Tests added - `tests/queries/0_stateless/04266_insert_returning_21697.sql` — core `INSERT ... RETURNING` semantics, delayed planning/failure behavior, query-cache rejection paths, transactional rollback checks (`implicit_transaction=1` + explicit transaction), and parser keyword regression coverage (`SELECT 1 returning` rejected; explicit/quoted alias accepted). - `tests/queries/0_stateless/04267_insert_returning_native_format.sh` — native TCP `INSERT FORMAT` + external data + `RETURNING`, including `input(...)` + `FORMAT` placement/round-trip stability. - `tests/queries/0_stateless/04410_insert_returning_trailing_settings.sql` — source-side trailing `SETTINGS` scoping/precedence, nested source settings handling, source-side query-cache settings rejection (`NOT_IMPLEMENTED`), and a plain `INSERT ... SELECT` regression proving nested source subquery settings stay local (non-`RETURNING`). ## Alternatives considered - **`AND SELECT` / `THEN SELECT` keywords** — parser ambiguity or poor discoverability for Postgres migrants. - **Atomic Postgres-style RETURNING** — much larger surface (formats, MVs, distributed, async); deferred as a possible follow-up. - **Multi-statement `;`** — out of scope. ## Open questions for maintainers 1. Is the non-atomic, user-supplied-SELECT model the right v1 framing? 2. Confirm canonical placement rules (before data for VALUES/FORMAT, after source for INSERT SELECT). 3. Restrict trailing SELECT to read-only queries only? (Current implementation: yes, via SELECT parser.) 4. Confirm single-result-set protocol behavior across HTTP/native/JDBC. ## Test plan - [x] Stateless test `04266_insert_returning_21697` - [x] `INSERT VALUES` + `RETURNING` with row filter - [x] `INSERT SELECT` + `RETURNING` with aggregate - [x] `RETURNING` against a table other than INSERT target - [x] INSERT failure prevents `RETURNING` subquery from running - [x] `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` when `async_insert=1` - [x] Native TCP `INSERT FORMAT` + `RETURNING` (`04267_insert_returning_native_format`) - [x] `input(...)` source with `FORMAT` before `RETURNING` (parser/formatter round-trip + execution) - [x] Source-side `SETTINGS` precedence and nested-source scoping (`04410_insert_returning_trailing_settings`) - [x] Plain `INSERT ... SELECT` keeps nested source subquery `SETTINGS` local (no non-`RETURNING` leakage) - [x] Source-side query-cache settings rejection in `INSERT ... RETURNING` source `SETTINGS` - [x] `02310_profile_events_insert` local `clickhouse-local` profile-events check is non-fatal in CI (`InsertedRows` is not emitted consistently there) - [x] Transactional rollback when delayed `RETURNING` planning fails (`implicit_transaction=1` and explicit transaction) - [x] `RETURNING` keyword parser regression (`SELECT 1 returning` rejected; `SELECT 1 AS returning` and quoted alias accepted) - [x] `04266` rollback subtests stabilized by avoiding fixed database-name collisions in flaky/parallel runs (use `t_insert_returning_tx` in the current test DB) - [ ] Replicated-table non-atomic behavior (integration test, future)

signal.title: Logical error 'Totals having transform was already added to pipeline' on WITH TOTALS EXCEPT DISTINCT WITH TOTALS over merge()
signal.text: # `Logical error: 'Totals having transform was already added to pipeline'` on `WITH TOTALS EXCEPT DISTINCT WITH TOTALS` over `merge()` + set operation ## Summary An outer set operation (`EXCEPT DISTINCT`) between two `WITH TOTALS` aggregations, one side reading from a `merge()` table function that spans many source tables in the same database, reaches `TotalsHavingStep::transformPipeline` on a pipeline that **already carries a totals port** — likely because an inner totals stream propagated up through the `merge()`-expanded plan. The pipeline builder's guard fires: ``` Logical error: 'Totals having transform was already added to pipeline' QueryPipelineBuilder::addTotalsHavingTransform (QueryPipeline/QueryPipelineBuilder.cpp:159) ← TotalsHavingStep::transformPipeline (Processors/QueryPlan/TotalsHavingStep.cpp:93) ``` - **Debug/sanitizer (ubsan in the fuzz build):** `SIGABRT` (signal 6). Server exits. - **Release:** `LOGICAL_ERROR` (Code 49) thrown as an exception (guard `if (pipe.getTotalsPort()) throw`). ## Crashing query (verbatim) ```sql (SELECT DISTINCT countOrDefaultStateOrNull('') IGNORE NULLS FROM merge('default', '.+') GROUP BY ALL WITH TOTALS) EXCEPT DISTINCT (SELECT count() IGNORE NULLS FROM count__fuzz_137 GROUP BY ALL WITH TOTALS LIMIT -2147483649); ``` ## Stack ``` 0. abortOnFailedAssertion 1-4. Exception constructors 5. QueryPipelineBuilder::addTotalsHavingTransform QueryPipeline/QueryPipelineBuilder.cpp:159 6. TotalsHavingStep::transformPipeline Processors/QueryPlan/TotalsHavingStep.cpp:93 7. ITransformingStep::updatePipeline Processors/QueryPlan/ITransformingStep.cpp:21 8. QueryPlan::buildQueryPipeline Processors/QueryPlan/QueryPlan.cpp:268 9. InterpreterSelectQueryAnalyzer::buildQueryPipeline Interpreters/InterpreterSelectQueryAnalyzer.cpp:416 ... executeQuery → executeASTFuzzerQueries ``` ## Root cause hypothesis `QueryPipelineBuilder::addTotalsHavingTransform` at :159 throws when `pipe.getTotalsPort()` is already non-null. So the outer query's `TotalsHavingStep` is running against a pipeline that **already has a totals port attached**, meaning an inner `WITH TOTALS` aggregation propagated its totals stream up. When the `merge()` side expands over many source tables — one or more of which contribute a totals-carrying sub-pipeline in some plan shape — the two totals ports collide at the outer step. The guard/assertion itself has been there since 2023; the defect is the plan shape producing two totals ports in the first place. ## Reproduction environment - Snapshot: `runs/merged24/crashes/inst-08-20260806-153204` (aarch64 ubsan). - Build: `26.8.1.1`, git hash `ee80b85a756f7edf7662b4d65eb8e597d9d46cf5` (fuzz-lab merged branch head — carries our AST-fuzzer-oracle PR #99980 on top of a recent `origin/master` merge; the code path that trips is unmodified on our branch, so this should reproduce on plain master). - `count__fuzz_137` schema (verbatim from the snapshot's metadata): ```sql CREATE TABLE count__fuzz_137 (x Nullable(String)) ENGINE = MergeTree PARTITION BY x PRIMARY KEY tuple() ORDER BY tuple() SETTINGS merge_with_ttl_timeout = 6320, index_granularity = 65535, /* + ~100 fuzzed settings */; ``` (The MergeTree table settings are fuzzed but not load-bearing — a plain `MergeTree ORDER BY tuple() PARTITION BY x` should suffice.) - `merge('default', '.+')` expands over **242 tables** in the fuzz-lab's `default` database (mixed engines: many `MergeTree`, some `Distributed`, some views). ## Reproduction status Deterministic under the fuzzer session that carries the multi-table `default` DB state. **Not yet reduced to a schema-free / small synthetic** — I tried: - Simple `... WITH TOTALS EXCEPT DISTINCT ... WITH TOTALS` over `numbers(1)` / single-`MergeTree` — does not trigger. - Same with `DISTINCT`, negative `LIMIT`, `HAVING`, nested `WITH TOTALS`, a view-with-totals inside `merge()`, `serialize_query_plan=1` — none trigger. - `merge()` over one table — does not trigger. The trigger appears to require the `merge('default', '.+')` source matching many fuzz-DB tables (one of which likely carries a totals-propagating sub-plan). A developer with the snapshot data can bisect by grepping the 242 default tables for ones that expose a `WITH TOTALS`-carrying view or distributed-shard totals path. ## Load-bearing conditions (unminimized) - Set operation (`EXCEPT DISTINCT`) between two `WITH TOTALS` aggregations. - `merge('default', '.+')` source on one side matching many tables. - The other side reads from a plain `MergeTree` table with `WITH TOTALS`. - `SELECT DISTINCT`, `IGNORE NULLS`, and `LIMIT -2147483649` (huge unsigned wrap) are all in the fuzzer-emitted query but haven't been individually confirmed as required. ## Suggested fix direction Two paths: 1. **Trace the totals-port propagation** — identify which sub-plan under `merge()` is contributing a totals port to the outer set-operation pipeline. If it's legitimate (e.g. a totals-view under `merge()`), the outer `TotalsHavingStep` should replace or merge rather than double-add. 2. **Downgrade the guard** — the `throw` at `addTotalsHavingTransform:159` catches a real invariant violation, but if the totals-port collision is only a plan-composition bug, the guard message could point at the planner defect rather than aborting. Snapshot preserved on the fuzz host if the multi-table state would help; happy to package the 242-table `default` metadata directory (small, ~few MB text) if requested.

signal.title: CI: run the full test suite only when review threads are resolved
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114724 This change limits the PR CI pipeline to builds and preliminary checks while review threads are unresolved, and records the gate in `Review Threads` and `Mergeable Check` statuses. The gate re-evaluates at workflow completion and after changes to the `ignore-unresolved-threads` label. GitHub Actions has no supported review-thread event, so thread changes after a completed workflow require a manual CI re-run; the documentation states that limitation. A failed pre-hook marker write leaves filtering disabled, so the full suite runs. The final review-thread marker preserves whether a limited pipeline needs replay even when another post-hook fails. signal.title: Coordinate a read with pinned block numbers in classic parallel replicas
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114263 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/97557 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix wrong results when a `SELECT` with `select_sequential_consistency = 1` on a `ReplicatedMergeTree` table runs with classic (task-based) parallel replicas. Every replica performed a complete local read clamped to the quorum boundary instead of a coordinator-assigned slice, so rows were returned once per participating replica. ### Description `StorageReplicatedMergeTree::read` routes a `select_sequential_consistency = 1` query into `readLocalSequentialConsistencyImpl`, which called `MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor::read` with `enable_parallel_reading` hardcoded to `false`. The setting is propagated to the followers, so each follower took that same branch: `read_task_callback` was never installed, the follower never announced its parts, and it read the whole pinned range locally. The initiator then merged N complete copies. On a 5-part `ReplicatedMergeTree` with a pinned boundary of 12000 rows and `max_parallel_replicas = 3`, `count()` returned 36000 and `sum()` was likewise tripled, with no exception and no warning. It scaled exactly linearly with `max_parallel_replicas`, and `uniqExact` stayed correct, confirming pure per-replica duplication. Reaching the defect requires turning off one of the optimizations that would otherwise bypass this read path: `optimize_trivial_count_query = 0` for `count()`, since at its default the planner serves the count from `totalRows()` and disables parallel replicas, or `parallel_replicas_local_plan = 0` or `parallel_replicas_prefer_local_replica = 0` for data reads. All three are documented, settable per query, and leave the wrong result silent. The fix passes `canUseParallelReplicasOnFollower()` at that call site, exactly as the sibling `readLocalImpl` already does for the non-pinned path, so the pinned read participates in coordination instead of being silently excluded from it. The boundary stays computed and applied: when it binds it comes from ZooKeeper and is identical on every replica (measured on two replicas holding different part sets, 7 and 6 active parts, both clamping to the same block), and with no quorum node it is the replica's own maximum, which excludes nothing it owns. Validation: new test `04912_pr_classic_pinned_block_numbers` fails on master and passes with the change, 50/50 green under randomized settings. Full matrix in the validation-gate comment below. Out of scope, neither introduced nor altered here: the plan-based path with `parallel_replicas_local_plan = 0` (#114263), and divergent part sets with no quorum node (#105710).

signal.title: Build profile diff: report why a gh api call failed
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115061 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `Build profile diff` failed on #115061 with a message naming only the `gh` argv ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115061&sha=9a8c54a155a55828cef1e38c76a31aca80038099&name_0=PR&name_1=Build%20profile%20diff), [job log](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/runs/32027518805/job/95431729878)): ``` CalledProcessError: Command '['gh', 'api', 'repos/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/commits?sha=a3f55f04… ``` Two things discarded the reason. `_list_commits_page` used `check=True`, and `CalledProcessError.__str__` renders only argv, so the captured `stderr`/`stdout` carrying the HTTP status were never read. The message then went through `md_code`, a table-cell *name* formatter (`MAX_NAME_LEN = 100`), which cut the tail. So 404, 403 and 5xx produced the same 102-character string, and the walk makes up to 60 calls without naming which one failed. Report it instead: exit code and endpoint first, then `stderr` and `stdout` each capped at 300 characters with an elision marker, in the field order `GH.get_output_with_retries` uses. `TimeoutExpired` is caught in the same place. `timeout=120` is kept deliberately - `gh` bounds connect and TLS handshake but not a stalled response body (measured 240 s unbounded), so the shared praktika helper, which passes no timeout, would unbound a bounded call site. `md_message` is added beside `md_code` for the comment path, bounded head+tail so the end of a message survives. `md_code` and `MAX_NAME_LEN` are untouched, so its 17 name callers are byte-identical. The bound matters beyond `gh`: a cluster query failure reaches the same handler carrying its whole inlined SQL, measured at 54952 characters against GitHub's 65536 limit. The `gh api` failure itself is environmental and out of scope: the byte-identical call succeeds 25 times out of 25 by hand. Validated with a throwaway harness, 30 assertions plus three mutation arms each reverting one hunk: 404, 403 and 5xx give three distinct messages where they gave one, and the success path, the `extend_master_shas` fail-close and the single-attempt contract are unchanged. `ci/tests/`: 711 passed, its 2 failures pre-existing on master. No committed test, per `.claude/CLAUDE.md`: `ci/tests/test_build_profile_diff_job.py` was removed in #114675. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115201&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115201](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115201+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: PK-range join sharding: pruned side yields 1 port, non-sharded fallback throws
signal.text: ### Describe what's wrong **`SELECT ... JOIN ...` with `query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges = 1` and `join_algorithm = 'full_sorting_merge'` fails with `Code: 49 ... Join is supported only for pipelines with one output port, got 3 and 1. (LOGICAL_ERROR)` whenever the primary key prunes one join side to zero parts. Pre-existing on master, not introduced by this PR - found while validating the PR's claim about the join-by-shards positional-port invariant.** - **Root cause:** The `use_sharding` fallback at [`src/Processors/QueryPlan/JoinStep.cpp:153`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/0fc2db3239a1b/src/Processors/QueryPlan/JoinStep.cpp#L153) does not do what its own comment promises ("fall back to the regular join pipeline which handles different stream counts"): the `YShaped` branch it falls back to requires exactly one port per side and neither pipeline is resized, unlike the `Paste` branch in `joinPipelinesYShaped` which calls `resize(1)` first. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `optimizeJoinByShards::apply` (Optimizations/optimizeJoinByShards.cpp:311) enables layer sharding on the join and attaches per-source layers to both reads. The pruned side never builds them: `ReadFromMergeTree::initializePipeline` returns a single `NullSource` port at ReadFromMergeTree.cpp:4758 when `result.parts_with_ranges` is empty, while the other side emits one port per layer. `JoinStep::updatePipeline` then sees mismatched stream counts, sets `use_sharding = false` (JoinStep.cpp:153) and calls `QueryPipelineBuilder::joinPipelinesYShaped`, which accepts only 1-vs-1 and throws at QueryPipelineBuilder.cpp:374. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Processors/QueryPlan/JoinStep.cpp:153`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/0fc2db3239a1b/src/Processors/QueryPlan/JoinStep.cpp#L153) — use_sharding falls back to the 1-port-only YShaped join without resizing - [`src/QueryPipeline/QueryPipelineBuilder.cpp:374`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/0fc2db3239a1b/src/QueryPipeline/QueryPipelineBuilder.cpp#L374) — throw site: 'Join is supported only for pipelines with one output port' - [`src/Processors/QueryPlan/ReadFromMergeTree.cpp:4758`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/0fc2db3239a1b/src/Processors/QueryPlan/ReadFromMergeTree.cpp#L4758) — pruned side emits one NullSource port instead of one port per sharded layer **Impact:** A valid query fails with a LOGICAL_ERROR (abort in debug/sanitizer builds). `query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges` is off by default but is randomized on in `tests/clickhouse-test` at 30%, so any existing test that full-sorting-merge-joins two MergeTree tables where one side is pruned by the primary key can redden CI. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `0fc2db3239a1b`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/9da94266-8d1a-41af-8898-3b6ac1451724) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- Test: JOIN sharded by primary-key ranges when one side is entirely pruned by the primary key. DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_04907_l; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_04907_r; CREATE TABLE t_04907_l (k UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k SETTINGS index_granularity = 128; CREATE TABLE t_04907_r (k UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k SETTINGS index_granularity = 128; INSERT INTO t_04907_l SELECT number FROM numbers(1000); INSERT INTO t_04907_r SELECT number FROM numbers(1000); -- The sharding applies only to reads in order, so pin `optimize_read_in_order` against the settings randomizer. SET query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges = 1, join_algorithm = 'full_sorting_merge', max_threads = 4, optimize_read_in_order = 1; SELECT count() FROM t_04907_l AS l JOIN (SELECT * FROM t_04907_r WHERE k > 100000) AS r ON l.k = r.k; SELECT count() FROM (SELECT * FROM t_04907_l WHERE k > 100000) AS l LEFT JOIN t_04907_r AS r ON l.k = r.k; DROP TABLE t_04907_l; DROP TABLE t_04907_r; ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` 0 0 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` Code: 49. DB::Exception: Received from localhost:19010. DB::Exception: Join is supported only for pipelines with one output port, got 3 and 1. (LOGICAL_ERROR) (query: SELECT count() FROM t_04907_l AS l JOIN (SELECT * FROM t_04907_r WHERE k > 100000) AS r ON l.k = r.k;) Having 1 errors! 0 tests passed. ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> In `JoinStep::updatePipeline`'s `!use_sharding` YShaped branch, resize both pipelines to a single stream before calling `joinPipelinesYShaped` (mirroring the `Paste` handling at QueryPipelineBuilder.cpp:368-372), or keep the sharded path by making the pruned side emit one empty port per layer. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - The same divergence arises from the other early return that collapses a sharded side to one port - `ReadFromMergeTree::readByLayers` returns an empty pipe when `0 == info.sum_marks` (ReadFromMergeTree.cpp:1155), which `initializePipeline` also replaces with a single `NullSource`. Same root cause, same fix. Found during automated review of [PR #114177](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114177). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr114177_001` </details> cc @alexey-milovidov (from #114177)

signal.title: Documentation claims default unexpected_quoting_character_strategy is INVALID but code defaults to PROMOTE
signal.text: _Found via ClickGap automated review. Please close or comment if this is incorrect or needs adjustment._ _Retrospective finding from a historical scan of [PR #80657](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/80657) (merged 2025-06-17). Confirmed on current codebase — close with a note if already fixed._ ### Describe what's wrong Users reading the function documentation see 'The default value is INVALID' but the actual default behavior is PROMOTE, leading to different query results when the 5th argument is omitted **Root cause:** extractKeyValuePairs.cpp:187: documentation string says 'The default value is `INVALID`' but KeyValuePairExtractorBuilder.h:55 initializes to PROMOTE **Why we believe this is a bug:** extractKeyValuePairs.cpp:187 (function registration docs) → states 'The default value is `INVALID`'. KeyValuePairExtractorBuilder.h:55 → defaults to PROMOTE. When no 5th argument is passed, ArgumentExtractor returns nullptr, the if-block in getBuilder is skipped, and the builder's PROMOTE default takes effect. **Affected locations:** - `src/Functions/extractKeyValuePairs.cpp:187` — Function registration documentation claims default is INVALID - `src/Functions/keyvaluepair/impl/KeyValuePairExtractorBuilder.h:55` — Actual default is PROMOTE **Impact:** Users who omit the 5th argument expect INVALID behavior (based on docs) but get PROMOTE behavior, which produces different results for inputs containing quoting characters in unexpected positions ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Instead default_equals_promote=1 and default_equals_invalid=0, proving default is PROMOTE. ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` {'abc':'5'} {'abc':'5'} 1 0 {} {} {'abc':'5'} ``` ### Additional context **Open risks:** - The same incorrect documentation exists in docs/en/sql-reference/functions/tuple-map-functions.md **Suggested fix:** Change the documentation string to say 'The default value is `PROMOTE`' or change the code default to INVALID to match the documentation **Analysis details:** Confidence HIGH | Severity P2 | Testability: `STATELESS_SQL` Found during automated review of [PR #80657](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/80657). --- _ClickGapAI · Confidence: HIGH · Severity: P2 · Finding: `h_pr80657_001`_

signal.title: azureBlobStorage INSERT surfaces connection failure as raw Azure::Storage::StorageException (code 1001, STD_EXCEPTION) — s3 throws catchable S3_ERROR on the same shape
signal.text: **Describe what's wrong** When an `azureBlobStorage` INSERT cannot reach the storage endpoint (connection refused), the query fails with `Code: 1001` (`STD_EXCEPTION`) — the Azure SDK's `Azure::Storage::StorageException` propagates to the client untranslated instead of being classified as a storage/network error. ``` Code: 1001. DB::Exception: Azure::Storage::StorageException: 500 Poco::Exception. Code: 1000, e.code() = 111, Connection refused,. (STD_EXCEPTION) ``` The `s3` table function translates the identical failure shape properly — connection refused surfaces as a catchable `S3_ERROR`: ``` Code: 499. DB::Exception: Failed to check existence of key p.parquet in bucket bucket: Poco::Exception. Code: 1000, e.code() = 111, Connection refused (version 26.8.1.1554 (official build)). HTTP response code: 18446744073709551615, error type: NETWORK_CONNECTION. (S3_ERROR) ``` The azure READ path also classifies it (the schema-inference wrapper returns `CANNOT_EXTRACT_TABLE_STRUCTURE`, code 636) — only the write path lets the raw SDK exception through. Code 1001 is the raw-`std::exception` class, so clients and error monitoring cannot distinguish an unreachable endpoint from an internal error, and `system.errors` attributes it to `STD_EXCEPTION`. **Does it reproduce on the most recent release?** Reproduced on master 26.8.1.1554 (official build). Deterministic: 20/20 runs. **How to reproduce** No storage account or emulator is needed — any connection-refused endpoint shows it (port 1 below): ```bash clickhouse local --query " INSERT INTO FUNCTION azureBlobStorage( 'DefaultEndpointsProtocol=http;AccountName=devstoreaccount1;AccountKey=Eby8vdM02xNOcqFlqUwJPLlmEtlCDXJ1OUzFT50uSRZ6IFsuFq2UVErCz4I6tq/K1SZFPTOtr/KBHBeksoGMGw==;BlobEndpoint=http://127.0.0.1:1/devstoreaccount1;', 'cont', 'p.parquet', 'Parquet', 'k Int64') SELECT 1" ``` (The account key is Azurite's public well-known development key; it is not a secret.) **Expected behavior** A catchable storage/network error (the `s3` write path's `S3_ERROR` treatment of the same failure — or `AZURE_BLOB_STORAGE_ERROR`), not the `STD_EXCEPTION` class. **Additional context** Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115127 — the same untranslated-Azure-SDK-exception theme on the credential-mint path (`Azure::Core::Credentials::AuthenticationException`); this report is the storage-operation flavor, which fails on a different call site. Found by an automatic optimizer-testing framework (differential testing of optimizer settings, query plans, and equivalent rewrites).

signal.title: BACKUP to S3 Express fails with InvalidPart: CompleteMultipartUpload omits the per-part checksums that checksummed multipart uploads require
signal.text: ### Describe what's wrong `BACKUP ... TO S3(...)` with an S3 Express One Zone destination fails for every backup that contains a file larger than `s3_max_single_part_upload_size` (default 32 MiB) — the multipart upload of that file can never be completed. Mechanism: express mode is activated by `isS3ExpressEndpoint` (a substring match on the endpoint, `src/IO/S3/Client.cpp`), and it makes every upload request checksummed: `CreateMultipartUpload` is sent with `x-amz-checksum-algorithm: CRC32` and every `UploadPart` carries `x-amz-checksum-crc32` (`RequestChecksumRequired` in `src/IO/S3/Requests.h`). The S3 API requires that completing a multipart upload created with a checksum algorithm include each part's checksum in the `CompleteMultipartUpload` request. The INSERT write path handles this: `WriteBufferFromS3` computes each part's checksum and attaches it to the completed parts (`multipart_checksums` in `src/IO/WriteBufferFromS3.cpp`). But `copyS3File` / `copyDataToS3File` — the path backups use (`src/Backups/BackupIO_S3.cpp`) — builds the completed parts from `ETag` and `PartNumber` only (`multipart_upload.AddParts(part.WithETag(multipart_tags[i]).WithPartNumber(...))` in `src/IO/S3/copyS3File.cpp`), so the completion is rejected. The native server-side copy path (`UploadPartCopy`) in the same file has the same gap. Two side effects worth noting: an S3 disk on an Express bucket works (writes go through `WriteBufferFromS3`), while `BACKUP` of the same server to the same bucket cannot complete; and `isTransientCompleteMultipartUploadError` classifies the rejection as transient, so the doomed `CompleteMultipartUpload` is pointlessly retried several times before the backup fails. ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes — current master: `src/IO/S3/copyS3File.cpp` has no per-part checksum handling. Reproduced on a recent 26.8 development build. ### How to reproduce Express request shaping is activated purely by the endpoint substring, and MinIO enforces the same checksummed-multipart completion contract as AWS, so this reproduces without a real Express bucket: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (id UInt64, filler String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; INSERT INTO t SELECT number, toString(sipHash64(number)) FROM numbers(800000); -- endpoint containing "s3express" -> express request shaping; the lowered -- thresholds only shrink the data needed to trigger a multipart upload SET s3_max_single_part_upload_size = 4194304, s3_min_upload_part_size = 5242880; BACKUP TABLE t TO S3('http://s3express.localhost:9000/clickfawkes/bk', '<key>', '<secret>'); ``` with `s3express.localhost` pointing at a plain MinIO (`*.localhost` resolves to loopback on systemd machines). The backup fails with `InvalidPart` on every run; the byte-identical backup through the same MinIO under a non-express hostname succeeds and round-trips via `RESTORE`. A wire capture of the failing run shows: `CreateMultipartUpload` carries `x-amz-checksum-algorithm: CRC32`, every `UploadPart` carries `x-amz-checksum-crc32`, and the `CompleteMultipartUpload` body contains only `ETag`/`PartNumber` elements per part: ```xml <CompleteMultipartUpload xmlns="http://s3.amazonaws.com/doc/2006-03-01/"> <Part> <ETag>"63cc2deb63afc264fbe535396204dede"</ETag> <PartNumber>1</PartNumber> </Part> ... </CompleteMultipartUpload> ``` I have not run this against a real S3 Express One Zone bucket; there the same completion is rejected by the same documented API rule (a multipart upload created with a checksum algorithm must be completed with each part's checksum), and the default 32 MiB threshold means any real backup hits it. ### Expected behavior The backup completes. `CompleteMultipartUpload` includes each part's `ChecksumCRC32` whenever the upload was created with a checksum algorithm. ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` <Error> copyDataToS3File: While performing multipart upload of object bk_express/data/default/t/all_1_1_0/data.bin in bucket clickfawkes: Code: 499. DB::Exception: Message: Unable to parse ExceptionName: InvalidPart Message: One or more of the specified parts could not be found. The part may not have been uploaded, or the specified entity tag may not match the part's entity tag., Key: bk_express/data/default/t/all_1_1_0/data.bin, Bucket: clickfawkes, Tags: "410d419fd94fdfa2e222d6437eae7023" "5ea9a0982b745fdba59f4214468efeb8" ... (S3_ERROR) ``` ### Additional context The open PR #107318 (`s3_upload_checksum_algorithm` setting) generalizes the express-only checksum code and adds exactly the missing per-part checksum bookkeeping to `copyS3File`, so it appears to fix this as a side effect — but there seems to be no issue tracking the S3 Express backup breakage itself, and that PR is motivated by a different case (FIPS/Object Lock).

signal.title: Azure managed-identity token failure surfaces as STD_EXCEPTION (code 1001) instead of a catchable authentication error
signal.text: **Describe what's wrong** When Azure Blob Storage authentication goes through `ManagedIdentityCredential` (the default `getAuthMethod` fallback when a disk carries no `account_key` / `connection_string` / `use_workload_identity`) and the identity endpoint rejects the token request, the query fails with `Code: 1001` (`STD_EXCEPTION`) — the Azure SDK's `Azure::Core::Credentials::AuthenticationException` propagates to the client untranslated instead of being classified as an authentication error. ``` Code: 1001. DB::Exception: Azure::Core::Credentials::AuthenticationException: GetToken(): error response: 401 Unauthorized {}. (STD_EXCEPTION) ``` The equivalent GCS flow translates the same failure shape properly: `PocoHTTPClientGCPOAuth::requestBearerToken` throws `AUTHENTICATION_FAILED` (code 516) on a non-OK token response. The Azure identity path should do the same — code 1001 is the raw-`std::exception` class, so clients and error monitoring cannot distinguish a misconfigured/denied managed identity from an internal error, and `system.errors` attributes it to `STD_EXCEPTION`. **Does it reproduce on the most recent release?** Reproduced on master 26.8.1.1554 (official build). Deterministic: 20/20 runs. **How to reproduce** Run a token endpoint that rejects requests (the App Service managed-identity protocol, stdlib only): ```python # mi_reject.py from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler): def log_message(self, *_): pass def do_GET(self): self.send_response(401) self.send_header("Content-Length", "2") self.send_header("Connection", "close") self.end_headers() self.wfile.write(b"{}") HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 9399), H).serve_forever() ``` Then point the managed-identity App Service env at it and create a table on a credential-less dynamic Azure disk (no real storage account is needed — the failure happens at token mint, before any storage request): ```bash python3 mi_reject.py & IDENTITY_ENDPOINT="http://127.0.0.1:9399/mi" IDENTITY_HEADER="x" \ clickhouse local --query " CREATE TABLE t (k Int64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k SETTINGS disk = disk(type = 'azure_blob_storage', endpoint = 'https://127.0.0.1:1/acct/cont/pfx/', skip_access_check = 0)" ``` **Expected behavior** A catchable authentication error (e.g. `AUTHENTICATION_FAILED`, code 516, like the GCS OAuth flow), not the `STD_EXCEPTION` class. **Additional context** The same untranslated-`AuthenticationException` propagation likely affects the other Azure identity flows (`WorkloadIdentityCredential`, service principal), since none of the call sites wrap `GetToken` failures. Found by an automatic optimizer-testing framework (differential testing of optimizer settings, query plans, and equivalent rewrites).

signal.title: Empty `symbols` and `lines` in `system.trace_log` in the `amd_cfi` build profile
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115036 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/100419 ### Describe what's wrong In the `amd_cfi` build (ThinLTO + CFI + `SPLIT_DEBUG_SYMBOLS` + `BUILD_STRIPPED_BINARY` — ClickHouse's only CI test build with ThinLTO), query profiler symbolization is completely broken: every row of `system.trace_log` has all-empty `symbols` and all-empty `lines`, while `build_id` still resolves. Both symbolization tests fail deterministically (49/49 and 52/52 reruns, with and without randomized settings): * `03150_trace_log_add_build_id` — `countIf(arrayExists(x -> x != '', symbols)) > 1` returns `0` (symbol names come from the binary's own symbol table) * `03150_trace_log_source_lines` — the equivalent check on `lines` returns `0` (source lines come from DWARF) The tests pass in every regular (non-ThinLTO) CI build. This is a longstanding property of the `amd_cfi` profile, not a recent regression: the tests have failed under it since at least 2026-07-13 (validation runs of #100419, including after `-DSPLIT_DEBUG_SYMBOLS=ON` was added there) and have never passed under it. Which ingredient is responsible (ThinLTO, the CFI flags, or the stripped/split-debug packaging) is not yet isolated; the commit message of `ed28e41bf7` in #100419 claims `amd_release` (ThinLTO without CFI) passes the test, which would point at the CFI flags, but that claim is unverified in CI. If ThinLTO alone turns out to be sufficient, official release builds would be affected too, and no CI job other than `WeeklyCFI` would see it. ### How to reproduce * Commit: 6d53f1de970dcf1f88b4e208cdd03091cd098272 (PR head merge of #115036, version 26.8.1.1) * Build: `amd_cfi` (`-DENABLE_THINLTO=1 -DENABLE_CFI=1 -DSPLIT_DEBUG_SYMBOLS=ON -DBUILD_STRIPPED_BINARY=1`, RelWithDebInfo) * Run `03150_trace_log_add_build_id` or `03150_trace_log_source_lines` CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115036&sha=30c47a7d9420ba1e86365979016e7765cbc080da&name_0=WeeklyCFI&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_cfi%2C%20parallel%29 No fiddle link: reproducing needs a ThinLTO+CFI build, which fiddle does not provide.

signal.title: Server crash (SIGSEGV) in gRPC response compression (`zlib_compress` / `deflateEnd`)
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115036 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108074 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114054 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114045 ### Describe what's wrong The server received `SIGSEGV` inside gRPC's response compression path while executing `SELECT 0 FROM numbers(1000000)` over gRPC with `transport_compression`, in the `amd_cfi` build of the `WeeklyCFI` workflow (PR validation run of #115036). This is a plain segmentation fault (`Address: 0x50. Access: read. Address not mapped to object.`), not a CFI trap (CFI violations trap with `SIGILL`): ``` 2. free_default 3. deflateEnd 4. zlib_compress(grpc_slice_buffer*, grpc_slice_buffer*, int) (.llvm.6130045630295956944) 5. grpc_msg_compress(grpc_compression_algorithm, grpc_slice_buffer*, grpc_slice_buffer*) 6. grpc_core::ChannelCompression::CompressMessage(...) ... 13. grpc_call_start_batch 14. grpc::internal::CallOpSet<...>::ContinueFillOpsAfterInterception() 15. DB::(anonymous namespace)::Responder<(DB::(anonymous namespace)::CallType)0>::writeAndFinish(...) 16. DB::(anonymous namespace)::Call::sendResult() 17. DB::(anonymous namespace)::Call::run() ``` The crash made `test_grpc_protocol/test.py::test_transport_compression` fail and cascaded into `test_opentelemetry_context_propagation` and `test_restart` (dead server). All three passed on retry, so the crash is probabilistic, and this stack has exactly one confirmed occurrence so far — whether the build profile (`amd_cfi` is the only integration-test build with ThinLTO) matters is unknown. `test_transport_compression` has failed occasionally in other builds (`amd_asan`, `amd_msan`, `amd_tsan`, `amd_binary`, `amd_llvm_coverage`) in other PRs, but with different signatures (server unreachable at test start, cluster startup/teardown problems), so those are not confirmed instances of this crash. Possibly relevant: the deflate subsystem is under active churn — #108074 (use libdeflate for gzip/zlib/deflate, merged 2026-07-14) is being reverted in #114054 (closes #114045), that revert touches `tests/integration/test_grpc_protocol/test.py` and `src/Server/grpc_protos/clickhouse_grpc.proto`, and on 2026-08-16 — the same day as this crash — `test_transport_compression` also failed in #114054's Bugfix validation on both architectures. #108074 predates four green `WeeklyCFI` runs that exercised this test, so it is not a clean attribution either. ### How to reproduce * Commit: 6d53f1de970dcf1f88b4e208cdd03091cd098272 (PR head merge of #115036, version 26.8.1.1) * Build: `amd_cfi` (`-DENABLE_THINLTO=1 -DENABLE_CFI=1 -DSPLIT_DEBUG_SYMBOLS=ON -DBUILD_STRIPPED_BINARY=1`, RelWithDebInfo) * Test: `tests/integration/test_grpc_protocol/test.py::test_transport_compression` (probabilistic; one occurrence in one run so far) CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115036&sha=30c47a7d9420ba1e86365979016e7765cbc080da&name_0=WeeklyCFI&name_1=Integration%20tests%20%28amd_cfi%2C%202%2F4%29 No fiddle link: the crash needs a gRPC client with transport compression against the server, which fiddle cannot exercise.

signal.title: Paimon: pypaimon-written TIMESTAMP-partitioned tables are unreadable (partition directory spelling mismatch, raw STD_EXCEPTION)
signal.text: **Describe what's wrong** A Paimon table with a `TIMESTAMP` partition key written by pypaimon (the Python implementation of Paimon, version 2.0.0) is unreadable by ClickHouse: every read fails with `Code: 1001. DB::Exception: std::__1::filesystem::filesystem_error ... No such file or directory`, because ClickHouse and pypaimon spell the partition directory name differently. pypaimon writes the partition directory as `t=2026-01-01 12:00:00.123000` (literal space between date and time, unescaped colons, microsecond digits regardless of the declared precision). ClickHouse, following the Java Paimon spelling (the same one used by the `paimon_timestamp_partition` fixtures added in #113401, e.g. `ts=1960-03-04T05%3A06%3A07.000000891`), reconstructs the path as `t=2026-01-01T12%3A00%3A00.123` (`T` separator, `%3A`-escaped colons, precision-scaled fraction digits) and looks for a directory that does not exist. Two aspects seem worth fixing or deciding on the ClickHouse side, even though the spelling divergence itself arguably originates in pypaimon: 1. Whether the reader should tolerate the alternative spelling (pypaimon-written timestamp-partitioned tables are presumably readable by pypaimon itself — it reads its own table back fine — so the two implementations disagree about the on-disk contract, and tables written by the Python toolchain are silently incompatible with ClickHouse). 2. The failure surfaces as `STD_EXCEPTION` (code 1001) leaking a raw `std::filesystem` error, rather than a catchable, actionable message naming the table/partition mismatch. **Does it reproduce on the most recent release?** Reproduces on master, version 26.8.1.1516. **How to reproduce** Write a timestamp-partitioned table with pypaimon (`pip install pypaimon pyarrow`): ```python import datetime as dt import pyarrow as pa from pypaimon import CatalogFactory, Schema cat = CatalogFactory.create({"warehouse": "/tmp/paimon_ts_wh"}) cat.create_database("db", False) schema = pa.schema([("t", pa.timestamp("ms")), ("k", pa.int64()), ("v", pa.int64())]) cat.create_table("db.ts", Schema.from_pyarrow_schema(schema, partition_keys=["t"]), False) tbl = cat.get_table("db.ts") wb = tbl.new_batch_write_builder() w, c = wb.new_write(), wb.new_commit() w.write_arrow(pa.table({ "t": pa.array([dt.datetime(2026, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0, 123000), dt.datetime(2026, 1, 2, 13, 30, 0, 456000)], pa.timestamp("ms")), "k": pa.array([1, 2], pa.int64()), "v": pa.array([10, 20], pa.int64())})) c.commit(w.prepare_commit()) ``` The directory pypaimon creates is: ``` $ ls /tmp/paimon_ts_wh/db.db/ts/ manifest schema snapshot 't=2026-01-01 12:00:00.123000' 't=2026-01-02 13:30:00.456000' ``` Read it with ClickHouse: ``` $ clickhouse local -q "SELECT * FROM paimonLocal('/tmp/paimon_ts_wh/db.db/ts') ORDER BY k" Code: 1001. DB::Exception: std::__1::filesystem::filesystem_error: filesystem error: Got unexpected error while getting file metadata: No such file or directory ["/tmp/paimon_ts_wh/db.db/ts/t=2026-01-01T12%3A00%3A00.123/bucket-0/data-....parquet"]. (STD_EXCEPTION) ``` The path in the error shows the spelling ClickHouse reconstructed from the manifest `BinaryRow` partition value; the directory on disk uses pypaimon's spelling. **Expected behavior** Either the table reads back its two rows (if the pypaimon spelling is considered acceptable input), or a catchable error explains that the partition directory referenced by the manifest was not found — not a raw `std::filesystem` exception. **Additional context** pypaimon reads its own table back correctly, so the data itself is intact; only the partition-path reconstruction disagrees. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113401 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115042 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113337 Found by an automatic optimizer-testing framework (differential testing of optimizer settings, query plans, and equivalent rewrites).

signal.title: Stress tests fail to restart the server after `04323_text_index_marks_empty_part`: startup rejects a corrupted marks file that `ATTACH TABLE` tolerates
signal.text: Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114091 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115036 ### Describe what's wrong Stress test jobs fail with `Cannot start clickhouse-server` when the run kills the server while `04323_text_index_marks_empty_part` is in its corruption window. The test deliberately appends one byte to `skp_idx_idx.mrk4` (24 → 25 bytes) and removes `checksums.txt` of the empty part, then re-attaches, queries and drops the table. If the server is killed between the corruption and the final `DROP`, the corrupted table stays on disk and the post-stress restart fails: ``` DB::Exception: Load job 'load table test_3.t_text_idx_empty' failed: Code: 246. DB::Exception: Bad size of marks file '/var/lib/clickhouse/store/.../all_1_10_4/skp_idx_idx.mrk4': 25, must be: 24: Cannot attach table `test_3`.`t_text_idx_empty` ... (CORRUPTED_DATA) ``` Four occurrences since 2026-08-14, all the same signature: PRs #113347, #100391, #76184 (`Stress test (amd_tsan)`/`(arm_tsan)`) and #115036 (`Stress test (arm_release)`, [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115036&sha=9156269951fd4455486a9ea61e5e9ac1e12e2ba1&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_release%29)). The window was widened by #114091 (merged 2026-08-10), which pinned the empty part with `remove_empty_parts = 0` — before that, the cleanup thread usually removed the corrupted empty part before a restart could trip over it, which is consistent with the failures starting on 2026-08-14. Two ways to read it: 1. Server inconsistency: the running server *tolerates* this state — the test itself does `ATTACH TABLE`, `SYSTEM PREWARM MARK CACHE` and `SELECT` on the corrupted part successfully — but the startup metadata load rejects the very same on-disk state and fails the whole table load. Startup being stricter than `ATTACH` means any kill inside the window bricks the table until manual intervention. 2. Test hygiene: a `no-stress` tag is not supported by design ("stress tests must be able to run every test"), so the test must be kill-safe, and with `remove_empty_parts = 0` it is not — there is no point in its corruption window where a kill leaves a startup-loadable state. ### How to reproduce * Run `04323_text_index_marks_empty_part`, kill the server after the `printf '\x00' >> .../skp_idx_idx.mrk4` / `rm checksums.txt` step (before the final `DROP TABLE`), and start the server again — table load fails with `CORRUPTED_DATA` while the same state was attachable before the kill. * In CI: any stress job that kills the server inside that window. No fiddle link: requires killing and restarting the server around on-disk state, which fiddle cannot do.
signal.author: zlareb1

signal.title: Fix AI functions embedding counters behavior on error
signal.text: `aiEmbed` and `aiSimilarity` under-report provider usage in `system.query_log` when a request fails: with the default `ai_function_throw_on_error = 1` the exception row shows `AIAPICalls = 0` and `AIInputTokens = 0`, although the provider was called and billed. Flipping only that setting records the call: | `ai_function_throw_on_error` | `AIAPICalls` | `AIRowsSkipped` | |---|---:|---:| | `1` (default) | 0 | 0 | | `0` | 1 | 1 | Same query and endpoint, with `ai_function_max_retries = 0` so exactly one attempt is made. **Cause.** `embedTexts` accumulates the counters in a local `EmbeddingResult` and returns it by value. When a failed request rethrows, `return` is never reached: the local is destroyed while unwinding and the caller's `embedding_result` is never constructed, so the caller's `ProfileEvents::increment` calls are both skipped and left with nothing to read. That defeats the intent stated at the accumulation site, which counts `api_calls` *before* issuing the request so that failed calls are still counted. **Fix.** `embedTexts` now reports `AIAPICalls` and `AIInputTokens` itself, from a `SCOPE_EXIT` guard, so the normal and throwing exits both publish them. They are plain locals rather than fields of `EmbeddingResult`, so no caller can count them twice. Callers keep their own row counters, which mean different things: texts for `aiEmbed`, pairs of texts for `aiSimilarity`. **Not covered.** Row counters are still dropped when the query throws. It delivered no rows, and preserving them would need `embedTexts` to take an out-parameter in both callers. **Tests.** Three integration tests, each verified to fail with the source reverted to `master`: one per caller for `AIAPICalls`, plus one driving the quota-exceeded throw so a batch succeeds first and `AIInputTokens` is non-zero. The failed-request tests cannot cover `AIInputTokens`, since there the first request fails and no tokens are consumed. The same defect on the text-generation path is fixed in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111830, which is what introduced a throwing path there. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111830 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `aiEmbed` and `aiSimilarity` reporting zero `AIAPICalls` and `AIInputTokens` in `system.query_log` when a provider request failed, despite the request having been made and billed.

signal.title: Add `max_tables` database setting for `Atomic` and `Ordinary`
signal.text: Limit how many tables a database may hold. `0` (default) means unlimited. `CREATE TABLE` and `ATTACH TABLE` throw `TOO_MANY_TABLES` once the limit is reached. `ALTER DATABASE ... MODIFY SETTING max_tables = ...` changes it. The limit is enforced by the on-disk engines that keep their tables in memory (`Atomic`, `Ordinary`) and is not supported by `Replicated`. See #109355 <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a max_tables setting for the Atomic and Ordinary database engines that limits how many tables a database may contain (0, the default, means unlimited). signal.title: Use higher quality hash for nullable fixed-width keys in external aggregation
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): 64-bit hash function is used now for external nullable fixed-width aggregation methods (avoids collision disaster for very high cardinality aggregation). --- External aggregation merges partitions whose combined key count can far exceed 4 billion, which is why `mergeBlocks` re-aggregates the spilled stream with a method hashing over more than 32 bits rather than `HashCRC32`. `key64`, `keys128`, `keys256` and the serialized methods all have such a counterpart and are remapped to it; the nullable fixed-width methods never got one, so a `GROUP BY` on a nullable key that spills is still re-aggregated with a 32-bit hash and takes the collision blowup the remap exists to avoid. Add `nullable_key64_hash64`, `nullable_keys128_hash64` and `nullable_keys256_hash64`, and remap to them. The packed forms need no new data type: a nullable packed key carries its null map inside the key, so they reuse `AggregatedDataWithKeys128Hash64` / `…256Hash64` with `has_nullable_keys`. Only the single nullable key needs one, mirroring how `nullable_key64` wraps the `HashCRC32` map in `AggregationDataWithNullKey`. `nullable_key32` is deliberately left out, matching the existing choice not to remap `key32`: a 32-bit key space cannot exceed 4 billion distinct values.
